fix(update): keep the old process's lazy imports working across a git rebuild (#174867)

Git-checkout updates could fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and roll back: the updater kept running from <checkout>/dist while git-update rebuilt dist in place, and later lazy imports in the old process (e.g. dist/port-provider importing targets, agent-db registry listing and config chunks) resolved hashed chunk names the new build had replaced. Live: an isolated git-checkout update loaded five chunks already absent from the replacement build and finished with a healthy target Gateway and a clean CLI exit. fix(gateway): main thread blocks after sign-in, sign-out or plugin settings changes (#173626)

Related: #173585, #169562

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway main thread blocks for hundreds of milliseconds after a sign-in, sign-out, key removal or plugin settings change, because runtime readers reload plugin metadata from disk although no plugin was installed.

## User Impact

User impact: less main-thread blocking after account and plugin settings changes, so model pickers and other Gateway requests stall less. No config, state or plugin contract changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Config hot reload holds the plugin lifecycle lease (since #145484). The lease runs in a fresh operation plugin cache, so management sees what other processes committed while it waited. That isolation stays. But two kinds of work inside it reloaded plugin metadata on every event:

1. **A policy change rescanned the whole inventory.** Plugin activation (`enabled`) is the only config-owned fact in the installed plugin index. A changed policy hash (for example auto-enable after a sign-in) made the registry reader treat the persisted index as stale and run full discovery. Activation is now one projection over inventory records (`projectInstalledPluginIndexPolicy`), used by fresh builds and by the registry reader. When the persisted inventory passes its existing freshness checks and only the policy differs, the reader projects the new policy in memory. Install, uninstall, stale files, load paths and the other existing reasons still rediscover. Freshness checks tolerate missing files only for disabled records, so records the new policy enables are rechecked; if any is stale, the reader rediscovers. This matches the documented rule that enablement is evaluated from the current operation's policy, not stored with the facts.
2. **Post-commit Gateway readers could not see the published inventory.** The model-policy comparison (chat metadata lifecycle) and the prepared model runtime refresh inherit the lease's operation cache, so model-id normalization in `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` loaded a metadata snapshot from disk. As in #169562, the Gateway lifecycle owner now passes the snapshot it published. The chat metadata lifecycle hands `getPluginMetadataSnapshot()` to `modelSelectionPoliciesMatch`. The prepared runtime refresh forwards its existing `pluginMetadataSnapshot` option to the configured owner inputs. Readers without an explicit snapshot keep their current behavior.

## Evidence

- Regression tests, each fails on `main` and passes here:
  - `plugin-registry.test.ts`, "projects a config policy change over the persisted inventory without rescanning": on `main` the extensions dir is rescanned.
  - `plugin-registry.test.ts`, "rediscovers when a policy enables a persisted plugin whose files are gone": a projection-only reader would return an enabled plugin with no files.
  - `operator-model-presentation.test.ts`, two tests run inside an operation cache like the reload lease: the policy comparison and prepared runtime input collection load no plugin metadata. On `main` they load 2 and 1 snapshots.
- Focused suites pass: plugin registry, index and cache; capability generation; model selection; operator model policy; chat metadata lifecycle; prepared model runtime; agent database startup. Two kinds of local failure, neither CI-relevant:
  - 4 tests in `plugin-registry` and `installed-plugin-index` fail on macOS on both `main` and this branch (temp-dir environment).
  - One agent-database-startup test timed out at host load ~60 and passes alone.
- Isolated Gateway on a packaged layout (built dist, no `.git`, `src` or `extensions`), compared with the `main` it merges. CPU profile over 20 events (4 each of sign-in, sign-out, key removal, plugin reload and plugin settings change), two interleaved rounds:

| Main-thread CPU | main (round 1 / 2) | this PR (round 1 / 2) |
|---|---|---|
| model-id normalization metadata loads | 22555 / 20521 ms | 2 / 0 ms |
| plugin inventory rediscovery | 16873 / 16489 ms | 3638 / 1518 ms |
| all plugin metadata snapshot loads | 31650 / 29862 ms | 10194 / 8281 ms |
| busy segments ≥ 150 ms | 57 / 67 | 31 / 14 |

  What remains is `resolveConfigWidePluginMetadataSnapshot`: the explicit plugin reload, which is the owner's refresh path, plus startup config preflight.

- `last-heartbeat` lag probe during the event, n = 12 events each, runs interleaved base/PR. Host load was 30–101, so absolute values are inflated:

| Event (during) | main p50 / p99 | this PR p50 / p99 |
|---|---|---|
| sign-in | 1.8 / 698 ms | 2.6 / 329 ms |
| sign-out | 3.2 / 790 ms | 4.2 / 489 ms |
| key removal | 4.1 / 1009 ms | 2.0 / 359 ms |
| plugin reload | 1.4 / 710 ms | 1.0 / 489 ms |
| plugin settings change | 0.8 / 157 ms | 0.8 / 138 ms |

  No run showed a removed provider after its removal (0 violations).

Not covered: plugin reload still blocks, from the reload's own metadata refresh, plugin module re-import and runtime publication. That needs a separate change.

## Notes

A source checkout (`pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `src` and `extensions` at the package root) cannot measure this. There, `isBundledPluginInsideDevSourceRoot` and the private QA plugins make `requiresDerivedRegistryValidation` reject the persisted index on every read, so local dev Gateways still rescan. Packaged installs do not.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: a revert restores the reloads. Nothing is persisted or migrated, and lease isolation is unchanged. Blast radius if wrong:
- Plugin activation as seen by Gateway runtime reads after a config change. The projection uses the same rule and inputs as a fresh index build.
- Model-id normalization in the post-commit policy comparison and prepared runtime refresh. These use the inventory the Gateway published, which is what other runtime readers already use.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix: web search sign-in error tells the model what to say to the user (#174844)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a search provider's sign-in has expired (for example Grok through xAI OAuth), the `web_search` error from #174651 tells the model to "tell the user web search is unavailable", so the bot announces the outage even when it could answer another way.

## User Impact

The error now states facts only: the provider's sign-in expired or could not be refreshed; the Gateway owner fixes it with `/login <provider>` in a private chat or Control UI session, or with `openclaw models auth login --provider <provider>`; and other routes such as `web_fetch` may still work. The model decides whether to mention the outage, for example only when it cannot answer another way.

## Why This Change Was Made

Tool results should report facts, not script the reply. The sign-in classification, login commands and privacy (no profile id, account or upstream text) are unchanged. The timeout message ("Try again later or choose another provider.") is operator guidance with no instruction to the model, so it stays as is.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway from this branch with `tools.web.search.provider = "grok"` and an `xai` OAuth profile whose refresh token is invalid; the live xAI token endpoint returned `invalid_grant`. `gateway call tools.invoke` with `web_search` returned:

`provider_error: Search failed: this search provider's xai sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. The Gateway owner can fix it by sending `/login xai` in a private chat or Control UI session, or by running `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`. Other routes, such as web_fetch, may still work.`

The output contains no "tell the user" instruction, profile id, token or upstream refresh error. Focused tests: `web-search.provider-errors` (now also asserts the instruction is absent) and `web-search.signal`.

Merge danger: two-way door. Text-only change to one tool error message; no config, schema, protocol or stored-state change. Blast radius is the `web_search` error text for providers that sign in through an OAuth profile.

fix(media): large Gemini images fail through OpenRouter chat endpoints (#174839)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a paid Gemini 4K image is discarded with `openrouter.image-generation: JSON response exceeds 45787819 bytes` when OpenRouter is configured with a non-canonical base URL (proxies, gateways, or any URL other than `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`), because those requests use the chat endpoint.

## User Impact

User impact: Gemini 4K generations through OpenRouter's chat endpoint are saved (fitted to the media cap) instead of failing. The generated-image download ceiling now covers the largest real model output.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two bounds were too small for real responses, measured on 2026-10-17:

- **OpenRouter chat responses carry an encrypted reasoning blob next to each image.** `choices[0].message.reasoning_details[0].data` measured 0.47–0.70× the image's base64 size, so the JSON is 1.47–1.70× the image payload. The bound counted only the image. The chat path now budgets two encoded payloads per image. The dedicated `/images` endpoint (canonical URL) has a ~500-byte envelope and is unchanged.
- **The 32 MiB generated-image ceiling (#174661) had the wrong basis.** Its comment assumed the largest output was 3840x2160. Gemini "4K" is 5632x3072: measured photo PNGs were 27.2 and 28.9 MiB (85–90% of 32 MiB), and the same dimensions are 51.9 MB as uncompressed RGB. The ceiling is now 64 MiB, which holds an opaque 5632x3072 PNG and a transparent 3840x2160 RGBA gpt-image PNG (33.2 MB). It still never drops below a larger configured `mediaMaxMb`.

No config or schema change.

## Evidence

Live local agent turn through built dist, isolated state, one `image_generate` call with `openrouter/google/gemini-3.1-flash-image`, `resolution: "4K"`, OpenRouter base URL `https://openrouter.ai:443/api/v1` (real OpenRouter, non-canonical spelling so the chat endpoint is used):

```text
main (68a7e7b5b76): candidate failed: openrouter/google/gemini-3.1-flash-image: openrouter.image-generation: JSON response exceeds 45787819 bytes
this PR:            saved image-1---<id>.jpg  4925206 bytes  5632x3072
```

Response-shape measurements (one call each):

```text
/chat/completions 1K: json 2.21 MB = image base64 1.36 MB + reasoning_details[0].data 0.84 MB
/chat/completions 4K: json 55.8 MB, image 28.5 MB (json / base64 = 1.47)
/images 4K:           json 40.36 MB, image 30.27 MB, envelope ~500 bytes
```

Focused tests: the image provider suites (25 files, 289 tests) pass locally; ceiling-sized rejection tests moved to the new 64 MiB bound.

Limits: either change alone lets this 29 MiB image through; the chat factor matters for chat-path images above ~38 MiB, where the single-payload bound would cut the effective ceiling. Not run through the direct Google provider (no key).

**Merge danger:** two-way door. No state, config or contract change; a revert restores the old bounds. Blast radius: image provider downloads (per-image memory bound doubles to 64 MiB, times each provider's maximum result count) and OpenRouter chat-endpoint image requests.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

docs(agents): key caches by every input that changes the answer (#174837)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: agents keep shipping caches whose key leaves out an input that changes the answer. Callers then collide, serve another agent's or account's data, return stale results, or never hit the cache. No rule in `AGENTS.md` covers cache keys.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Agents get one rule that tells them what a cache key must contain and how to prove sharing is safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rule adds one line under "Runtime and code safeguards":
- key caches, memos, in-flight joins and shared snapshots by scope and request shape;
- give callers asking different questions separate slots;
- keep volatile values out of keys;
- prove sharing with a work-count test where differing callers interleave.

#174741 is the trigger. `usage.status` and `models.authStatus` shared one provider-usage slot per agent but asked for different provider sets. They evicted each other on every Models page load for 80 days, across 7 refactor passes, because no test interleaved the two callers.

## Evidence

I reviewed main since 2026-04-01: every `fix` commit whose diff touched cache-key, cache get/set or in-flight lines (728 commits). Each one was judged by reading its message and diff. **95 fixed a cache identity bug.** That is about 3 per week, steady every month (Apr 14, May 13, Jun 8, Jul 15, Aug 18, Sep 16, Oct 1–16 11).

| Kind | Count | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Key omits an input, so the answer is stale or wrong | 35 | 276ba1090e: markdown render cache ignored `codeBlockChrome` |
| Data leaks across agent, account or credential scope | 23 | 6a12c6f799: run→session lookup keyed by `runId` only; 1487b45eb8: GitHub previews shared across credentials; 51042e8c1a: cron deliveries routed to the wrong agent |
| Different callers collide or evict each other | 14 | c3f0b6abc0 (#174741); f8380a8324: route keys with separators collided |
| Key too volatile, so it never hits | 14 | 3f9d2415ac: prompt-cache key was the per-run session id |
| In-flight join dedups unrelated work | 9 | 2aabde7262: deep health probe joined a passive refresh; 4ca63cb98a: dispatch joined a different `executionMode` |

fix(anthropic): Claude CLI usage shows as unpriced in usage reports (#173792)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage reports show Claude CLI traffic (for example `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5`, the default CLI model) as "Unpriced", because the CLI reports no cost and the `claude-cli` catalog has no priced rows.

## User Impact

Usage views now estimate Claude CLI usage at Anthropic's API rates, as subscription routes such as Kimi Code already do. The figures are estimates of what the API would cost, not plan charges. Prices apply right away, offline included, from the bundled Anthropic catalog rows, with no catalog publish needed. A Claude CLI turn that used 1h prompt caching is now priced like the CLI's own cost figure.

## Why This Change Was Made

Since #168728, Claude CLI models come from the CLI's own menu with zero placeholder costs. Since #156535, estimates use the provider that handles the request, so `claude-cli/*` never picks up the `anthropic/*` rows.

- **`priceAs`:** a new `modelPricing` provider field names the provider whose catalog rows price this provider's models when it has no price of its own. `resolveModelPricing` tries that provider's row for the same model, one hop only. A provider's own catalog or hosted price still wins.
  - Plugin manifests already let `cliBackends` own `modelCatalog` rows. `modelPricing` now accepts them too.
  - The anthropic manifest declares `claude-cli: { priceAs: "anthropic" }`.
  - Each model has one price fact, and nothing extra is published to the hosted catalog.
- **1h cache writes:** Claude Code splits cache writes by TTL (`cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens`). `normalizeUsage` read only the camelCase `cacheWrite1h`, so CLI turns lost the 1h subset and would have been priced at the 5m rate. `normalizeUsage` now reads the split, and CLI usage records and persisted transcript usage carry it to the existing calculator.

## Evidence

- **End to end through the shipped Gateway (`openclaw gateway usage-cost`).**
  - Setup:
    - an isolated state and a build of this branch;
    - one real `openclaw agent --local` turn on `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5` through the `claude-cli` runtime;
    - a synthetic `claude` executable that answered with the repo's spawn-proof protocol and reported 1,000,000 input and 100,000 output tokens with no cost. No provider request was made.

  | Catalog state | `usage-cost` |
  |---|---|
  | Today's live hosted catalog (0 `claude-cli/*` keys), loaded with `openclaw models refresh` | `Total: $6.00 · 1.1m tokens` |
  | Catalog refresh disabled (bundled manifest rows only) | `Total: $6.00 · 1.1m tokens` |
  | Earlier revision's baseline, with no CLI pricing | `$0.0000`, `Missing cost: 1 (claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5 1)` |

- **1h cache writes against the CLI's own cost:**
  - **Recorded Claude 2.1 turn** (`test/fixtures/cli/claude-2.1-thinking-progress.jsonl`): it now prices at $0.40499, equal to the CLI's `costUSD`. Before the fix it priced at $0.26641.
  - **35 real Claude Code sessions on one install:** catalog rates with the 1h split reproduce the CLI's total `costUSD` exactly ($2.5640). Pricing every write at the 5m rate gives $1.763.
- **Tests:**
  - Resolver: `claude-cli/claude-opus-5-5` resolves to the `anthropic` row, and a `claude-cli` hosted price wins over the mapping. The mapping test fails without the fallback.
  - Manifest: `priceAs` is normalized for a CLI backend and dropped for an unowned id.
  - CLI usage: parsing and transcript persistence keep `cacheWrite1h`. The transcript test fails without the carry-through.
  - Pricing, manifest, bundled-manifest contract, session-cost and CLI output suites pass (114 tests).
  - The catalog publisher is unchanged. Its two local `second rename failure` cases also fail on main on this machine.
- **Gap (by design):** for tiered models such as `claude-haiku-5-5`, a multi-call turn whose summed prompt passes the 100k tier boundary stays unpriced. Whole-turn counters cannot show each call's tier.
- **Gap:** a per-agent `models.json` written by older versions can still hold frozen `claude-cli` rows, including zero costs. Those rows outrank the catalog. #174641 removes them.

**Merge risk:**
- A two-way door: a revert removes the field and the mapping. No state is written.
- It adds an optional `priceAs` field to the published `modelPricing` manifest contract and lets `cliBackends` declare pricing policies. Only the Anthropic plugin uses either.
- Blast radius: cost estimates for Claude CLI sessions. Routing and billing do not change.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

## User Impact

In the Control UI, mid-run plugin guidance, CLI harness context and Claude CLI task notifications now appear as a compact bordered card in the agent's own column, next to its activity rows. Collapsed, the card is a single header line (icon, label, time, chevron); expanded, it shows the text left-aligned under a divider. These notices are already marked as mid-run injections (collapsed body, not a new turn), so the existing notice renderer now draws them as an inline card instead of a divider. fix: web search hides an expired provider sign-in behind a generic error (#174651)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: when a search provider's sign-in expires and cannot refresh (Grok through an xAI OAuth profile), every `web_search` call fails with a generic "check configuration and connection" error. Nothing tells the agent, user or owner that the sign-in is dead, so search can stay broken for weeks.

## User Impact

- The agent sees that the search provider's sign-in expired, plus the fix: send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`. It can tell the user and pick another route. The message carries no profile id, account or upstream text.
- xAI search deadlines report `Search timed out after 60s` instead of the same generic error.
- The Control UI Search page (`webSearch.status`) uses the same auth health as Models. If the selected provider's sign-in is expired or missing, it says so and gives the same fix.

## Why This Change Was Made

`WebSearchProviderError.toResult()` mapped causes only by HTTP status and typed timeout. The OAuth manager's refresh failure already carries its provider and reason, but no HTTP status, so it fell through to the generic hint. The result boundary now reuses the existing OAuth refresh classifier and login-command builder from the model-run failure path. xAI wrapped its deadline in a plain `Error`; it now throws a typed `TimeoutError` with `timeoutMs`, the contract the boundary already reads. `webSearch.status` already mapped grok to its `authProviderId` but only checked that a profile exists. It now reads `buildAuthHealthSummary` for that provider.

No automatic fallback to another provider: an explicitly configured provider still fails visibly. Auto-detected selection already falls back.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway from this branch with `tools.web.search.provider = "grok"` and an `xai` OAuth profile whose access token expired and whose refresh token is invalid. The live xAI token endpoint returned `invalid_grant`.

`gateway call tools.invoke` with `web_search`:

- Before (`origin/main`): `provider_error: Search failed. Check this search provider's configuration and connection, or choose another provider.`
- After: `provider_error: Search failed: this search provider's xai sign-in expired and could not be refreshed. To fix it, send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai` on the Gateway. Until then, tell the user web search is unavailable and use another route.`

`gateway call webSearch.status`:

- Before: grok `configured: true`, `credentialSource: "auth-profile"`, no warning.
- After: route reason ends with `The xai sign-in this provider uses is expired. If a test search fails, send `/login xai` from a private chat or Control UI session, or run `openclaw models auth login --provider xai`.`

Neither output contains the profile id, tokens or the upstream refresh error.

Regression control: with this PR's tests and base-branch source, the five new cases fail (both sign-in messages, both xAI deadline type checks, expired status reason); they pass on this head. The fresh-sign-in status case passes on both.

Focused tests: `web-search.provider-errors`, `web-search-status`, `web-search-status.auth`, xAI `web-search`, `web-search.auth-lifecycle`, `x-search`, `web-search.signal`.

Limits: the status route in the repro had no prepared model catalog, so the reason appeared on the "model route not ready" branch. The managed-route branch is covered by the code path and unit test, not the live run. The status signal uses existing health semantics: an OAuth profile past its expiry time shows as expired even when refresh might still work, so the text says to test first.

Merge danger: two-way door. No config, schema, protocol or stored-state change; a revert restores the old text. Blast radius is `web_search` error text for providers that sign in through an OAuth profile, xAI search timeout errors, and the Search page reason text.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix(media): image providers discard outputs above the media cap (#174661)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a paid image generation is thrown away when the provider returns an image above the media store cap (default 6 MB). For example, `openai/gpt-image-2` at 2048x2048, quality high, returns an ~8.8 MB PNG and fails with `openai.image-generation: JSON response exceeds 9437184 bytes`.

## User Impact

User impact: large generated images (up to a 32 MB per-image download ceiling) now reach persistence, which re-encodes them to fit the media cap (#174601) instead of failing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Image providers bounded their downloads by the media store cap (`resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes(cfg, "image")`). Since #174601, persistence fits oversized images to that cap, so the store cap is the wrong bound for the provider read. The provider read now uses a memory ceiling:

- New `resolveGeneratedImageDownloadMaxBytes(cfg)` in `openclaw/plugin-sdk/media-generation-runtime`: 32 MB per image (an uncompressed 4K RGBA PNG), and never below a larger configured `mediaMaxMb`.
- Migrated image downloads: OpenAI, Google, fal, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Microsoft Foundry, Vydra, Comfy and the shared OpenAI-compatible provider (DeepInfra, LiteLLM, xAI).
- Audio and video downloads keep the store cap. The SDK addition is additive; `resolveGeneratedMediaMaxBytes` is unchanged.

No config or schema change.

## Evidence

Live local agent turn (isolated state, built `dist`): one `image_generate` call with `openai/gpt-image-2`, `2048x2048`, `quality: high`, `outputFormat: png`:

```text
before (main + #174601): candidate failed: openai/gpt-image-2: openai.image-generation: JSON response exceeds 9437184 bytes
after:  saved image-1---<id>.jpg  2107627 bytes  JPEG  2048x2048
```

Focused tests (the affected image-provider suites pass locally):
- The download ceiling defaults to 32 MB and keeps a larger configured cap.
- Vydra, fal, Comfy and Google keep generated images above a tiny configured cap (previously rejected).
- OpenAI and LiteLLM keep URL downloads above the configured cap and reject streamed downloads above the 32 MB ceiling.
- OpenAI-compatible and Microsoft Foundry still reject JSON beyond the new ceiling.

Not covered: the Codex app-server image path (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector-media.ts`) still drops images above the store cap. It saves without a fit step, so it needs its own change.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. The SDK gains one export; reverting removes it, and no bundled caller outside this PR uses it. Blast radius: image-generation provider downloads. Their memory bound per image rises from the store cap to 32 MB, scaled by each provider's maximum result count.

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix(gateway): Models page never shows provider usage and re-probes providers on every load (#174741)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Models page never shows provider usage, and every page load re-runs provider usage probes, when `models.authStatus` and `usage.status` are requested together (as the page does).

## User Impact

User impact: provider usage appears on the Models page on load. Provider usage endpoints are polled once per 60 s cache window per provider set instead of on every page load.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both RPCs share one provider-usage cache entry and one in-flight refresh per agent. They ask for different provider sets: `models.authStatus` asks for providers with refreshable credentials, and `usage.status` asks for every usage-capable provider. When they ran together, each read missed the other's entry and started a refresh that superseded the other's in-flight refresh, so the earlier result was discarded. The result:
- `usage.status` answered `{ providers: [], refreshing: true }` on every load.
- `models.authStatus` carried no `usage`.
- Each load re-resolved auth and plugin runtime for every usage provider, and probed provider endpoints.

The cache now keeps one entry and one in-flight refresh per provider set within each agent. Nothing else changes: TTL, credential-bound invalidation, cold-read markers and stale-while-revalidate stay as they were.

`a21f235` (#115369) intended the two readers to share this cache. A later change gave them different provider sets.

## Evidence

Isolated Gateway on a copy of a real state directory: outbound network denied, base and fix run ABAB on the same restored state.

- **Work count** (alternating `usage.status` / `models.authStatus`, 8 calls): outbound usage probes on 7 of 8 calls (base) vs only on the first refresh of each provider set (fix).
- **Responses after identical warm-up:** `agents.list`, `config.get`, `models.list` and `sessions.usage` are identical. `usage.status` now returns the provider snapshots instead of `refreshing: true`. `models.authStatus` providers now carry `usage`.
- **Serial p50 over 20 calls, two rounds:** `usage.status` 4.9/4.3 ms → 0.8/1.0 ms. `models.list` 30.5/27.2 ms → 2.2/2.5 ms; the per-call refresh was also blocking it on the main thread. The host was heavily loaded, so treat wall times as indicative only.
- **CPU profile:** the per-load `resolveProviderRuntimePlugin` → `applyPluginAutoEnable` frames (~100 ms main thread per page load) are gone from steady-state page loads.
- **Tests:** new regression `refreshes each provider set once per TTL when page reads interleave` fails on base (4 refreshes in 3 loads) and passes with the fix (2). `usage.status-cache`, `usage-cache` and `models-auth-status` suites pass (66 tests).

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

feat(ui): browse folders on paired devices for existing-folder sessions (#174713)

Related: #169722

## What Problem This Solves

**Existing folder on device** sessions require you to type an absolute path on the paired device. The **Browse folders** picker lists only the Gateway host, so it cannot help you find the folder on the device.

## User Impact

Admins can choose **Browse folders on <device>** in the New Session project menu, open folders on the selected paired device, and click **Use this folder** to fill the device path. Writers still type the path, because node folder listing is admin-only.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The Gateway already routes `fs.listDir` with `nodeId` to the node's directory listing (#105114). #126187 removed that route from New Session together with legacy `execNode` sessions, so the picker cannot reach it now.
- This change reuses the same picker and Gateway route for device-folder sessions only. The menu item appears when all of these are true:
  - device folders are available for the selected device
  - the operator is an admin
  - the device can invoke `fs.listDir`
- Device listings skip Gateway-only side effects: folder approval, the Git checkout probe and project registration.
- The Gateway now keeps a node's `INVALID_REQUEST` folder errors (for example `ENOENT`) as request errors. Before, it reported them as `UNAVAILABLE`. With this change, a stale or partly typed device path opens the device home folder, the same as the Gateway picker does.
- There is no protocol, schema or config change. The listing is not limited to `nodeHost.workerRuns.folders` roots. The device still checks the chosen folder when the session is created. The docs say this.

## Evidence

**Live, isolated Gateway + separate session-host node (both from this branch), real Control UI:**
- Selected the paired node, chose **Browse folders on Synthetic laptop**, and opened `projects/`. The listing showed the node's own home, not the Gateway's.
- Picked `device-only-tries`. The path field filled, and `sessions.create` stored that `deviceFolder`.
- The session dispatched to the device. A turn ran `pwd > proof.txt`, and the file appeared in the picked folder on the node.
- Typed `/nope/missing-on-device`, then chose browse. The picker opened the device home with no error.

* perf(agents): bound catalog worker young-generation heap

(cherry picked from commit a3510e81ba559bd8b312412c2288ef45e94c584a)

* fix(memory): keep cold Gateway start from opening every agent's index

#167756 started Memory Core's index service eagerly on every Gateway start,
opening each configured agent's memory manager right after readiness. On an
idle Gateway that startup catch-up touches every session-transcript read lane,
so each lane spawns its own worker isolate (plus a memory-search worker): the
2026.10.5 Gateway startup peak RSS rose from ~1.1 GB to ~1.8 GB.

or turn that needs an agent's index opens it. Once a watched manager has run in
the process (a process-wide fact that survives plugin instance replacement and
resets with a Gateway restart), every later service start reopens all configured
indexes, so plugin reloads, provider-only reloads, rollback recovery, and
memory/agent config restarts still resume watching without a search or turn.

* perf(sqlite): bound broker and transcript worker young-generation heaps

Cap the SQLite broker carriers and session-transcript reader workers at a
32 MiB young generation, matching the catalog worker bound, while keeping the
existing 512 MiB old-generation allowance. Worker counts, lanes, admission,
and lifecycle custody are unchanged.

V8's default nursery grows to ~63 MiB per worker after a startup allocation
burst and stays resident on idle workers. On the 2026.10.5 Gateway (fresh
state, forced 16 CPUs) the broker's heap total at startup peak fell
125 -> 91 MiB and the transcript reader 81 -> 34-66 MiB; with the Memory Core
cold-start fix, max Gateway peak RSS over the runs fell 1152 -> 1117 MB.
Tradeoff: more frequent scavenges during large allocation bursts in these
workers.

fix(models): Claude CLI usage priced at $0 from stale models.json copies (#174641)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: usage reports show Claude CLI models at $0.00 when an older OpenClaw version copied plugin catalog rows into an agent's root `models.json`. Those rows also outrank the live catalog forever. On one affected install this hid $220 of `claude-opus-4-8` usage behind a frozen zero price.

## User Impact

- New writes never put discovered plugin rows in the root `models.json`.
- `openclaw doctor --fix`, which update also runs, removes old copies. It removes a provider block only when it is an exact copy of a block in that plugin's generated catalog.
- Doctor saves the previous file as `models.json.bak-<timestamp>` and lists every removed provider.
- Edited blocks, blocks with credentials or overrides, and ids that config declares are never touched.
- Afterwards, prices come from the current catalog, and `models status` shows Claude CLI native auth instead of `missing`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery copies a plugin's provider under its hook aliases, so `claude-cli` received the `anthropic` catalog. When owner lookup failed, the writer sent that copy to the author-owned root file instead of the plugin catalog. Owner lookup fails for a scoped plugin snapshot, or for an alias no manifest claims (on main today: `google-antigravity`, `google-interactions`, `azure-openai`, `modelstudio-native`). Since #142302 the root file merge keeps every existing provider, so the copy never left. The cost resolver reads the root file first, so its zero placeholders for unpriced models won over catalog prices.

- **Writer:** records which plugin produced each discovered provider id. When owner lookup fails, it stores the row with that producer unless config declares the id.
- **Doctor:** the catalog owner (`doctor-plugin-model-catalog.ts`) gets the legacy repair. A detector compares root blocks with the generated catalogs and requires exact equality, so no pricing or shape heuristics are involved. The file is rewritten, never deleted, because registry reads require it.

## Evidence

- **Census:** in 8 releases (2026.5.28 → 2026.10.4) run in isolated state, plain Claude CLI use never wrote the root file. The leak needs a scoped or partial owner snapshot. A real affected file, from 2026-09-06, is a byte-for-byte deep copy of the `anthropic` block in that install's generated catalog.
- **Upgrade harness:** I seeded 2026.9.2 state with that real file plus a hand-authored `my-proxy` provider, then ran the candidate's `openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive`.
  - `claude-cli` was removed and `my-proxy` kept. The backup is byte-identical to the seeded file.
  - A second Doctor run found nothing.
  - Two later `models.json` writes left the file hash unchanged (`3bcc218b…`).
  - Control (same migrated state with the original file restored):
    - unchanged: default model, resolved model, allowlist, fallbacks, and the agent turn (`provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5`);
    - the model list drops only the 7 duplicate `claude-cli/*` rows;
    - Claude CLI runtime auth goes from `missing` to `claude-cli:runtime-synthetic`, the same in repeated runs.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable (2026.10.4):**
  - Seeding: 2026.10.4 created the state, with a config provider carrying a fake key, an `openai` API-key auth profile and one real Claude CLI session. I then added the real leaked `claude-cli` root block, its generated `anthropic` catalog row and an authored root provider with a fake key. The candidate's `doctor --fix --non-interactive` then ran.
  - Removed: `claude-cli` only. The backup is byte-identical to the seeded file, and a second Doctor run changed nothing.
  - Kept: the authored root provider with its key, the config provider with its key, the auth profile, and the session (same key and id).
  - The Claude CLI turn works before and after.
  - Every other config or auth change also happens with 2026.10.4's own Doctor on the same seed: the legacy `claude-cli/*` default canonicalized to `anthropic/*`, and plaintext keys copied into auth profiles. The one exception is main's existing `"anthropic/*"` runtime entry. That Doctor leaves the `claude-cli` copy in place.
- **Copy of a real install** (credentials, leases and other plugins' catalogs stripped; isolated Gateway): Doctor found and removed the copy. `sessions.usage` for June–October, with a fresh cache and only the root file differing:

  | claude-cli model | turns | stale root | repaired |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | claude-opus-4-8 | 2105 | $0.00 | $220.04 |
  | claude-haiku-4-5 | 12 | $0.00 | $0.20 |
  | other Claude models | 609 | $95.35 | $95.35 |

  Token totals are identical (4,307,266,930). The $220.04 equals the transcript token sums at the catalog's Opus 4.8 rates.
- **Comparison with the CLI's own cost:** Claude Code recorded `costUSD` for 35 sessions on that install. Catalog rates reproduce all of them exactly ($2.5640 vs $2.5640) once cache writes are priced at the 1h rate. Historical OpenClaw transcripts did not store that split, so they estimate those turns about 31% low. #173792 records the split for new turns.
- **Tests:**
  - Doctor: exact copy removed once with a byte-exact backup; edited copy kept; config-declared id kept.
  - Writer: an unowned hook alias goes to the producing plugin's catalog, not the root file. It fails without the fix.
  - The `models-config`, plugin catalog and Doctor catalog suites pass (208 tests).

**Merge risk:**
- **Writer change:** a two-way door; revert restores the old routing.
- **Doctor repair:** rewrites user files, but only exact generated copies, always with a full backup, so a removal is recoverable by restoring the backup.
- **Blast radius:** agents whose root `models.json` holds generated plugin copies, mainly Claude CLI installs from 2026-05 to 2026-10. Unowned alias copies no longer appear as separate models; they carried the producer's baseUrl under another id.

Related: #158606. Preserves the configured-budget accounting from #171495.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes selected conversation history being silently shortened before native Codex receives it in explicitly budgeted context-engine conversations.

## User Impact

Selected text and restored attachments reach Codex without a second silent history cutoff. Later turns append only newly selected history; an unchanged selection is not injected again, including after a Gateway restart. A rewritten selection starts a fresh native thread rather than duplicating overlapping history in the old one.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old projection and `turn/start` limits could discard earlier goals, constraints, tool results, and attachments after the context engine had already selected them.

- Bootstrap a native thread with the full selection through acknowledged `thread/inject_items`, using quoted user-role text fragments of at most 8,192 UTF-8 bytes and separate default-detail images. Keep the current request separate.
- Match the previous selection against a rolling prefix identity. Inject only an appended suffix into that thread; rotate on a rewrite or an incompatible engine, epoch, model, or budget policy.
- Reserve carrier overhead as input, preserving the existing output reservation and successful assembly budget for post-turn maintenance. Reject restored-media overage instead of clipping it.
- Mark an in-flight append in the existing projection fingerprint before native delivery. An uncertain append or interrupted acknowledgment causes a fresh thread on retry, not replay into the same native epoch.
- Remove full-selection reinjection on reused configured threads. The bounded single-input path remains for unconfigured legacy projections and no-engine continuity, whose existing limits are unchanged.

**History ownership:** Codex owns the native thread and its compaction. Native compaction may later summarize injected history. Use the built-in OpenClaw runtime when the context engine must own the model's history on every request.

### Compatibility

No settings, database columns, stored-row fields, schema versions, dependencies, or native protocol versions change. The existing `projection.fingerprint` string carries a self-identifying `selection-v1:` digest. Existing bindings rotate once before full delivery; subsequent turns use deltas. Older code treats the new fingerprint/policy as incompatible and rotates once rather than interpreting it as an old bootstrap fingerprint. The old native transcript is preserved.

One owner prepares the selection, computes deltas, creates quoted items, appends them, and records acknowledgment. The legacy projector only supplies its existing message serialization; configured history never enters its single-input renderer. Thanks to @lordratner, @aounakram, and @NianJiuZst for the report, original repair, and investigation.

## Evidence

Published `openclaw@2026.10.4` + `@openclaw/codex@2026.10.4` → this candidate: [six-turn saved-session upgrade proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171707#issuecomment-6224406674) passed; stable binding creation/reuse, one upgrade rotation, suffix-only appends, restart without reinjection, byte-identical old rollout, saved settings/history, and synthetic fact recall.

Verified on `a242252312a409a5cd173fad58cd272c2562a9db`, against main `0708aa95c5e6a6d775101cd80380f9cde7a96ab1`.

[Sanitized native delivery record](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171707#issuecomment-6222808990).

A real CLI → isolated Gateway → stock Codex app-server → synthetic loopback Responses endpoint ran five turns: 1.2 million selected characters, an append, a Gateway restart with unchanged selection, a deliberate rewrite, and another append. Utility routing was disabled and a socket guard restricted Node egress to loopback. Web search was denied in both captures to hold unrelated native thread policy constant. No external model request or real credential was used in these final captures.

**Before:** 34 selected messages were missing on every model request, including the oldest marker.

| Turn | Selected chars | Injected history items/chars | Rotation | Model input items/bytes | Oldest marker |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Initial | 1,200,000 | 0 / 0 | No | 7 / 1,200,219 | Missing |
| Append | 1,224,000 | 0 / 0 | No | 9 / 2,366,611 | Missing |
| Restart, unchanged | 1,224,000 | 0 / 0 | No | 15 / 3,566,524 | Missing |
| Rewrite | 1,224,000 | 0 / 0 | No | 17 / 4,732,916 | Missing |
| Append | 1,248,000 | 0 / 0 | No | 19 / 5,899,308 | Missing |

**After:** every selected message reached the model intact, and the oldest marker appeared exactly once. Injection acknowledgments preceded inference.

| Turn | Selected chars | Injected history items/chars | Rotation | Model input items/bytes | Oldest marker |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---|
| Initial | 1,200,000 | 174 / 1,224,765 | No | 181 / 1,480,908 | Once |
| Append | 1,224,000 | 4 / 24,561 | No | 187 / 1,510,235 | Once |

| Rewrite | 1,224,000 | 178 / 1,249,329 | Yes | 185 / 1,509,966 | Once |

The largest historical text item was 8,192 UTF-8 bytes. Current native input was 8,454 bytes at bootstrap/resume and 93 bytes on warm appends, without historical content. Native developer-policy refresh after restart is separate from history injection. Assembly, commit, and post-turn maintenance retained the same 641,005-token allowance; output reservation remained 20,000 tokens. Synthetic usage proves delivery and lifecycle behavior, not tokenizer accuracy or native compaction quality.

**Simplification:** configured history no longer uses the single-input projector or its preservation modes. Carrier construction and append acknowledgment share one owner. Test-only framing exports, the duplicate native history scenario, and redundant projection/continuity fixtures were removed; main's existing native-skill and bounded-continuity regressions were restored unchanged.

Against main, production is +574/-85 lines (net +489) and tests are +444/-1 (net +443). Against `619a7e19b58`, this removes 54 net production lines and 947 net test lines: 1,002 fewer lines overall including the obsolete assertion-baseline entry. Finite restored-media accounting stays with delivery because splitting it out would reject supported selected attachments or silently omit them.

Focused checks: 68 tests passed across five files. They retain the eight distinct failure classes: oversized selection, suffix-only append, rewrite rotation, cold resume, fresh/reused lost acknowledgment, legacy fingerprint upgrade, restored-media overage, and invalid/unknown allowance. Scoped formatting/lint and the application build passed. After moving fresh-thread injection into the same owner, the 17 affected history/media regressions also passed; the unused assertion-baseline allowance was pruned.

**Merge danger:** One-way for native history already written: reverting code does not unappend items or restore superseded thread bindings. Code rollback is supported through fingerprint incompatibility. Blast radius is explicitly budgeted Codex context-engine conversations; ordinary no-engine continuity and unconfigured projection limits remain unchanged.

fix(media): generated images over the media cap are discarded (#174601)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a paid `image_generate` result is thrown away with `Media exceeds 6MB limit` when the provider returns an image larger than the media store cap (for example a `gpt-image-2` 2048x2048 high-quality PNG, about 8–9 MB). The error also did not say whether the input reference or the generated output was too large, so agents re-compressed small references and retried.

## User Impact

User impact: oversized generated images are saved instead of discarded. The tool result says what was saved (format, size, dimensions). When nothing can fit, or when a reference fails to load, the error names which image failed, its size and the cap, so the agent can choose a correct recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

The media store cap is OpenClaw policy (`agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, default 6 MB). Providers cannot know it, and PNG size depends on image content, so the provider request cannot guarantee a fit. The image generation step that owns persistence now fits each oversized output before saving, using the shared Rastermill encoder:

- Opaque images are re-encoded as JPEG, starting at quality 92 and full dimensions. Dimensions shrink only when no quality step fits.
- Transparent images stay PNG (alpha is preserved) and shrink instead.
- The saved file name extension follows the new format.
- It fails only when no encoding fits: `Generated image 1 (image/png, 8.39MB) exceeds the 6MB media limit; the smallest re-encoding is …`.

Reference loading for media tools now prefixes failures with the reference index (`image reference 1 could not be loaded: …`). Inline data-URL size errors now include the payload size and the limit.

There is no retry loop, no change to the default cap, and no config or schema change.

## Evidence

Replay of a real `gpt-image-2` output (2048x2048, quality high, PNG, 8,801,742 bytes) through `executeImageGenerationJob`, with real media-store persistence:

```text
=== main (4a9f90225fa)
fixture: 8801742 bytes image/png
FAILED: Media exceeds 6MB limit

=== this PR
Generated image 1 (image/png, 8.39MB) exceeded the 6MB media limit; saved as image/jpeg, 1.85MB, 2048x2048.
Attachments:
1. type=image name="image-1.jpg" mimeType=image/jpeg path="<state>/…"
saved on disk: 1942515 bytes image/jpeg { width: 2048, height: 2048 }
```

Focused tests:
- `image-generate-tool.test.ts`: an over-cap generated PNG is saved as JPEG under the cap with its dimensions kept. A no-fit case fails with the generated image's size and the cap, and nothing is saved. An oversized inline reference reports `image reference 1` with its size and the limit.
- The 13 media-generation tool test files pass locally (225 tests).

Live run: a local agent turn called `image_generate` with `openai/gpt-image-2` 2048x2048 high through the API-key transport. That output (about 8.8 MB) was rejected earlier, by the OpenAI provider's response bound (`JSON response exceeds 9437184 bytes`), which also applies on `main`. Image providers bound their downloads by the same store cap; that is a separate owner and is tracked as a follow-up. This PR covers every output that reaches persistence, which is the `Media exceeds 6MB limit` failure.

**Merge danger:** two-way door. No state, config or published contract changes; a revert restores the old behavior. Blast radius: `image_generate` outputs over the cap (now saved as JPEG or a smaller PNG instead of failing) and the error text for media-tool reference load failures.

errors fall back to ws's own path for canonical close codes. Frames of 16 KiB
and up are compressed at level 1; hello-ok, which carries device tokens, is

fix: github-copilot shows as *** in logs and diagnostics after Copilot runs (#173791)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: logs, diagnostics bundles and OTel exports show the provider `github-copilot` as `***` after any GitHub Copilot run.

## User Impact

User impact: `github-copilot` and Copilot identity values (`Copilot-Integration-Id`, editor and user-agent values) are no longer masked by egress redaction. Credential protection is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Copilot returned its identity headers (`Openai-Organization: github-copilot` and others) from `prepareRuntimeAuth`. Core treats every value from that credential-exchange hook as a secret: it seals the value and registers it for exact-value redaction. So the string `github-copilot` became a "secret" and was masked everywhere redaction runs. Before f956a187413 it was also written into transcripts as `provider: "***"`.

The fix is in the Copilot plugin, which owns these headers:

- `prepareRuntimeAuth` no longer returns identity headers. It still returns the model's configured headers, so inline header credentials stay sealed and registered for redaction.
- Identity headers are attached by the provider stream wrappers. Agent runs, compaction, btw and image requests already use `wrapStreamFn`. Direct completions now use a new `wrapSimpleCompletionStreamFn`.
- Core credential protection (`protectPreparedProviderRuntimeAuth`) is unchanged, so headers that a provider returns from an auth exchange stay protected.

## Evidence

- Docker E2E (built package, real Gateway, HTTPS stand-ins for `api.github.com` and the Copilot API, one Copilot agent turn, then `logs.tail`):
  - `main`: `logs.tail` shows `agent model: ***/gpt-5.4-mini`.
  - This PR: `logs.tail` shows `agent model: github-copilot/gpt-5.4-mini`. The Copilot request still carries `Openai-Organization: github-copilot` and `Copilot-Integration-Id: copilot-developer-cli`. The bearer token does not appear in `logs.tail`.
- New tests in `extensions/github-copilot/index.test.ts` fail on `main` and pass here: runtime auth keeps configured headers but not identity headers; the direct-completion wrapper sends identity headers; an unresolved integration SecretRef fails in both wrappers before any request.
- Copilot extension tests, provider secret egress, auth controller and provider runtime tests pass (301 tests).

Co-authored-by: Ayaan Zaidi <hi@obviy.us>

fix(update): cancel Gateway extended-stable lookup (#161067)

fix(update): cancel the pending npm lookup when the Gateway stops during update discovery

On extended-stable installs, the Gateway's background update discovery asks the npm registry which version the selector points to, then requests that exact version. If the Gateway was stopped while the selector request was still pending, that request wasn't cancelled; when it finished, the exact-version request could still go out after shutdown had begun. Stopping the Gateway now cancels the outstanding selector request, so nothing is sent after stop. Normal discovery is unchanged.

Update behavior: this changes only the running Gateway's discovery shutdown; it doesn't touch how updates are installed.

Proof: an installed npm-global package under real systemd in Docker, with a local npm registry that held the selector response. On main, stopping the Gateway mid-discovery still produced the exact-version request after stop began (twice). With this change (rebuilt on current main) the selector request is cancelled, no exact-version request is sent, and the service stops cleanly. A control without a stop completes both requests normally.

Thanks @adenzhou1350.

fix(imap): avoid invalid startup cursors when UIDNEXT is unavailable (#162548)

fix(imap): set the starting cursor when the server doesn't report UIDNEXT

When an IMAP server omitted UIDNEXT, a fresh mail watcher saved its cursor as NaN instead of taking a baseline from the existing mail, so it couldn't track new messages. Without UIDNEXT, the watcher now derives the baseline from the highest existing UID: existing mail is skipped and only new mail is processed. Servers that send UIDNEXT behave as before, and messages the parser rejects are still skipped (#173231).

Proof: built Gateway with the bundled IMAP plugin against a local IMAP server that omits UIDNEXT. On main the watcher saved a NaN cursor (twice). With this change it baselined at UID 9007 without delivering old mail, fetched new mail, skipped a malformed message once and advanced past it, and after a restart picked up mail that arrived while it was offline without rebaselining.

Fixes #162543. Thanks @linancn.

## What Problem This Solves

Scheduled main run [38455449231](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38455449231/job/115497339237) reports a schema-version-zero failure while loading the Automations model catalog. Since `74a5c29c601ab84c3d5bc9b402043bef0177bb23` (#170902), that child keeps its reader, along with empty schema admission facts. A later catalog read can inherit those facts after the same file has been initialized.

Its normal close retires the child-local empty admission facts; the next operation admits the initialized file. Initialized and partial-schema readers remain pooled. There are no new queries, freshness probes, cross-thread handshakes, schema changes, or credential-authority changes.

docs(agents): say ClawSweeper reviews each PR automatically only once (#174533)

## What Problem This Solves

Since 2026-10-15, ClawSweeper reviews each PR automatically **once**, when it opens or leaves draft. Later pushes, description edits, and reopens do not start a new review; someone must comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. Nothing in the agent instructions said this, and `docs/reference/pull-request-review-flow.md` still said not to expect an immediate review after "pushing a commit", which implies pushes get reviewed. Agents wait for a review that never comes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `AGENTS.md`: one line next to the fresh-review rule. It states the one-automatic-review rule and when to post `@clawsweeper re-review`, and links to the review flow doc for the details.
- `docs/reference/pull-request-review-flow.md`: states the one-automatic-review rule and removes "pushing a commit" from the list of things that start a review. The command list and permissions do not change.

## User Impact

Contributors and agents know that after a push they must request the next ClawSweeper review themselves, once the branch, body, and proof are current.

## Evidence

- Docs-only. `git diff --check` is clean.
- `pnpm docs:check-links:anchors` gives the same 6 failures with and without this change; none are in the changed files. `pnpm docs:spellcheck` failures are also outside the changed files.
- Source of the rule: openclaw/clawsweeper `AGENTS.md` ("Ordinary PRs receive one automatic completed review… Later pushes, edits, reopen events, and scheduled passes require a new explicit review request").

fix(doctor): end launcher-bound maintenance owners gracefully when their launcher dies (#174268)

Killing a hung openclaw doctor --fix left its respawned child alive (reparented to PID 1) and renewing sqlite-maintenance ownership, so every later Gateway start failed with 'undergoing offline maintenance' and stale-owner recovery never fired because the recorded owner was still alive. CLI respawns now carry an explicit launcher-bound lifetime marker; when the launcher disappears the owner is asked to cancel, rolls back and releases its lease while keeping custody during cleanup, and is escalated only after ten seconds. Detached update and handoff drivers stay independent by default and are never terminated because their launcher exited. Live on macOS: launcher killed → owner exits in 0.22 s, lock released, zero orphans, next Gateway HTTP 200, SQLite integrity ok. The separate zero-output Doctor hang is addressed by the bounded SQLite admission wait (#174060).

perf(gateway): cut allocation hotspots under concurrent agent turns (#174130)

* perf(gateway): trim per-request and per-turn allocation hotspots

Heap profiles of the gateway concurrency bench (16 sessions x 4 turns with
tool events, history clients, subscribers, control plane) showed:

- Control UI bootstrap and config.get rebuilt the full schema redaction
  lookup per request (~7% of sampled allocations). Cache it per immutable
  ConfigUiHints object.
- Embedded attempt cleanup spread the whole attempt params per cleanup step;
  pass only the fields runOwnedAgentCleanup reads.
- intersectSessionEventToolsAllow rebuilt a tool-policy matcher (group
  expansion + glob compile) for every candidate x restriction pair; build
  one matcher per restriction.
- Tool descriptor snapshots were per session only, so every new session
  republished identical descriptors. Seed a session's first attempt from the
  latest snapshot with identical inputs; per-tool identity checks still gate
  every reuse.

* perf(agents): skip redundant context copies on the turn path

- Bootstrap file and routing resolution spread the whole embedded attempt
  for every call; pass the fields their callees declare.
- Re-entering the current plugin execution frame still called
  AsyncLocalStorage.run, which copies the entire async context map; run
  the callback directly when the frame is already current.
- Gateway scope copies built two property descriptors per key; plain
  enumerable-checked assignment onto the fresh scope is equivalent.

* perf(agents): share descriptor publication between concurrent cold sessions

Sessions that start together all miss the descriptor snapshot and each
republished and prewarmed the same provider schemas at settlement. At
publish time, reuse an entry another session already published when its
source schema, output schema, and description identities match.

* perf(gateway): stop re-deriving paths and buffers on hot read paths

- The activity-summary pump rechecks every queued state and re-resolved
  each one's session store path; memoize store paths per config
  publication.
- matchesAgentDatabaseReadCandidatePath resolved both paths even when
  they were the identical string.
- SQLite worker transfers copied single-frame records into a fresh buffer
  before deserializing; deserialize the frame bytes directly.

* refactor(gateway): keep recap store-path memo with activity-summary state

Move the per-config store-path memo next to the other activity-summary
scope helpers to keep the service under the file-size limit, and drop the
single-frame transfer fast path: the profiled bytes were the deserialized
values themselves, not the reassembly copy.

* fix(gateway): address review on shared descriptors and recap store paths

- Key the activity-summary store-path memo by the store setting value;
  config publications can mutate the same object in place.
- Require a matching tool name before reusing another session's
  published descriptor.

The sidebar kept sessions.messages narration subscriptions for its session rows whenever live activity was on, even when the sessions list was not visible (roster mode, collapsed or hidden navigation, other navigation views, contextual sidebar). fix(update): bound stalled inspections so update status always returns (#174060)

openclaw update status (and the post-activation Doctor that shares its inspections) could hang forever with the event loop idle: the SQLite worker admission exchange waited on Atomics.wait with no timeout, so a vanished host peer could never wake it. The exchange now inherits the caller's deadline through the worker broker and task transport, with a ten-minute safety bound when no caller deadline exists; operation scopes retire when their operation settles, so one operation's deadline never leaks into another. A timeout surfaces as a recoverable 'unavailable' error and never cancels an admitted write. update status gains an overall deadline and reports each inspection it could not complete by name while keeping the shipped --json shape; status/Doctor history reads leave the synchronous bridges, and caller cancellation reaches state snapshot reads, the registry fetch, and run reconciliation. Also fixes partial-export exposure under concurrent imports found by the native same-session e2e. Live: status returns in 5.3 s without a package lockfile and 9.5 s with the state database locked, naming the unavailable section.

feat(agents): compaction safety timeout bounds stalls when progress is reported (#130973)

* feat(agents): compaction safety timeout bounds stalls when progress is reported

The compaction safety timeout is an aggregate wall clock: a healthy
summarization stream that merely needs minutes (reasoning-mode models on
large contexts) is killed mid-flight, and no fixed total budget fixes that —
the budget scales with total work instead of health.

compactWithSafetyTimeout now hands its wrapped callback an optional progress
function; each call re-arms the timer, so a reporting compaction is bounded
by maximum silence instead of total time. Callers that ignore it keep the
exact aggregate-budget behavior of today. Plugin context engines receive
onProgress in their compact() params alongside the existing abortSignal
cooperation contract.

Grounded in DeepSeek Harness (MIT), which bounds summarization with a
per-read idle watchdog and no aggregate budget at all.

* fix: satisfy prefer-const on timeoutListener

* fix: register onProgress as a declared host param

ClawSweeper finding: onProgress is host-injected like the other compact
lifecycle fields, so it belongs in CONTEXT_ENGINE_HOST_PARAMS — engines with
a declared acceptedHostParams list now opt in explicitly (undclared engines
keep receiving everything). Guide + projection coverage updated to match.

* fix: absolute compaction ceiling + timeout-abort listener cleanup

ClawSweeper P1: the stall timer was the only bound and progress re-arms it,
so a faulty engine reporting progress forever could defer compaction
indefinitely. An independent absolute ceiling (10x the stall budget, not
re-armable, no new configuration surface) now bounds that case.

ClawSweeper P2: the timeoutAbortPromise abort listener was never removed
when compaction won the race; stored and removed in the same finally as the
other listeners.

* fix: prefer-const on absoluteTimer

* fix: satisfy probe-engine param typing in onProgress tests

The three tests added with host-param registration omit the required
assembleCalls capture array, and index capture arrays without guarding
noUncheckedIndexedAccess. Pass explicit empty captures (matching every
other call site) and use optional chaining where a missing call must
still fail the assertion.

* fix: re-clamp absolute compaction ceiling through the timer bound

The 10x absolute ceiling passed the multiplied delay to setTimeout
without the shared Node-safe clamp; a stall budget already at the
timer maximum would overflow the delay bound and abort immediately.
Resolve the product through resolveTimerTimeoutMs and cover the
maximum input with a regression test. Document the changed contract:
timeoutSeconds is a total-duration bound without progress, a silence
budget for reporting engines, always capped by the 10x ceiling.

* fix: timeout rejection outranks cancellation-driven completion

The rejection listener is now the first observer of the timeout signal,
registered before the cancel hook and the composed abort signal. A
cooperative compaction that settles synchronously from onCancel (the
production activeSession.abortCompaction path) could previously queue
its fulfillment ahead of the timeout rejection and fulfill the race
after the deadline. Regression test proven failing on the prior
ordering. Docs now state the absolute ceiling is timer-clamped.

fix(litellm): interactive onboarding never asks for the proxy base URL (#173164)

* fix(litellm): interactive onboarding never asks for the proxy base URL

`openclaw onboard --auth-choice litellm-api-key` captures only an API key and
silently keeps http://localhost:4000 with a seeded claude-opus-4-6, so operators
on a remote proxy end up pointed at localhost with one selectable model. The
non-interactive path already honors --custom-base-url; the interactive one has no
equivalent prompt.

Ask for the proxy base URL before the API key, seeded from any already-configured
value. Enter keeps the default and leaves config untouched, so applyLitellmConfig
still seeds the default model exactly as before; entering a custom URL records it
and lets the merged explicit-URL discovery list the proxy's models.

* fix(litellm): honor an explicit switch back to the default proxy URL

Eliding the prefilled default was correct only when nothing was being replaced.
With an existing remote proxy configured, choosing http://localhost:4000 was
discarded, leaving requests pointed at the old proxy with no visible outcome.

Elide the default only when the provider row has no URL to replace, and prove
prompt rejection by cancelling mid-prompt so a blocked URL cannot reach config.

* fix(litellm): hint the default proxy URL instead of prefilling it

Driving the shipped wizard over a pty showed the prompt pre-fills its
initialValue, so a typed URL appended to it and failed validation as
"http://localhost:4000https://...". Hint the default as a placeholder and
prefill only when an existing URL is there to edit.

* fix(litellm): keep authored settings from a case-variant provider row

applyLitellmBaseUrl read providers.litellm by exact key. A config using
models.providers.LiteLLM therefore missed its row, and the fresh lowercase row
written here took precedence, dropping the operator's authored model
definitions, apiKey, and request options from the effective configuration.
Resolve the row through the normalized lookup the shared preset already uses.

## What Problem This Solves

Routine diagnostic instrumentation builds state and performs message/tool-schema work with no product consumer. The chat pane keeps a separate timing buffer that is only written; the Debug page reads the Gateway event log instead. Agent preparation also recounts compaction messages and serializes tool definitions solely for routine debug summaries.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior, configuration, protocol, or SDK change. Routine successful operations no longer produce the retired trace summaries; operator failures, lifecycle events, and documented slow-stage diagnostics remain available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the pane-local timing buffer, correlation map, timing-only paint callback, hydration timing events, and their mechanism-only tests. Keep the real after-paint hydration scheduler, send/progress/request clocks, queue state, recovery, and Gateway timing protocol unchanged.

Remove CLI argv/environment/session trace formatting, Decision tool-surface measurement and its first-primary-request observer, compaction debug recounts, the now-orphaned provider routing log formatter, and routine prompt/run/memory-preflight success traces. Authentication/environment policy, Decision pruning, compaction execution, failure logs, OTel IDs/events, and documented slow-stage warnings stay with their existing owners. No config, protocol, SDK, persistence, dependency, or release change.

Net production removal: **868 lines** (+4/-872 against the branch base, excluding tests, fixtures, test support, generated files, and declarations). Test reductions only remove assertions for retired instrumentation; retained behavior coverage stays.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- Pane timing history and cross-ACK diagnostic correlation disappear rather than retaining a bounded map for an unread buffer. The latest bound fix [#171146](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171146) describes diagnostic metadata, not an activation/foundation. Actual outbox/progress clocks and Gateway timing fields remain; slow startup remains diagnosed by the Gateway.
- CLI per-invocation argv, auth-key-name inventories, and hashed resume summaries are no longer logged. The extracted owner came through [#166711](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/166711); its real auth/environment operations remain unchanged. Operators retain failures and existing content-free process outcome metadata.
- Decision debug schema-size counters and the first-request observation callback disappear. [#153340](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/153340) used the counters for experiment verification; the feature is implemented and its permission/pruning/restoration tests remain. No model quality, token-cost, or performance claim depends on these normalized-character counters.
- Compaction no longer walks/re-estimates all messages before and after work just to print debug deltas/top contributors. The extracted diagnostics owner came through [#167325](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167325); real conversation detection, model-call IDs, hooks, failures, fallback warnings, and usage accounting stay. No recovery or durability guard is removed.
- Routine successful prompt/run lifecycle and memory preflight traces are quiet. Canonical lifecycle events, failure logs, slow-stage warnings, and actual policy decisions stay. No security, live-authority, concurrency, or data-integrity guard is removed.

perf(gateway): verify reconnect device tokens from committed pairing state (#173723)

After device lookups moved to the process-owned pairing publication (#173415), device token verification became the slow connect step under load: each reconnect verified and stamped lastUsedAt inside a device-pairing write transaction, so a Team burst showed deviceTokensMs 1.1-2.5 s. Valid-token reconnects now verify against the committed pairing publication (same publication and invalidation as device lookups, database fallback when incomplete), and last-use bookkeeping runs afterwards, re-verifying that the current token still authorizes before recording use. The verification policy moved unchanged into a shared module (revocation, token match, issuer generation, legacy browser tokens, approved scope baseline); issuance and rotation keep their guarded write path.

Seven interleaved AWS pairs per auth mode, 4,200/4,200 reconnects kept their tokens: token phase p90 2,573 -> 0.07 ms (shared auth) and 2,651 -> 0.06 ms (device-token auth); attach p90 2,575 -> 0.98 ms and 2,652 -> 0.92 ms. Runtime +141 LOC. Exact-head CI green.

fix(macos): detach leaked Peekaboo snapshot image after failed attach (#172903)

On a busy host, hdiutil attach can fail with EAGAIN after creating the
snapshot image's devices but before mounting them. Cleanup only detached
by mountpoint, found nothing mounted, and deleted the image while its
devices stayed attached. The standalone cleanup operation also never set
the image path.

When the mountpoint detach fails, cleanup now detaches any attachment of
the snapshot image by its whole-disk device (matched in hdiutil info by
resolved image path, never -force) and fails closed, retaining files and
printing the hdiutil detach command, if it stays attached. Attach retries
EAGAIN up to three attempts, detaching leftovers between attempts.

Release note: macOS packaging no longer leaks the Peekaboo snapshot disk
image when attach fails transiently on a busy host.

perf(state): reuse committed receipts and current plugin contracts (#173732)

## What Problem This Solves

Background image mutations reread the image metadata and preference immediately after committing them. Workboard similarly reloads a complete card before dependency promotion after link/reclaim writes have already returned that card. Return or reuse the owner's committed values instead.

Beam and MSTeams use the current host's V2 keyed-store contract directly, removing runtime probes for atomic methods and tests for unsupported older hosts. Their CAS retries and publisher authorization remain.

## Removed checks and accepted edges

| Removed work | Accepted edge / retained boundary |
| --- | --- |
| Background post-write metadata and preference reads | The response describes this mutation's state; a later edit is visible on the next read. Profile ownership, expected-value conflict checks, quotas and commit authority remain. |
| Workboard post-link card reload | An unsupported independent writer can produce a visible CAS conflict instead of being incorporated by the reload. Parent-state checks and final CAS remain. |
| Workboard post-reclaim card reload | Same boundary; promotion uses the committed claim-free card. Initial reads at claim/start/dispatch entry points remain. |
| Beam atomic-method capability probe | Bundled plugins require the current host; older-host method absence is unsupported. Publisher authorization and CAS remain. |
| MSTeams atomic-method capability probe | Bundled plugins require the current host; older-host method absence is unsupported. CAS preserves concurrent learnings. |

No schema, retention, SDK surface, or worker-routing changes. Image payloads stay out of metadata reads.

## SQL and main-thread impact

Pending measured results. Source-derived savings are two SELECTs per background mutation and thirteen SELECTs plus one worker request per Workboard link/reclaim. These are operation savings, not warmed-turn savings. The touched owners have zero T1 calls before and after.

The shared harness v3 comparison covers three alternating base/candidate pairs, including first turn, warmed turns and restart. No latency claim is made from a loaded host.

## Evidence

Both Codex review rounds completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings. Changed-file formatting, core type-aware lint, plugin lint and `git diff --check` passed. The initial default lint wrapper timed out generating unrelated SDK declarations; the source-backed core configuration passed.

CI passed the changed background (17), Workboard store (87), Beam store (6), Beam receiver/integration (10), Beam retry (4), and MSTeams feedback (5) tests. Production/test typechecks, core/extension lint, source/export contracts, Madge (zero cycles), and the T1/dialect ratchets passed. CI exposed a touched closed mock factory; it now preserves real exports, and its obsolete baseline entry was removed using the shrink-only generator. The owner inventory confirms T1 0 → 0. The local MSTeams regression also passed all five tests. Knip was run on both current main `1b650393cea` and merged head `18d3395bc98`: identical inherited findings, no candidate-only findings. Three alternating shared-harness pairs will be published after landing under the campaign’s land-on-green rule. The initial baseline completed, but a concurrent host runtime upgrade broke the candidate restart before application code loaded; the six valid runs will use one pinned working runtime. This host failure is excluded from the comparison. No update/Doctor/migration/plugin-loading/service-lifecycle or SDK surface changed, so the update cell and SDK API diff do not apply.

LOC against the base: production +25/−16 (net +9), tests/support +71/−72 (net −1), docs +4. The production growth is the explicit background receipt replacing a database read; the plugin changes reduce code.

## Audit finding retained

The plugin journal's existence-before-write probe cannot be replaced with a simple insert-if-absent without changing supported shared cursor/journal namespace retention behavior. At capacity one, insertion order can determine whether the journal entry or cursor survives. That path is unchanged.

## Follow-ups from the final census

Outside this reviewed change: initialize known-empty retention facts after `pluginState.replace` clears its namespace (source-derived one SELECT saving per nonempty replacement); remove SMS and memory-wiki older-host probes; remove the cron receipt filter duplicating its SQL predicate. These have not been implemented or measured.

Further source-only candidates: reuse transaction-local snapshots in restart-sentinel writes (one or two SELECTs; needs update-cell proof); use conditional writes/RETURNING for local-workspace create/update (one SELECT each); remove worker-environment create readback using its known-empty ports; pass already-validated background facts into the generic preference writer. None is included or claimed as a measured saving here.

## Inherited static findings

`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mts` reports the same eight production unused exports on main and candidate: `mergeReplyDirectiveResults`, `countActiveDescendantRunsFromRuns`, `countPendingDescendantRunsFromRuns`, `attachWaitingStatusProgressContinuation`, `sanitizeAssistantFinalAnswerText`, `createActivatedProjector`, `renderLegacyTemplate`, and `SolidContentPresentation`. The full-tree scan reports the same three on both: `mergeReplyDirectiveResults`, `attachWaitingStatusProgressContinuation`, and `createActivatedProjector`. Script export scans pass. All affected files are untouched by this PR. Main integration preserved the reviewed patch exactly (identical stable patch ID).
