fix(gateway): retarget an admission that reserved the rotated-away route

_admit_native reserves the route in one tracked write and commits the
admission in a later ordered one. A delivery that reserved the old route
before the exhaustion reset, then committed after the re-home, landed on
the abandoned old session: a retry of a moved message got a second
admission id there and a new message stayed stranded.

The reset records old owner -> session key (rotated_owners);
_admit_native_write, inside the ordered commit, retargets such a
reservation at the key's current live route, so a retry dedupes onto the
moved row and a new message queues behind it. Publication and scheduling
follow the committed row's target instead of the stale reservation.

fix(gateway): fence the fresh FIFO for the whole exhaustion reset

Delaying our own schedule call was not enough: a native redelivery
(_schedule_admitted) or a migrated loop wake (move_route_wakes) still
started the fresh session's drain while the reset was evicting the agent,
clearing scope and syncing the Telegram topic binding. The early turn then
resolved back onto the exhausted session through the binding-heal path and
the next message stayed queued under admission_conflict.

reset_and_rehome_messages now takes the fresh session's claim_gate (the
lock every FIFO claim already waits on) in the same task step as the
rotation commit, before any later ordered admission can schedule, and
returns release(); the reset runs its cleanup in try/finally and calls
release() once at the end, which lifts the gate and schedules the FIFO.
A cancelled reset lifts it when the write completes.

Docstring now states the real guarantee: rotation (sessions.json) and
re-home (one SQLite transaction) are ordered with admissions, not atomic
across the two stores.

fix(gateway): order the exhaustion re-home with redeliveries and cleanup

The compression-exhaustion reset rotated the route, then moved the queued
messaging rows in a second write. A transport redelivery of a queued
message in that gap resolved to the fresh session and inserted a second
row there; the move then hit UNIQUE(principal_id, target_session_id,
request_id) and rolled back, stranding every queued message. The route
rotation and the move are now one ordered tracked_write, so an admission
that resolves to the fresh session commits after the move and dedupes
onto the moved row.

The move also scheduled the fresh session's drain itself, before the
caller evicted the cached agent, cleared the conversation scope and
re-synced the Telegram topic binding, so a moved message could start a
turn on stale state (or follow the stale binding back to the exhausted
session). reset_and_rehome_messages now returns the scheduling step and
the caller runs it after that cleanup.

Test: a redelivery racing the reset dedupes and B, C run once in order;
the drain is scheduled after clear + binding sync. Red on 517cce275e1
(IntegrityError UNIQUE / schedule before clear), green here.

fix(gateway): run messages queued behind an exhausted context on the fresh session

When a native messaging turn exhausted its context, the auto-reset rotated
the route to a new standalone session but left the messages already queued
behind that turn (B, C) on the old owner. The old drain then refused them
(admission_conflict) and paused, so they never ran, while a message
admitted after the reset (D) ran on the new session ahead of them.

The reset now re-homes the old owner's still-queued messaging:* admissions
onto the fresh session in one SQLite transaction (rehome_queued_inputs):
each row keeps its admission id, request id and seq, so FIFO order holds
and a transport retry of a moved message still dedupes. The reset and the
re-home run under the old owner's mutation_lock, and the write is ordered
with native admissions. The exhausted turn is started, so it is never moved
or replayed. Reset semantics are unchanged (new standalone session, no
lineage edge); /new and /stop still cancel queued messages.

Salvage of #139673 by @helix4u (smaller redo: re-home the queued admissions
instead of modelling the reset as compression lineage). Headline test
adapted from theirs.

fix(security): hold the plugin gate on websockets and for every served profile

The runtime gate on /api/plugins/<name>/ stopped short in several ways.

- PLG-8: _plugin_api_runtime_gate is HTTP middleware, so a plugin disabled
  while the server ran kept accepting new websocket connections until
  restart. A pure ASGI gate now applies the same rule to upgrades. It closes
  before accept, ahead of the route's own credential check (that check is
  the disabled plugin's code, and a gated-mode ticket is single-use); on the
  wire that is the same 403 handshake an unknown route or a refused
  credential gets, so it is no plugin-name oracle.
- PLG-9: under a secondary profile's native ticket the gate read only that
  profile's plugin lists. Dashboard discovery scans only the launch home and
  the root, so every copy this server imports, hands to a plugin host or
  serves files from is the launch profile's. A plugin the launch profile
  disabled stayed reachable for the secondary profile (routes and assets),
  and that profile's first request for a plugin only it enabled hot-mounted
  the launch copy in its scope: imported here, or, under its own
  plugins.isolation: host, run by its plugin host with its secrets
  (GHSA-mcfc-hp25-cjv7). The hot mount also took plugins.isolation from the
  requesting profile, so an in-process secondary imported a plugin the
  launch profile runs in a host.
- A session-token request with ?profile= ran a plugin in the selected
  profile's scope even when that profile had disabled it.

One rule now holds for HTTP, websocket upgrades, assets, the dashboard
plugin list (no tab whose script and API refuse) and the hot mount:
a plugin is served only while the launch profile, whose copy it is, has it
enabled and so does the profile the request acts for (a native ticket's
profile, a ?profile= selection once its scope is bound, else the launch
profile). Mount decisions, hot mounts included, are the launch profile's
alone, its isolation mode included. The gates read the enable lists once
per profile scope from the cached read-only config.

fix(desktop): stamp group log entries strictly after the tail

Group room watermarks are log INDICES, but the gateway mirror merge
(mergeRemoteGroupChatSnapshotIntoRooms, run on every sync read-back)
re-sorts the local log by `at` and breaks ties by entry id, a random
UUID. Two appends in the same millisecond (or after a clock step
back) therefore came back in random order under unchanged watermarks:

- a user follow-up sorted ahead of an already-seen row slips under
  the member's watermark and is never delivered ("got 1 call"), or
- the member's own reply / the earlier ask moves past the watermark
  and is fed back as news, re-driving the member ("got 3 calls").

appendGroupChatEntry now stamps `at = max(now, tail.at + 1)`, so log
order is also time order and the merge sort is a no-op on local rows.
mirrorExternalGroupWrites already did this for its own bursts.

This is the CI flake in group-activity.test.ts 'queues follow-ups
without cancelling the active turn or losing its reply delta'
(expected 2 prompt.submit calls, got 3): a loaded runner put the
appends in one millisecond. The test now pins Date.now and hands out
descending UUIDs, which makes the reorder happen on every run: red
6/6 against the old group-chat.ts, green 6/6 with the fix.

fix(gateway): identify a Windows pipe peer by its token, not its PID

The native control pipe identified a client by GetNamedPipeClientProcessId +
OpenProcess on that PID. A one-shot `hermes gateway ensure` child (Desktop's
boot-time auto-start) can exit before the server gets to it; OpenProcess then
fails and a same-user client is refused as "belongs to another user", which the
caller folds into authorization/inaccessible.

The peer's identity now comes from the token the kernel captured when the
client opened the pipe: the client dials with SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT |
SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION (the server may read the token, never act as the
client), and the server reads the request line first (ImpersonateNamedPipeClient
needs data read from the pipe), then impersonates, OpenThreadToken(OpenAsSelf),
RevertToSelf, and compares the TokenUser SID with its own. That token survives
the client's exit. A RevertToSelf failure stops the worker instead of serving on
with a borrowed identity. Older clients that dial anonymously still go through
the PID path. A peer that can't be identified either way stays refused.

The draft in #139105 does the opposite: it serves an unreadable peer as
`sid:unresolved` and relies on the pipe DACL alone. This change keeps the
identity check and gets the identity from somewhere that still exists.

Windows-only tests (platforms("windows")): a client process whose PID the
server can't open is served with the owner's SID; a peer with neither a token
nor a readable process is refused. Not run natively here; needs a Windows
retest.

fix(gateway): keep a stale Bot pin whose Bot Chat was deleted

A session delete moves its admission rows to retired receipts keyed by the
route principal (automation:<route>), which the pin never recorded, so the
owner scan read a committed pin on a deleted Bot Chat as "never admitted",
withdrew it, and a same-id resend ran the message a second time. A pin whose
target is retired now counts as possibly committed and stays the explicit
unknown record, as on main.

refactor(gateway): make the owner scan's requeue and withdraw explicit branches

The age, home and admission checks stay apart from the action: requeue_pin or withdraw_pin runs in its own branch and a requeued ticket is appended to the scan's records there, which removes the _requeue helper. No behaviour change. Review feedback from Greptile.

fix(gateway): keep legacy Bot tickets FIFO behind an unresolved pre-admission pin

A legacy ticket whose _migrate admission got an owner-state refusal stays a
pre-admission pin until the owner scan requeues it past the grace window. A
recovery or delivery inside that window skipped the pin and admitted the
tickets queued after it, so the requeued ticket ran out of order (B, A).

_scan_owner_receipts now also returns the lowest _legacy_order of a legacy pin
of this home that is still unresolved (inside grace, or its requeue lost to a
concurrent change), taken from the same scan. _migrate, which both owner
recovery and delivery go through, admits only legacy tickets ordered before
it. A pin whose admission committed, or one without owner, is no barrier.
The barrier lasts one scan: past grace the pin is requeued and released, and
a failed requeue is re-read by the next scan. An owner-state refusal mid-pass
already raises out of _migrate, so later tickets never ran in that pass; the
new test pins that down.

Refs #139138

fix(gateway): requeue a stale legacy Bot pin instead of deleting its message

A pre-admission pin `_admit` lays over a legacy mailbox ticket (`legacy=`)
is the only copy of that queued, never-run message. The owner scan withdrew
any stale pin with no committed `bot:<key>` admission, so a transient
refusal on the legacy migration path dropped queued work.

The scan now restores such a pin (it carries the ticket's `owner`) to the
queued legacy ticket under the mailbox lock, only while it is still that
unadmitted pin, stripping only the fields the pin added and keeping id,
message, sequence and created_at. `_migrate` then admits it once under the
same delivery id in its FIFO place. Non-legacy stale pins are still
withdrawn; a pin whose admission committed is never touched.

Fixes #139138
Refs #134889 (MSG-9)
Refs #139162

fix(gateway): withdraw stale Bot receipt pins whose admission never committed

A pre-admission `ambiguous` pin stays on disk when its admission was
refused by a build older than the terminal-refusal change, when a
process died between pin and commit, or when `_migrate` hit an
owner-state refusal on a legacy ticket (`legacy=` keeps the pin). Every
owner scan then logged it as a malformed receipt, and a same-id resend
answered `unknown_execution` forever.

The owner's scan (`recover_bot_deliveries` and `_migrate`, both under
the mailbox lock `_admit` holds) now collects these pins and withdraws
one with the existing `withdraw_pin` when it is older than
`_PIN_GRACE_SECONDS` (300 s) and no admission row exists for its
`bot:<key>` (`_admission_at`, the lookup `_admit` already uses). It logs
one INFO line per pin (key, age), no message content. A pin whose
admission committed, a pin inside the grace window or one for another
profile home keeps its warning and is never rewritten. The bare
`scan_receipts` without an authority only reads, as before.

fix(cli): retry the schema probe on a transient disk I/O error

PRAGMA table_info ran on the raw connection, so one disk I/O error
made bare -c return no session and /sessions return an empty list.
The session SELECT already replays that blip through
_read_retrying_ioerr. The probe now uses that same read. A positive
answer is still the only cached result. An error that survives the
retry budget still propagates and is not stored, and an absent column
is still re-probed.

fix(cli): do not cache a failed or negative schema probe

A PRAGMA table_info error was stored as "created_source is missing". The
reader then matched source only, so a newer local CLI row disappeared, and
the in-chat reader kept that answer after the lock cleared. A successful
"column absent" answer was sticky the same way: after another connection
added the column, /sessions still omitted the new local row.

Only a successful positive probe is cached. A lock or I/O error propagates
and is not stored. An absent answer is re-checked on the next lookup, which
stays a read.

fix(cli): skip created_source on read-only pre-column stores

Bare hermes -c, --resume latest, and in-chat /sessions open state.db
read-only, so they never run the migration that adds sessions.created_source.
The surface predicate named that column anyway. SQLite raised
"no such column: s.created_source", the caller swallowed it, and -c exited
as if no CLI session existed. hermes sessions list is the same read-only
open, so the recovery hint does not heal the file.

When PRAGMA table_info shows the column is absent, match the requested
source labels only — the previous filter's result when the key was missing.
A store that has the column still pages local rows by created_source, and
created_source=unknown stays excluded.

fix(cli): page CLI sessions by creating surface before the limit

hermes -c, /sessions and /resume read gateway rows labelled source=local
through SurfaceLabelReader. That reader fetched a fixed window of every
local row, (limit+offset)*3+50, and only then kept rows whose
created_source matched the requested surface. Sixty newer Desktop or TUI
sessions filled the bare -c window (limit 1 fetches 53 rows) and two
hundred filled the /sessions window (the listing asks for 40 rows, which
fetches 170), so the classic CLI session dropped out of the page.
hermes sessions list never used that reader.

The source predicate now matches non-local rows for the requested source
and local rows only when created_source is one of the requested surfaces,
and that predicate is applied in SQL before LIMIT/OFFSET. A partial index
on local rows (created_source, started_at) lets the local branch seek one
surface instead of walking every Desktop and TUI row.

#138838 and #139058 repair a created_source=unknown placeholder on upsert.
This change does not treat unknown as a CLI session; once those fixes
stamp the real creator, the same predicate finds the row.

fix(gateway): keep a Bot delivery refused for owner state resendable

A Bot Chat admission refused with nothing committed became a terminal
"refused" receipt for every reason except queue_full. That included
refusals about the owner rather than the delivery: runtime_draining
while the gateway drains for a restart or update, storage_unavailable,
stale_epoch. The same-id resend then answered the stored refusal with
no admission, so cron/bot_chat_legacy marked a report sent during a
restart as transferred and the sender saw agent_blocked.

Classify the refusal with one named set (_OWNER_STATE_REFUSALS):
owner-state refusals withdraw the pin like queue_full, so the resend
admits once; refusals about the delivery (permission_denied,
invalid_params, admission_conflict, ...) keep the terminal receipt. A
refusal raised after the admission row committed still leaves the
unknown pin.

fix(gateway): keep a local Bot delivery's operator access on its one retry

A peer-minted Bot Chat is owned by `api-peer`. A local operator's
bot_relay.deliver into it is admitted through `session:operator` (granted only
by the verified interactive transport), and its receipt stores the operator's
principal_id. After a transient provider failure, _maybe_retry() rebuilt that
principal with only session:submit/session:read, so _target() refused the
retry with permission_denied and the promised one retry never ran.

Shape chosen: the receipt records `operator: true` only when the admitting
actor actually held session:operator (AuthorityConnection strips any claimed
operator capability unless the transport grants it). The retry adds
session:operator back only when that flag is set, and the existing check that
the resolved target is the receipt's admitted session still pins the retry to
the same chat, so nothing is widened. Receipts written without the flag (older
receipts, non-operator senders) retry exactly as before. The api-peer
ownership decision is unchanged, and the retry still reuses the derived
admission identity (`bot:<id>:retry`) and the committed payload.

fix(gateway): declare a refused Bot delivery's receipt in the deliver contract

A same-id resend of a delivery the FIFO refused (nothing committed) answers
its terminal refused receipt, which has no admission. CanonicalBotDeliverResult
required admission_id, so through AuthorityConnection.dispatch the answer was a
ContractViolation under test isolation, and in production Desktop's
settleRelayDelivery() treated it as "identity unavailable" and kept the
envelope retained: the refusal never reached the sender.

The contract now declares the refused shape explicitly: admission_id is
optional and `refused: true` marks the receipt, with a validator that a result
either names its admission or is a refused `failed` receipt without one. The
resend carries `refused`; the generated TS/OpenRPC are regenerated with
scripts/gen_gateway_contracts.py. The relay settles a refused failed receipt
for its envelope as the sender's terminal answer (posted back, no longer
retained); an answer with neither an admission nor a refusal is still retained.

The first refusal is unchanged: a JSON-RPC 4001 refusal whose data.reason the
relay already forwards.

fix(gateway): mint a headless peer DM's Bot Chat through its owner

`hermes peer dm` creates the remote canonical "Bot Chat" through
`POST /api/sessions` when it is missing. On a headless gateway (no
Desktop/CLI ever made one) that create minted a plain API row. A remote
sender never binds unowned history, so the authority FIFO door
(`admit_peer_turn` -> `session_bot.deliver` -> `resolve_local_target`)
answered every DM 502 "Bot Chat admission refused: not_found".

Under session authority a titled "Bot Chat" create now goes through the
owner's own creation step, the one a first `bot_relay.deliver` already
takes (`session_bot._create_bot_chat`: titled-create lock, commits off the
owner loop). The chat is then a LOCAL session its FIFO owns and the DM is
that chat's own admission. This adds no second creation route and no API
turn. An explicit id, another title, or an existing Bot Chat keeps the
ordinary handler and its answers.

A peer-created API "Bot Chat" left over from before is refused by name
(`bot_chat_not_local`, or `bot_chat_unbound` for unbound legacy local
history) with a remedy, never a bare not_found. The full clause goes to
gateway.log. An existing API-created "Bot Chat" row is not repaired:
it still gets the named bot_chat_not_local refusal and must be renamed
or deleted.

fix(gateway): admit an upstream-authorized adapter's fresh native inputs

The unified gateway's durable admission derives allow_adapter_delegation

authorization model IS the upstream (A2A peers: bearer-token authenticated

fix(gateway): settle a definitely refused Bot delivery as a terminal receipt

_admit pins the receipt (status ambiguous, no admission_id) before
admitting. Only queue_full withdrew that pin; every other refusal
(permission_denied and friends) left it behind for good, so each bulk
mailbox scan warned about it as a malformed receipt and a same-id
redelivery answered unknown_execution forever.

When the admission raises and no row exists at the delivery's FIFO
identity, the pin now becomes a terminal failed receipt (refused, typed
reason agent_blocked, content-free error; the refusal clause goes to
gateway.log only). The scan validates that shape, recovery and legacy
migration never re-send it, and a same-id redelivery answers it. A pin
without that proof (a refusal raised after the row committed, a crash
in the two-store window) is unchanged and still warns.

fix(discord): re-authorize durable role grants through the ingress gate resolver

The durable re-authorization read DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES from the scoped
env or the raw top-level `discord:` block only, so a profile that sets
its role allowlist under `platforms.discord` (flat or `extra`) admitted a
role-authorized member at ingress and then dropped the message with
permission_denied.

Recovery now resolves the gate with the same `_gate_raw` ingress uses,
applied to the Discord PlatformConfig that `load_gateway_config()` builds
for the transport profile at check time: scoped env first, then `extra`
with the loader's precedence (`platforms.discord.extra` over the flat
key and the top-level block). Reading current config instead of the
connect-time `self.config` keeps a config revocation effective.

fresh `__new__:<uuid>` draft key. The always-on background drain treated
that key as a stored session id, submitted it, and after the rejections
exhausted the retry budget classified the key as a gone session and
deleted the prompt, before the creation handoff could move it.

Skip fresh draft keys (isFreshDraftScope) in the drain loop. Those
entries wait for the announced handoff, which re-keys them onto the
stored id where the drain handles them normally. Stored-key drain
behaviour is unchanged.

Refs #139161

fix(desktop): re-scope the composer queue when a runtime is claimed

composerQueueScopeKey asks storedSessionIdForRuntimeId whether the
runtime id is claimed, which reads $sessionTiles, $sessionStates,
$activeSessionId and $selectedStoredSessionId through .get(). ChatBar
only re-rendered on sessionId/route changes, so a claim that lands while
both stay put (the first send's session.create publishes the runtime
before its mirror) left the scope on the runtime key until something
else re-rendered.

ChatBar now resolves the scope through useComposerQueueScopeKey, a
useStoresSelector over exactly those stores. The selector returns the
scope string, so the hot $sessionStates churn does not re-render the
composer unless the scope itself changes.

fix(desktop): hand a create-window follow-up to the new chat

A follow-up queued while the first send's session.create is in flight
lands under the chat's fresh draft key. The queue re-key correctly
refuses fresh -> stored moves (#139190), so nothing handed the entry to
the new chat: it sat under a key no composer reads until the next
rotateFreshDraftKey() orphaned it.

Move it at the same announced handoff that already moves the draft
text: when the composer consumes the creation announcement for its
stored id, migrate the queue from that composer's own fresh key
(migrateQueuedPrompts dedupes by id). adoptNewSessionDraft now reports
whether the announcement matched, so the queue moves even with no draft
text. A routed session's queue never moves.

perf(desktop): track a pending submission without scanning the journal

Each send tracked its admission by reading the whole receipt journal (every
session's v2 keys, parsed) twice on the renderer thread. Read the one
admission by its entry key with the legacy-blob fallback, keeping the merge
(stronger status, text/displayText, later fence, retired stays retired).
Tip->root journal adoption, which does enumerate, now runs from tracking only
the first time a lineage is observed; reconciliation still adopts on every
snapshot.

creation follow the chat onto its stored id, a follow-up queued during the
first turn lands on and drains into the new chat, and session A's queued
entry is neither moved nor submitted. Fails on the previous resolver (the

fix(desktop): one pending-receipt journal for tracking and reconciliation

Reconciliation projected snapshots onto the lineage root, but submit still
tracked receipts under the stored id it targeted (possibly the compression
tip), and a tip journal written before the tip->root row loaded was never
read again. The receipt and its snapshots could land in different journals
(stronger started/unknown status and displayText lost), and a delayed older
empty snapshot could hide a card whose sequence fence stayed under the tip.

Tracking and reconciliation now share one identity (the key the queue panel
reads). When a key starts resolving elsewhere, its journal is folded into the
resolved one: per admission the stronger status wins, text and displayText
are kept from either record, and the later fence of one numbering survives.
Projection only: no retry, no local queue, no local delete of server rows.

fix(desktop): scope the composer queue panel to the session it renders

A new chat showed the queue of the session just left. On a new-chat route
the composer fell back to the runtime id, which still names the previous
session for a frame after the switch, and the runtime re-key effect then
could migrate that session's queue onto the fresh draft key. The runtime
id now stands in only while no stored session claims it, and the re-key
migrates only between two runtime-derived keys.

Server queue rows were projected under the stored id the runtime reports
(the tip after compression) while the panel reads the lineage root, so
those rows reached the panel only through rotation migrations. Each
migration appended a fresh copy, and no later snapshot retired the copies
on the root: duplicate cards that Delete could not remove and that came
back. Pending snapshots now project onto the key the panel reads, and a
migration keeps one row per id.

fix(worker): close the owner connection when execute ends

WorkerRPC.close() had no production caller and RuntimeSessionStore.close() does not close the RPC, so the owner socket lived until process exit. execute() now closes it after store.close() in its finally, on success and on a start failure; a failing close is suppressed so it never replaces the turn result or the start-failure exit.

Refs #134889 (KB-3)
Refs #139162
Refs #139011

fix(worker): redial once when the owner closes an idle link before the send

An owner close landing after the idle check (reader.is_alive()) but before ws.send() made send itself raise ConnectionClosed, and the caller got an outcome-unknown error for a request that never left. websockets 15 raises ConnectionClosed from send only before a complete frame is written (closed on entry, or the socket write failed), so the call now drops the link, redials with a fresh ticket and sends once more. Any error after a successful send (reply wait, timeout, mid-flight close) still drops the link and propagates unchanged, never resent; a failing resend is not retried again.

Refs #134889 (KB-3)
Refs #139162
Refs #139011

fix(worker): resolve a key-less worker's primary failure against this turn's fallback chain

worker_api_key() walked only the frozen session snapshot's fallbacks on a
primary AuthError. For an ordinary session the owner sends the refreshed
profile chain in construct_v1, so an expired primary (e.g. a lapsed nous
login) with a fallback added after session creation now failed to start,
where the key-less agent used to reach that fallback at init.

Walk the chain the agent will actually get: construct_v1's when the owner
sent one, the frozen snapshot's otherwise (older owner). A resolved fallback
still yields api_key=None, so its key is never paired with the primary
endpoint; when no entry resolves the primary AuthError is re-raised and the
Kanban start exit (75/78) is unchanged.

Refs #134889 (KB-5)
Refs #139162
Refs #139155

test(worker): wait for the observed idle close, not the clock

Code-health follow-up to the owner-connection reader: the reconnect test
waits for the reader thread to exit instead of sleeping; the reader's
catch-all (handed to the calling thread, which raises it) and the flood
fixture's 5 ms spacing (separate broadcasts are the behaviour under test)
carry reviewed health waivers.

Refs #134889 (KB-3)
Refs #139162
Refs #139011

test(gateway): cover a key-less worker's credential failure and fallback boundary

The existing Kanban exit tests call record_start_failure directly, and the
fallback test only showed the constructor receiving api_key=None. Add:

- an AuthError raised by the key-less worker's own route resolution goes
  through execute -> _construct_agent -> record_start_failure and books 75
  (quota wall) / 78 (re-login) on a bound claim; the agent is never built.
- when resolution lands on a configured fallback, the real AIAgent builds
  its primary (MiniMax, Anthropic protocol) client without the fallback
  provider's key, asserted at build_anthropic_client with fake keys. A turn
  through the fallback is not driven.

Both fail when the fix is mutated: resolving outside the start-failure
handler books 1, and returning a fallback entry's key builds the primary
client with it.

Refs #134889 (KB-5)
Refs #139162
Refs #139155

fix(worker): read the owner connection continuously and drop the library keepalive

The retained owner WebSocket was only read during a call. The owner
registers every worker connection as a live transport and broadcasts
sessions.changed to it, so a worker busy in a model call or tool piled up
more than websockets' 16-frame receive high-water mark, the library paused
socket reads, and pings and the close handshake stalled with them. The
next persistence call was then sent into a connection the owner was
already closing and failed with an unknown outcome, which the store
latches. Separately, the default 20 s client keepalive ran its own pong
deadline, so a short owner stall could close the connection inside a
call's 20 s receipt budget.

A reader thread now owns the socket for its lifetime: it discards pushed
events as they arrive and hands the reply for the one outstanding request
id (or the close exception) to the waiting caller. ping_interval=None
leaves the per-call receipt budget and the observed close as the only
liveness checks. Buffering stays bounded (library queue, at most one reply
plus a close in the hand-off queue); calls stay serialized under the lock
with per-request ids; an idle close observed before a send still redials
with a fresh ticket; any error after a send drops the connection and
propagates without a resend. Server checks still run per request.

Alternatives not taken: stopping broadcasts to worker connections would
need a new transport rule in the owner (it does not tell worker
connections apart today) and still leaves the client keepalive; an idle
timeout would add a redial per quiet stretch and still pause reads inside
the window.

Refs #134889 (KB-3)
Refs #139162
Refs #139011

fix(worker): reuse one owner connection per managed worker

WorkerRPC dialed a fresh WebSocket for every persistence call: a new
discovery, identify, single-use worker-adoption ticket and WS accept on
the owner loop each time, so a busy worker multiplied every owner stall
into owner_unavailable failures.

Keep one authenticated connection per WorkerRPC. It is discovered,
identified (self-RPC guard) and ticketed on connect exactly as each
call was; requests stay serialized by the existing lock and are now
correlated by an increasing id. Events the owner broadcast between
calls are drained before a send, which also surfaces a close the owner
sent while idle, so that case redials before anything is written. Any
error once a request may have been sent drops the connection and
propagates unchanged (ConnectionClosed / worker_receipt_timeout); it is
never resent, so the store latches it and its journal replays the
same sequence as before. No server or protocol change.

Refs #134889 (KB-3)
Refs #139162
Refs #139011

fix(agent): name the caller when the worker RPC guard fires on a loop

A managed worker that reaches the synchronous persistence RPC on a thread
with a running event loop gets WorkerPersistenceError
('synchronous_rpc_on_event_loop'), which the store keeps as a sticky
failure. When a best-effort writer (aux usage, the tools pin) swallows
that first raise at debug, the logs only show the later sticky failures
(append_message, flush_token_counts, turn.cleanup) and never the code
that tripped the guard.

The guard stays as it is. Before it raises, it now logs a WARNING with
the RPC method, the thread name and a module:function:line summary of the
frames above the store. The store's own frames are left out, and no
locals or argument values are logged.

A static pass over the worker's loop owners did not confirm a trigger,
so this commit only adds the diagnostic. Checked: async tool handlers via
_run_async, async aux calls (accounting is already off-loop), MCP
sampling and list_changed, the periodic lease/liveness scheduler, the
process registry, deadline helpers and smart approvals.

Refs #139029
Refs #134889 (KB-2)
Refs #139162

fix(gateway): resolve a key-less managed worker's route credential like the in-process turn

A managed worker launched without a launch key (every Kanban run) handed AIAgent
api_key=None. On the anthropic_messages wire only native Anthropic recovers a
missing key, so a custom provider (MiniMax and other Anthropic-protocol hosts)
sent `Authorization: Bearer ` and died as a transient APIConnectionError.

Move the policy-route resolution out of _resolve_policy_agent_runtime into
session_worker_construct.route_runtime and call it from both the in-process
turn and the worker's agent construction. The worker resolves inside its own
profile environment (the owner's _worker_env), so it never reads another
profile's key, and a key from a fallback entry is never paired with the
primary provider. A bound launch key still wins. Resolution errors stay inside
_construct_agent, so Kanban start failures keep their exit mapping.

Refs #134889 (KB-5)
Refs #139162
Fixes #139155

Co-authored-by: liuhao1024 <liuhao1024@users.noreply.github.com>

fix(docker): end a hung s6 command at the runtime deadline

The s6 discovery returned before discover_existing_gateway_service's
exception mapping, and the s6 start branch did not map TimeoutExpired.
A hung s6-svstat or s6-svc (5 s timeout) therefore escaped
ensure_gateway_runtime as an uncaught subprocess.TimeoutExpired instead
of the starting/deadline receipt every other supervisor backend returns.

Route _s6 through the shared backend dispatch and map TimeoutExpired to
TimeoutError in the s6 start branch.

fix(docker): start gateway through s6 runtime service

fix(docker): isolate supervised logs from interactive terminals

fix(hooks): in-memory launch consent ends with the config entry; refused entries don't suspend removal

Re-review of #139067 (teknium1, unsupportedpastels): an unsaved launch approval is dropped when its
hook leaves config.yaml, so removing and re-adding asks again; a well-formed plugin-only event
under hooks: is refused but no longer suspends removal; hooks.md notes gateway run --accept-hooks
covers every served profile.

fix(hooks): drop resume accept_hooks; keep only unsaved launch consent; warn when removal is suspended

- TUI resume/activate no longer sends accept_hooks: CanonicalResumeParams forbids extra keys, so
  every resume under HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS would fail with invalid_params
- accept_for_launch holds only approvals the allowlist write lost, so a later revoke of a saved one
  takes effect; config parsed once
- one warning per home when a malformed hooks: entry or unreadable allowlist suspends removal
- hermes hooks list tolerates malformed allowlist records (allowlisted_pairs); revoke text names the
  opt-in exception; stale lock comment and save_allowlist warning corrected

fix(hooks): keep in-memory consent across re-syncs; never disarm on malformed input

Review of #139067 (teknium1, unsupportedpastels, greptile):
- a launch's --accept-hooks survives a failed allowlist write (accept_for_launch)
- gateway run --accept-hooks keeps approving hooks added after start
- config + allowlist are read under the same lock as the apply, so no stale snapshot lands last
- a malformed hooks: entry or allowlist record adds but never removes
- register_from_config never re-asks for an already-wired hook
- skipped hooks warn once per process; TUI --resume carries --accept-hooks

fix(cli): shell-hook consent and freshness under the one-gateway runtime (CLI-5)

Since #106742 every `hermes chat` turn runs in the gateway, which registered shell hooks once at
startup with no TTY. The classic CLI lost main's first-use "Allow this hook to run? [y/N]" prompt,
`--accept-hooks` was dropped on the full-parser chat path (only HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1 worked), and
hooks added, approved, removed or revoked after the gateway started never took effect until a
gateway restart.

- The classic CLI asks for consent on its own terminal before it opens its gateway session
  (skipped for a remote gateway and for --safe-mode / --ignore-user-config launches).
- `--accept-hooks` on chat exports HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS, which rides session.create.
- The gateway re-syncs the profile's hooks from its live config on every local session create /
  resume (new shell_hooks.sync_from_config): newly configured or approved hooks register, removed or
  revoked ones are unregistered, under one lock hold. Consent is the allowlist or an opt-in in
  force (hooks_auto_accept / HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS), as on main. It never prompts or writes, a
  re-sync failure never blocks opening the session, and an empty (failed-open) config or an
  unreadable allowlist adds but never removes, so a fail_closed guard is never disarmed by a
  half-saved file or a failed allowlist write.
- `--accept-hooks` on session.create records consent (record_consent_from_config); the resume that
  follows registers. register_from_config keeps its old add-only contract for every other caller.
- `hermes hooks revoke` text now says a running gateway drops the hook at the next session open.

Regression from 46a5a627 (teknium1, Oct 12; cherry-picked from 4dbd7426, merged with #106742),
which moved hook registration out of the classic CLI process.
Refs #134889 (CLI-5).

fix(compression): name the model that actually failed when every aux fallback is exhausted

The auxiliary fallback ladder writes each fallback candidate into route_info
before trying it. When every candidate fails, the ladder re-raises the PRIMARY
error, but route_info still named the last fallback. The compressor reads
route_info to decide which model failed, so an overloaded Codex primary with a
dead Nous fallback logged "Summary model 'openai/gpt-5.6-luna' was overloaded",
told the user to check auxiliary.compression.model (which they never set), and
re-sent the summary to the same overloaded primary as a "main-model retry".

Restore the primary route on exhaustion so the route matches the raised error.

fix(desktop): keep single-letter WSL dirs on the bridge, test drive aliases on every OS

The drive-alias rewrite (/c/..., /cygdrive/c/..., /mnt/c/...) now only
fires when the native C:/... target exists, so a real WSL root directory
with a one-letter name (/e/projects) still resolves through
\\wsl.localhost\<distro>\ instead of a nonexistent E: drive.

The mapping moves into shellDriveToNativePath with an injectable exists()
so its cases run in CI on every OS; the previous assertions only took the
new branch when process.platform was win32, which no PR lane runs.

Read the simulator settings from Simulator, not the subclass (#702)

coverage_dir, coverage_root and artifacts_dir are set on TrmnlSim::Simulator,
but were read through self.class: a subclass (TrmnlX::XSim, which every general
example on the TRMNL X uses) has its own, unset copies. So on the X those
examples wrote no per-run coverage, saved no artifacts on failure, and wrote
absolute source paths, failing coverage_spec's setup boot example.

Gave the X's portal waits the suite's usual 90 s (#701)

The TRMNL X takes 11 s of wall time to reach the portal on an idle machine, so
the 15 s and 30 s budgets on these waits failed whenever the simulator ran
slower; under parallel_rspec it ran at a fifth of that speed. Pinned to the
efficiency cores (taskpolicy -b), 2 of 3 examples timed out at 30 s and none at
90 s. The setup redirect's later steps time out the same way there, since the
setup screen's refresh is bound by the interpreter.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Moved the saved-network and X portal examples into their own files (#700)

* Moved the saved-network examples out of portal_spec.rb

parallel_rspec hands out whole files, so portal_spec.rb (83 s on the OG) set the
suite's wall time on its own. SavedNetworks is a separate concern (several saved
networks, not the portal pages) and takes 22 s of it, so it gets its own file and
another worker. Its scan check uses Simulator#portal_scan instead of a local copy.

parallel_rspec hands out whole files, and trmnl_x_spec.rb (445 s) set the
TRMNL_X run's wall time on its own. PortalTimeout, Onboarding and FailedJoin
are the setup portal's examples and need only the shipped fixture, so they get
their own file and another worker: a TRMNL_X run takes 4:54 instead of 7:35.

trmnl-sim's CI still runs the old trmnl-spec suite, every device in one job, and times out

fix(httpclient): Time out reading a body when the server goes silent (#12990)

* fix(httpclient): Time out reading a body when the server goes silent

writeToStreamDataBlock() waited for the rest of a body for as long as
connected() held. A server that stops sending part way through a body
without closing the connection leaves connected() true, so getString()
and writeToStream() never returned. Give up after _tcpTimeout without
data and return HTTPC_ERROR_READ_TIMEOUT, as handleHeaderResponse()
already does for the headers.

* fix(httpclient): Wait between empty reads of a TLS body

NetworkClientSecure::read() returns at once when no data has arrived,
so readBytes() returns 0 without waiting for its timeout, and the body
loop polled the socket without pause through every gap in a TLS body.
Wait 1 ms before retrying, as the loop already does when available()
is 0.

fix(tests): billing journey reads Renews for an active plan and tops up a current preset (#10096)

## Problem
v0.14.0 release suite run 38967530794 (attempt 3):
`10-billing-journey:149` passed checkout and the real Stripe
subscription (`account-state` returned `subscription.status: active`),
then failed `getByText('Active', { exact: true })`. The failure
screenshot of deployed staging shows the plan card reading **Credits ·
$100/mo · Renews Nov 16** with 15,050 credits: #10007 made
`current_period_end` real, so an active plan reads "Renews <date>". The
same screenshot shows the next step is stale too: top-up presets are $25
/ $100 / $250 / $1,000 / Custom (#9814), and the spec clicks `$10`.

## Change
- The active-plan check expects `/^Renews /`.
- The top-up step picks `$25`, clicks `Add $25`, and asserts `amount:
25` on `POST /v1/billing/purchase-credits`.
Labels checked in `apps/web/translations/en.json`: `renews` = "Renews
{date}", `billing.topup.addAmount` = "Add {amount}", `amountGroup` =
"Top-up amount"; `CREDIT_PRESETS = [25, 100, 250, 1000]` in
`credit-topup-section.tsx`; `Manage billing` still renders in
`billing-tab.tsx`.

## Verification
`bun build --no-bundle` parses the spec. Browser journeys are not run on
the owner's Mac; the proof is the next release suite against deployed
staging.

fix: clear the v0.14.0 release gate — kortixd bundles permission-rules, spec flow-id parse, billing subscribe on the ladder, connector Settings tab scope (#10094)

## Problem
The v0.14.0 release suite (Tests - release run 38961808802, attempt 3,
release head 5fdf3cc174) stayed red on four failures that survived the
automatic rerun. Each came from a same-day merge into dev that no suite
had run on:

1. **packages-kortixd**: `KORTIXD_SHARED_SOURCES lists exactly the files
the daemon imports` — #10089 made kortixd import
`packages/api-contract/src/permission-rules.ts`, which the list did not
name. The list feeds the sandbox-image fingerprint, so a change to that
file would not have rebuilt images.
2. **core / route-coverage**: `1 specification flow(s) are not
registered: PATCH`. #10090 wrapped a line of the APP-14 spec so it
starts with `\`PATCH\` with …`, which matches the spec flow-id pattern
`^\`[A-Z]…\``.
3. **deployed browser shard 4, `10-billing-journey:149`**: the step "A
real Stripe test subscription activates the account" got `400` from
`POST /v1/billing/plan`: it subscribed at `monthly_usd: 20`, which is
below the credits ladder ($50 minimum).
4. **deployed browser shard 4, `49-connector-connect-landing:341`**:
`getByRole('tab', { name: 'Settings' }).last()` clicked the *project*
top-nav Settings tab (failure screenshot shows project settings). The
connector's own Settings tab renders only once write access resolves, so
until then the project tab was the last match. It passed on some
retries: a race.

## Change
1. `permission-rules.ts` added to `KORTIXD_SHARED_SOURCES` (no imports
of its own; both Dockerfiles already copy all of
`packages/api-contract`).
2. The APP-14 line now reads "A `PATCH` with …". No meaning change.
3. The billing journey subscribes at `100`, the same tier its checkout
step starts.
4. Spec 49 clicks Settings inside the connector's tablist (the one with
an `Accounts` tab), so it waits for the right tab.

## Verification
- `bun test src/__tests__/shared-sources.test.ts` (kortixd): 3 pass, 0
fail.
- `bun tests/bin/ke2e.ts coverage`: before `✗ coverage gate failed …
PATCH`; after `✓ coverage gate passed`.
- Billing ladder: `apps/web/src/features/billing/compute-pricing.ts`
`CREDIT_TIERS` starts at 50.
- Browser specs are not run on the owner's Mac; the proof is the next
release suite against deployed staging, dispatched right after merge.

fix(tests): billing journey drives the credits tier dropdown, not the retired preset radiogroup (#10092)

## Problem
The v0.14.0 release gate (Tests - release run 38956715811, deployed
browser shard 4) failed `10-billing-journey.spec.ts:127` on attempt 1
and on the automatic rerun: `getByRole('radiogroup', { name: 'Monthly
plan amount' })` expected 1, received 0. The serial spec then skipped
`:147` (the checkout journey), which clicks `radio /Pro/`.

The product is correct. The failure screenshot of deployed staging shows
the Plan pane with the `CreditTierSelect` dropdown (`20,000 credits /
month`) and `Subscribe for $200 / month`. The credits-plan work (#9814 →
#10007) replaced the preset radiogroup and the free dollar input with
one tier dropdown on a fixed ladder (50, 100, 200, 300, 500, … 10,000).
There is no $250 tier and no free input any more.

## Change
Both tests drive `combobox 'Monthly credits tier'` → `option /^N
credits/`, the pattern `free-tier-pricing-onboarding.spec.ts` already
uses:
- `:127`: opens on 20,000 credits / $200, picks 50,000 → `Subscribe for
$500 / month`, picks 10,000 → `Subscribe for $100 / month`.
- `:147`: picks the 10,000-credit tier before `Subscribe for $100 /
month`; the checkout request assertion (`monthly_usd: 100`) is
unchanged.

## Verification
- Labels checked against `apps/web/translations/en.json` on dev:
`billing.credits.tiers.label` = "Monthly credits tier",
`creditsPerMonth` = "{credits} credits / month",
`planCard.subscribeAction` = "Subscribe for {amount} / month".
- `bun build --no-bundle` parses the spec.
- Browser journeys are not run on the owner's Mac. The proof is the next
release suite run against deployed staging, dispatched right after this
merge.

feat(apps): external Apps — add any site by URL, framed in Kortix (#10090) ## Summary An App can now be a site hosted elsewhere. **Add app** on the Apps page (or `kortix apps create --url `) adds any https site. The Apps grid lists it beside the Apps Kortix runs. The full-screen App view frames it, so a third-party tool reads as part of Kortix. Problem: a project's tools live in many places. Only the Apps Kortix deployed could sit in the Apps page, so a team's dashboard, vendor tool or another team's service always meant leaving Kortix. What it does: - **API.** `POST /projects/:id/apps` takes `external_url` (https only, no credentials, else `400`). - The API reads the site's `X-Frame-Options` and CSP `frame-ancestors` once, through the existing SSRF guard (`safeEgressFetch`, 5 s). - A site that allows framing gets `capabilities: ["preview"]`. - A site that refuses gets `capabilities: []` plus the warning `app_external_not_frameable`. - A site the API cannot reach (a private address, a timeout) counts as frameable, because the viewer's browser may reach it. - Deploy, rollback and `/token` answer `409 app_capability_unsupported`. - `access-session` returns the site URL. - The App's Kortix host answers `302` to the site, after the access gate. - `PATCH external_url` moves the App. On an App Kortix runs it answers `409 app_not_external`. - An external App takes no App slot and reports `estimated_monthly_usd: 0`. - **DB.** Two new columns: `apps.external_url text` and `apps.external_frameable boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false`. Additive only. - **SDK.** Adds the optional field `external_url` to `App`, `CreateAppInput` and `UpdateAppInput`. Additive only, no breaking change. - **CLI.** - `create --url` and `set --url`. - `list` shows `external`. - `show` shows `external · hosted elsewhere`. - `create`, `set` and `show` print the `hosted` and `capabilities` rows. - **Web.** - "Add app" sits in the Apps header. The dialog asks for a URL and a name. The name defaults to the host. - Cards and the App view frame the site. A refused site shows one line plus "Open in a new tab". - The "External" status replaces "Not deployed". The Versions menu is hidden for an external App. - 6 new strings in all 9 locales. - **Docs.** `apps.mdx` gets a new section, "Show an App hosted elsewhere", and the CLI reference rows. The spec and flow add **APP-14**. ## Demo video https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b32cab73-2e74-4866-a305-08ede0c86d38 ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / chore - [ ] Docs / skills - [ ] Infrastructure / CI - [ ] Security fix - [ ] Breaking change ## How was this tested? All local, in worktree `apps-external`: - `pnpm test -- --id APP-14`: **1/1 passed**, 8 steps. The steps cover: - 400 for an http URL, a URL with credentials, and a `javascript:` URL; - create and read-back; - deploy and token both 409; - access-session returns the site URL; - the Kortix host 302s to the site; - PATCH moves the URL, and PATCH on an App Kortix runs answers 409 `app_not_external`; - delete. - `bun test apps/api/src/apps/external.test.ts`: **5/5**. Covers the XFO / CSP `frame-ancestors` parser: `'none'`, `'self'`, `*`, `https:`, wildcard hosts, the scheme mismatch, multiple policies, and the XFO fallback. - SDK, TDD: - The new type test failed `tsc` first, with 6 errors. - After the change, `apps.test.ts` passes **28/28** and `tsc` is clean. - `public-surface`, `public-type-surface` and `contract-drift` pass. - `pnpm smoke:install` passes. - CLI: `apps-capabilities` (15), `apps-set` (14) and `commands/apps.test.ts` (5) pass, and `tsc` is clean. - Web: - `apps-feature-gate` **16/16**, `app-preview` 43/43, `app-shared` 5/5. - `tsgo` reports no errors in `features/apps`. - eslint is clean on the changed files. - `kortix-brand/scripts/audit.sh` is clean on the new file. Its existing findings are on lines this PR does not touch. - API: `tsc` clean, eslint clean on the changed files, `pnpm --filter @kortix/db lint` reports 0 issues. - i18n: `node apps/web/scripts/i18n-catalogs.mjs check --base=origin/dev` passes for all 9 catalogs. - Real surfaces on the local stack: - agent-browser: added `https://example.com`. The `POST` body was `{"slug":"example-com","name":"example.com","external_url":"https://example.com"}` and the response had `capabilities ["preview"]`. The App view framed the site. - Added `https://github.com` (`x-frame-options: deny`). It showed the fallback tile and Open in a new tab. - The menu of an external App shows only Access and Delete. Dark theme checked. - Real CLI process: `apps create --url` printed the framing warning. `--url http://…` exited 1 with the validation error. `set --url`, `list` and `show` printed the external rows. `deploy` was refused. - Test change: `apps-feature-gate.test.ts` lost two `toContain('if (!app.active_deployment_id)')` source-text assertions. That guard line now also checks `external_url`. Per testing rule 6, a source-text assertion is deleted, not updated. The rest of both tests still guard the same behavior. ## Security & data review - [x] No secrets, keys, or credentials are committed (verified by secret scan / review) - [x] Authorization checks are in place for any new/changed endpoints (IAM / access control). Create and PATCH keep `project.app.write`. Access-session keeps the App access check before it returns the URL. The Kortix-host redirect runs after the access gate. - [x] User input is validated (e.g. Zod) and output is safe. `external_url` is https only, has no userinfo and is ≤ 2048 characters. The server fetches it only through `safeEgressFetch`: DNS-pinned, private ranges refused, redirects re-validated, 5 s timeout. The frame keeps the existing `framePolicy('app', url)` sandbox. - [x] No sensitive data (tokens, PII, secrets) is written to logs - [x] No customer names, people's names, emails, or real prod IDs in the code, commits, this PR text, or the demo video (synthetic local user only) - [x] DB schema / migration changes are reviewed and reversible. They add two columns: one nullable, one with a constant default. Old code ignores both. - [ ] Touches auth / IAM / crypto / billing / migrations → requested the relevant code owner. Migration only, additive. ## Rollout / rollback - The migration is additive and safe for mixed versions. - No flag. The feature is off until someone adds an external App. - Rollback: revert this PR. External App rows then become empty deployment-less Apps that show "Not deployed", until someone deletes them. - Known limit: a site that keeps its sign-in in a cookie can ask the viewer to sign in again inside the frame, because browsers limit cookies in third-party frames. The docs say so, and "Open in a new tab" is always available. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

fix(permissions): the most specific rule wins on both harnesses, whatever the key order (#10089) ## Summary A prod session (v0.13.57) refused every `Skill` call: the compiled rule was `skill: { : allow, …, '*': deny }`, and OpenCode 1.18.23 applies the **last** matching rule in key order (`permission/index.ts` `fromConfig` + `evaluate` = `findLast`). #10000 fixed that one function by writing `*` first. The class stayed open: any Kortix-built or user-authored map with `*` after a specific rule (for example `bash: { "git push *": ask, "*": allow }`, or `{ bash: ask, "*": allow }`) still resolved to the `*` rule on OpenCode, while pi used the most specific rule. Two harnesses, two semantics, and the docs already promised "the longest matching pattern wins". **Guarantee, both harnesses:** the most specific matching rule wins, whatever order the keys are written in. Longest pattern = most specific; equal lengths compare by code unit, later wins. Keys follow the same order (`bash` outranks `*`); a key whose map matches nothing falls back to a less specific key. An agent block still outranks the global block on OpenCode. One shared ordering, `@kortix/api-contract/permission-rules` (`comparePatterns`, `orderPermissionRules`), applied at every path a rule takes to OpenCode: | Where rules are built / merged / forwarded | Order-dependent before? | Now | |---|---|---| | API `compile-agent-config.ts` v2 `skillsGrantToPermissionRule` | yes (prod: `*` last = every skill denied) | ordered (`orderPermissionRules` at the end of `compileAgentBlock`) | | API v2 agent `.md` `permission` copied through | yes (author order) | ordered, same call | | API v3 `compileAgentV3` (`permission` + `skills`/`subagents` allowlists) | yes (author order; allowlists fixed in #10000) | ordered | | kortixd `buildOpencodeConfigContent`: Slack `question: deny`, `capabilityToolRules`, `denyBuiltinSkills`, `applyAgentToolAccess` | yes (`denyBuiltinSkills`/removed tools relied on "append last") | step 9 orders the global and every agent block; a removed tool now also drops more specific keys it covers (`pty_spawn` under `pty_*`) | | Project `harnesses/opencode/opencode.json[c]` and a config dir's `agents/*.md` (OpenCode reads them itself; `mergeDeep` keeps their order) | yes | new `open-code/permission-order.ts` plugin: its `config` hook orders every block before any agent is built | | pi `harness/pi/interactions.ts` | no for patterns; yes-ish for keys (a tool map with no match returned "no rule" instead of falling to `*`; no wildcard keys) | resolves keys most specific first with the shared compare, falls through like OpenCode | | pi subagents (`runtime.ts` child policy) | same as pi | same resolver | | `kortix_permissions`, agent grants | no (set membership, not patterns) | unchanged | A side effect: the compiled JSON of a project whose permission keys were out of order changes, so its `agent_config_etag` changes once and a running session may show the "config changed" reload hint after deploy. ## Demo video The prober session on the local stack (Platinum sandbox, OpenCode): `alpha-probe`/`beta-probe` (listed) load, `gamma-probe` (unlisted) is refused, `echo blocked-check-1` is refused by `"echo blocked*": deny` written before `"*": allow`, `echo allowed-check-2` runs. The refusal text shows OpenCode's flattened rules in the new order. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11cc87a7-5d8a-42aa-9516-29c386b1209e ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [ ] New feature - [x] Refactor / chore - [x] Docs / skills - [ ] Infrastructure / CI - [ ] Security fix - [ ] Breaking change ## How was this tested? Tests first: the new API rows failed on `dev` (2 fail) and the kortixd composition/fall-through rows failed with the fix reverted (2 fail), then passed. - `bun test src/__tests__/permission-rules.test.ts` (packages/api-contract): 8 pass. Full package: 389 pass, 0 fail. - API compile suites (hermetic env): `compile-agent-config`, `agent-config-push`, `session-reload-latest-etag`, `unit-sandbox-agent-compiler`: 111 pass, 0 fail. New rows evaluate the compiled JSON with OpenCode's own algorithm (`toEqual` ignores key order, which is why no earlier test saw this). - kortixd, every suite that touches permissions/config composition (31 files via `scripts/test.sh`): 827 pass, 0 fail. New `permission-precedence.test.ts`: 13 cross-harness rows (pi resolver == OpenCode `findLast` over the ordered block), a row proving unordered OpenCode disagrees, the composed config from an unordered (old-API) compiled set, and the plugin's `config` hook output == `orderPermissionRules`. - `tsgo --noEmit`: kortixd, api, api-contract clean. `eslint src`: kortixd and api clean. `test:architecture`: 264 pass. starter: 74 pass. `tests/unit/docs-frontmatter`, `no-docs-tree`: pass. Local stack (`pnpm worktree start permission-order`, Platinum, synthetic project shipped with `kortix ship`): 1. OpenCode, agent `prober` (`skills: [alpha-probe, beta-probe]`, `.md` `bash: { "echo blocked*": deny, "*": allow }, "*": allow`): alpha + beta load (markers returned), gamma refused, `echo blocked-check-1` refused, `echo allowed-check-2` → `allowed-check-2`. 2. OpenCode, agent `globber` (no `permission` in its `.md`; project `opencode.jsonc` `bash: { "echo global-blocked*": deny, "*": allow }, "*": allow`): `echo global-blocked-3` refused (the plugin path), `echo fine-4` → `fine-4`, unlisted `beta-probe` refused. 3. pi (`pi_harness` on), agent `prober`: `echo blocked-check-5` → "The project policy denies this bash call.", `echo allowed-check-6` → `allowed-check-6`, skills listed: `alpha-probe`, `beta-probe` only. ## Security & data review - [x] No secrets, keys, or credentials are committed (verified by secret scan / review) - [x] Authorization checks are in place for any new/changed endpoints (IAM / access control) — no endpoint changed - [x] User input is validated (e.g. Zod) and output is safe - [x] No sensitive data (tokens, PII, secrets) is written to logs - [x] No customer names, people's names, emails, or real prod IDs in the code, commits, this PR text, or the demo video (AGENTS.md → "NEVER write customer data or PII") - [x] DB schema / migration changes are reviewed and reversible — none - [ ] Touches auth / IAM / crypto / billing / migrations → requested the relevant code owner — not touched ## Rollout / rollback No migration, flag or env var. The API change applies on deploy; the kortixd change reaches a sandbox with the next daemon build. Each half fixes OpenCode on its own for Kortix-compiled config (a new API with an old daemon, or an old API with a new daemon). Revert = revert this commit. ## Reviewer checklist - [ ] Change is scoped and understandable - [ ] The demo video shows the change working - [ ] The tests that cover the change ran locally and passed - [ ] Security & data review above is satisfied --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

fix(manifest): a v2 manifest with imports keeps skills, commands and extensions out of the merge (#10087) ## Problem #10000 made `skills`, `commands` and `extensions` importable map keys (for v3). The import resolver applied them to every manifest version. A **v2** manifest with `imports:` and a non-map top-level `skills` / `commands` / `extensions` now throws `` `skills` must be a map ``. Compiled governance becomes `null`, and the session's config release fails. Prod (0.13.57) compiles the same manifest. Found in the pre-promote regression sweep. ## Evidence before the fix (dev, real session) A synthetic v2 starter with `imports: [.kortix/extra.yaml]` and `skills: [kortix-cli]`, on a throwaway dev project branch: ``` GET /v1/projects//sessions//config release: source=image-default, failed_release_id=3ebea3704c56…, fallback_reason="release 3ebea3704c56 failed: the default agent \"kortix\" is not loaded" ``` The same fixture through `buildConfigRelease` (real git, the prod tree `da10fd3082` against dev): - prod: `project` variant governance = full agent set - dev: `project` variant governance = `null`; `agent:*` variants = `compiled governance failed: kortix.yaml: \`skills\` must be a map` ## Fix `resolveManifestImportsSync` merges only the v2 collections (`triggers`, `connectors`, `agents`, `apps`, `tools`) for a v2 root. v3 keeps all importable keys. ## Verification - New test fails first, then passes: `packages/manifest-schema` `bun test` → 639 pass, 0 fail. - `apps/api` `compile-agent-config.test.ts` + `builder.test.ts` → 113 pass, 0 fail. - Differential compile (prod tree vs fixed branch) over 11 fixtures (v1 `kortix.toml`, v2 `.kortix/opencode`, v2 `harnesses/opencode` with `tools/*.ts` + own `bun.lock`, v2 current starter, `skills: [list]`, `tools:` map, pi, >128 KiB agent, triggers+connectors, imports, imports+skills): `project` governance is identical to prod for all 11. - Dev verification after deploy: in the merge comment. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

docs(audit): regenerate the audit action reference (mcp_sign_in.check) (#10085)

The audit-actions doc guard (`tests/unit/audit-actions-doc.test.ts`)

label. Regenerated with `bun
apps/web/scripts/generate-audit-actions-doc.mjs`. Verified: `npx vitest

Dev green: fix the last red tests, fake clocks, no quarantine, staging App origin, mcp-sign-in-check audit label (#10084)

## Problem

`dev` must be green for the single release suite to pass. Red on `dev`
(contract lanes, run 38948130012, and then a new break):

1. kortixd `pi harness > a steered message dismisses an open question`
failed about 1 run in 62.
2. apps/web `the waiting row … with a queue on screen` failed 3 of 3
runs.
3. The audit route-label guards failed in apps/api and apps/web, after
#10078 added `POST …/connectors/mcp-sign-in-check` without a label.
4. Two unit tests waited on real time (`ecs-stabilize-budget` 29 s,
`exit-once-decided` 15 s) and flaked under load.
5. 11 flows and 1 DB suite sat in quarantine and the release gate
skipped them. Rule 4 says: fix or delete.

## Changes

1. **kortixd:** the test derived a "new" message id by swapping the last
character, which collided with the minted id about 1 run in 62
(`runtime.steer` correctly answered `duplicate`). A `siblingId()` helper
now picks a character that cannot collide. No product change.
2. **web:** the test pinned the exact one-line `<TurnViewport>` tag,
which #10072 changed on purpose. It now asserts the layout: the busy row
sits inside the turn viewport, after `<SessionTurn>`.
3. **Audit label** for `mcp-sign-in-check`:
   - "Checked MCP server sign-in", translated in all 9 locales;
   - the generated route and title maps are regenerated.
4. **Fake clocks:**
- `ecs-stabilize-budget` 29.4 s → 0.6 s, with exact budget assertions; a
mutation check (60 s → 30 s grace) fails 2 cases.
   - `exit-once-decided` 15.1 s → 0.25 s.
5. **Quarantine removed:**
   - TUN-6 fixed (its root cause was fixed by #9576).
- CONN-26 deleted: it needed the in-sandbox connector tools that #10073
removed.
   - SESS-23, SESS-23-pi and CFG-12-pi are back in the gate.
- 6 App flows are back. The apps-router Worker's `STAGING_API_ORIGIN`
pointed at a dead tunnel, so every staging App host answered Cloudflare
530; it now points at `staging-api-euw2.kortix.com`, which answers 200.
- The `integration-project-snapshot` DB suite gets local Supabase
Storage as its bucket.
   - The quarantine mechanism itself is deleted.

## Verification

- **kortixd** `pi-harness.test.ts`: 10/10 runs pass, and 5 parallel runs
pass. Forcing the colliding id reproduces the exact CI error on the old
code.
- **web** `session-chat-busy-row-fallback.test.ts`: 10/10 runs pass.
- **Audit labels:**
- `pnpm --filter kortix-api test
src/__tests__/unit-audit-route-labels.test.ts`: 10 pass.
  - `@kortix/shared` `audit-labels.test.ts`: 22 pass.
- web `audit-display-helpers.test.ts` and `audit-i18n.test.mjs`: 51
pass.
- **i18n:** `audit-i18n.mjs --max-hardcoded=0` reports 0 missing, 0

Test latency: one Promote dispatch, one release suite as the only gate; tsgo, pnpm check, Mac guard, faster CodeQL (#10075) ## Problem Testing latency slowed AI-driven development. Measurements: - **Typecheck:** API took 52–56 s per run. - **Agents ran whole package suites locally**, for example all 2,129 `apps/web` tests to verify one change. - **The release tree was tested twice:** on the PR into `staging` (local stack) and again on the PR into `prod` (deployed staging). Staging is not used for soak testing. - **The release gate's API part** took 10–17 min per shard on each of 6 shards. - **CodeQL** took ~20 min. ## The model: fast development, one gate at Promote to Production | Where | What runs | Blocks? | |---|---|---| | Your box | `pnpm check`: tsgo typecheck and lint of the touched packages, and only the test files related to the changed files | your judgment | | Push to `dev`, PR into `dev` | seconds-long guards only | no | | Nightly on `dev` | contract lanes (core-flows, core-db, packages-*), no browser | no | | PR into `staging` | nothing: Promote opens and merges it | no | | Release PR into `prod` | **the release suite, once**: contract lanes, the deployed API smoke and the browser journeys against staging, CI, CodeQL and the scanners. `full suite + quality gates` requires every check on the commit to be green. | **yes, the only gate** | ## Changes 1. **One Promote dispatch** (`promote.yml`, input `ref=dev`, `dry_run`): - takes the dev SHA, merges it into `staging` with a merge commit (conflict-safe `read-tree` build); - dispatches build-staging, waits for 8 consecutive health reads on the merge SHA; - opens the release PR and approves its held runs. `ref=staging` is the hotfix path. Every tree check moved from the staging PR to the prod PR. 2. **One release suite** (`tests-release.yml`): - calls `tests.yml` (workflow_call) for the contract lanes; - runs the deployed API smoke: 45 flows tagged `deployed`, one or two per deployment seam, in 1 job, measured at 3 min 27 s; - runs 4 browser shards against staging. The gate check waits for every other check on the release commit and requires it green. 3. **No browser lane in `tests.yml`.** Browser journeys run only in the release suite. `tests-browser-nightly.yml` and the quarantined `13-sdk-only-session` spec are deleted. 4. **Contract lanes:** `core` is split into `core-flows` (6.5 min) and `core-db` (8.2 min); it took 11–12 min as one lane. 5. **Typecheck on tsgo** (`@typescript/native-preview@7.0.0-dev.20260707.2`, incremental): - API: 52–56 s → 6.7 s cold, about 1 s warm. Web: ~9 s → ~1–3 s warm (cold baseline measured under load). - tsgo and tsc agree on 0 errors after 126 web, 7 mobile and 3 other fixes. 6. **`pnpm check`** (`scripts/check.ts`): the whole local loop. 7. **Mac guard on every package `test` script** (`scripts/test-guard.mjs`): a whole-package run exits 2 in about 0.5 s. Named files, CI and Linux run unchanged. 8. **CodeQL:** `security-extended` (every security query kept), test code excluded. Measured 20 → 8.9 min. 9. **CI:** typechecks that the contract lanes also run are removed. Measured 4.8 min. 10. **Full-history gitleaks** (9 min, report-only) runs on schedule only. 11. **Browser videos:** CI records a video for every journey (`video: 'on'`). 12. **Docs:** - The `AGENTS.md` testing philosophy now has 7 rules: never a full or whole-package suite during development, one gate, small isolated tests. - Updated the testing, contributing and kortix-release skills. - Added 2 learnings entries. ## Verification - `cd tests && npx vitest run --config unit/vitest.config.ts`: 106 files, 865 passed. `npx tsc --noEmit -p tests`: exit 0. `actionlint`: clean. `node --test scripts/test-guard.test.mjs`: 4/4 pass. - `apps/api` and `apps/web` `typecheck` (tsgo): exit 0. - Promote dry runs: - 38939423091 and 38939438585 (branch tl-promote); - 38940953624 (this branch). The red tests were the ones already red on `dev`: - INIT-1/3 and 7 API manifest tests, owned by #10036; - the web i18n audit; - 3 old-layout guards, fixed afterwards. - Deployed smoke rehearsal against staging (38937150392): 45/45 green in 116 s. - Release-suite structure rehearsal (38942269957): the workflow loads, the called contract lanes run, and the gate check reports. - Mac guard, measured: - `pnpm --filter test` is refused in 0.6 s; - one named file runs in 0.95 s; - `CI=1` runs the full package suite. ## Not verified yet - **A green release suite.** It needs staging on `dev`'s tree. fix(web): limited project members see only the Customize tabs they can manage (#10068) ## Summary KRTX-2144. A project member with limited permissions saw the Customize row, saw all eight Customize tabs, and five of them opened onto "You don't have access". Visibility also changed between visits, because each surface treated an in-flight permission probe differently: the sidebar row was optimistic, the tab bar was static, and the page gate waited for a denial. This PR adds one access rule, `capabilityAccess()` in `project-sidebar/project-settings-nav.tsx`, and every Customize surface reads it: the sidebar row, the More menu, the tab bar, the page-body gate, the `/customize` redirect and the command palette. - A tab shows only when the caller holds its read leaf **and** one of its write leaves (`TAB_PREFERENCE[].manage`). Customize is configuration, so read-only access no longer earns a tab. Files (shared folders, content) still needs only `project.read` and the `drives` flag. Settings already gates on `project.settings.write`. - No surface acts before the probes settle. The tab bar holds its height with `invisible` until the answer arrives, so no tab appears and then vanishes. A failed probe settles closed. - A typed or bookmarked URL to a tab the caller cannot open is replaced with the first allowed tab, or the project home when there is none. The denied page never mounts, so its requests never fire. - `PROJECT_PAGE_ACTIONS` gains the 7 write leaves, so the decision is still one `effective:batch` request. Result for the built-in Member role (`project.read`, `agent.read`, `trigger.read`, `trigger.fire`, …): no Customize row, no Agents or Triggers configuration, and no Customize entries in ⌘K. Managers keep every tab. A custom role gets exactly the tabs it can manage. Behaviour change to note: a member who holds only `trigger.read` + `trigger.fire` no longer has a "Run now" button in the web UI. Firing is still allowed by the API and the CLI. provider re-reported the same loss on *every* `/start` poll — 163
`runtime.lost` Sentry reports in ~3 min (Better Stack error spike

as lost (`runtimeIdentityState === 'unavailable'` &&

idempotent preserve. Same terminal card, silent guard, no provider
restore hammer. First-loss recovery is untouched.

consumed) and passes with the fix; 69 tests across `session-open/` +
`runtime-identity*` pass.

fix(sdk): a compaction inside a turn renders where it happened, not at the bottom (#10067) ## Summary A compaction inside a running turn rendered at the bottom of the chat, under the final answer, instead of where it happened. During the turn, the turn folded into "Worked for …" at every compaction and unfolded when work resumed (the reported flicker). Root cause: pi (and OpenCode 1.18, see the `opencode-v2` golden fixture) compacts inside a turn and keeps naming the original prompt in `reply_to` on every later reply. `sessionLogTurns` filed all of those replies under the prompt, so each compaction turn rendered after the whole answer. A reply with no `reply_to` after a marker went into the compaction turn, which draws only its marker, so that work was not shown at all. Fix (`packages/sdk/src/core/session-log/turns/turn.ts`): the replies after such a compaction form a continuation turn `:continued` right after the marker. It is `partial` (a stand-in prompt, so no bubble on web or mobile). It is the working turn when the working projection names the prompt or the marker. `SessionLogTurn.continues` (additive, new type `SessionLogContinuation`) links it. The web busy-row check (`session-chat.tsx`, `activeTurnId`) reads it. Tracked in KRTX-2565 (a Slack triage report with a screen recording). ## Demo video No local video. The local stack cannot produce a pi mid-turn auto-compaction without a cloud box and a pushed `harnesses/pi/settings.json`. fix(api): a lost session's /start answers from the row instead of re-checking the provider every call (KRTX-2566) (#10066) ## Summary KRTX-2566. Problem: with the page of a lost session open (its box removed at the provider), the web app sent `POST …/sessions/:id/start` continuously. Each call made Platinum requests and logged `runtime.lost` with a Sentry event, for one loss. Measured on the local stack, same incident on both builds: a new session adopts a pre-warmed session whose box Platinum has removed; the page stays open 60 s. | | `dev` | this branch | |---|---|---| | `POST /start` | 365 | 2 | | `runtime.lost` log lines (each also a Sentry event) | 182 | 1 | | Platinum `restore-from-backup` attempts | 182 | 1 | | Page shows "This session's computer was lost" | yes | yes | Kept open 400 s on this branch: 1 `POST /start`, 0 further logs, 0 Platinum calls. **Cause: the server and the client fed each other.** 1. Each `/start` on a lost row claimed an in-place recovery (row → `provisioning`, `claimInPlaceRuntimeRecovery`), the provider refused the restore, and the loss was preserved again (row → `stopped`, `preserveEstablishedRuntime`). 2. The `session_changed` trigger makes the session stream send a runtime frame for each flip. 3. The SDK re-reads `/start` on any changed runtime frame (`use-session-stream.ts` `applySessionControlFrame`), with no delay. So the loop ran at the `/start` latency. A second bug: `preserveEstablishedRuntime` reports a loss "once per identity", but `/start` reaches it after the recovery claim has overwritten `runtimeIdentityState` with `recovery_claimed`, so the check never matched and every pass was reported as a new loss. **Fix (API only):** 1. `stoppedWakeResult` answers a lost row (`runtimeIdentityState: 'unavailable'`) whose last check (`runtimeUnavailableAt`) is under `LOST_RUNTIME_RECHECK_MS` (5 min) old with the same terminal verdict as before (`stage: 'failed'`, `retriable: false`, `reason: 'runtime_identity_unavailable'`), from the row: no provider call, no claim, no write. No write means no frame, so the loop cannot start. After the window, the next `/start` re-checks the provider once, as today. 2. The report-once check also treats `runtimeUnavailableAt` on the same `preservedExternalId` as "already reported". The claim keeps that stamp; an accepted recovery strips it. 3. `RUNTIME_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE` moves to `runtime-wake-fence.ts` (no DB import) so the projection can use it; `runtime-identity.ts` re-exports it. 4. A learnings entry: "Never write the row on a terminal /start answer". Unchanged: Restart runs its own recovery (`restartInPlace`); Continue (`/recover`) strips the lost keys; the SDK is not touched, so published clients get the fix too. ## Demo video No video: the visible page is the same lost banner before and after. fix(web): a draft keeps its attached files across a session switch and a reload (#10064) ## Summary Draft text survived a session switch or a reload, but attached files did not. The composer deleted them, and the user had to attach them again. Product audit item #71. **Why:** a composer's upload controller is disposed when the composer unmounts, on a session switch or when the boot shell hands over to the live chat. `dispose()` deletes every listed upload from the server (`prompt-attachments.ts`), on the stated assumption that "drafts keep no handle". The draft stored only URL-based files (`kind: 'remote'`), never an upload. A reload never runs `dispose()`, but the draft had nothing to bring the file back with. **What changes:** - `@kortix/sdk`, additive: - `PromptAttachmentController.restore([{ attachment, file? }])` lists finished uploads as `ready`, with no request. the gate after auth (`blobUploads`, `MAX_BLOB_UPLOADS = 4`,
