fix(connectors): MCP OAuth sign-in completes (Basic auth sends no body client_id); hide the empty shared account; no 404 toast on remove (KRTX-2185) (#10053)

## Summary

KRTX-2185. A custom MCP server with OAuth failed every sign-in on prod
with `token_exchange_failed`, right after the consent screen. #10039
shortened the add flow; this PR fixes the failure itself and closes the
remaining gaps.

**Root cause (API).** For `client_secret_basic`,
`applyClientAuthentication`
(`apps/api/src/connectors/oauth2-lifecycle.ts`) sent the `Authorization:
Basic …` header **and** a body `client_id`. An authorization server that
reads a body `client_id` as `client_secret_post` answers `401
invalid_client: "Missing client_secret."` RFC 6749 §2.3 requires one
client authentication method per request. Reproduced against the
reported server, with Kortix's own lifecycle functions and a fake code:

| Token request | Answer |
|---|---|
| Basic + body `client_id` (before) | `401
{"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Missing client_secret."}`
|
| Basic only (after) | `400 {"error":"invalid_grant"}`: client auth
passes; the code is fake |

The callback `catch` in `oauth2-store.ts` logged nothing, which hid the
cause for 4 days. It now logs `[connector] OAuth code exchange failed`
with the provider's error. The legacy `oauth2.ts` path already omitted
the body `client_id` (`oauth2.test.ts:88`); both paths now behave the
same.

**Web.**

is no longer listed or counted as an account on the connector page or in
the Accounts list. That covers connectors added through Install or the
custom form. "Everyone" in Add account still reuses the slot, and the
proposed account name no longer skips past the slot's name ("wisprflow
2" → "wisprflow").

in** when the caller has no account; the button opens Add account with
"Only you".
- Removing a connector no longer toasts `connector not found`. The page
navigates away and refreshes every query except the deleted slug's
config, which used to refetch and 404.
- The custom connector form proposes the slug from the URL's domain when

Testing reset: one tree, one run — no Tests on push to dev, no attestations, 9 money-path browser specs, 220 low-value test files deleted (#10058) ## Problem Tests were the bottleneck of AI-driven development, both in compute and in wall clock, and they produced no signal: - **On the laptops:** five agent sessions ran `pnpm test` at once on one laptop (load average 112, swap full). The cause was an absolute `core.hooksPath` that pointed every worktree at a stale `pre-push` hook demanding a fresh attestation. #10032 fixed the laptop side. - **On `dev`:** from 2026-10-12, every push to `dev` ran 10 `Tests` lanes. 43 of 43 completed runs were red, ~2,600 job-min a week. 21 browser tests failed in every run. - **On the prod PR:** it re-ran CI, CodeQL, DB Migrations, i18n and the secret scans on the staging tree plus `VERSION`. - **In the release gate:** `Tests - release` passed 5 of 39 runs. v0.13.57 needed 5 rounds over 20.4 h. - **In git history:** 559 of 4,626 commits in 60 days only touched `tests/attestations/`. ## The philosophy (now in `AGENTS.md`, "Testing philosophy") 1. Test at the boundaries users touch: HTTP API, CLI, SDK public surface, DB migrations, a few money-path browser journeys. 2. Run each suite **once per tree**. fix(sessions): web and mobile open a session on its own model (#10056) ## Summary A session whose model was set from the CLI, the SDK or Slack opened in the web with a different model. Its first web message ran on that model, which replaced the session's model with no sign. Product audit item #68. **Why:** the CLI, the SDK and Slack store a session's model as its pin (`metadata.opencode_model`) and send it with every prompt. The web composer never read the pin: - Its model came from browser-local picks: the session slot, then the per-agent slot. Next came the server default and the account default. - The web sends that model with every prompt (`overrides.model`), and the prompt's model wins over the pin (`apps/api/src/projects/lib/prompt-model.ts`). - The one guard, a seed from the last transcript message, ran only when the account had no default model (`autoSeed` returns early on `globalDefault`). It also wrote the model into the per-agent slot, so one session's model leaked into every other session of the same agent. The mobile session composer had the same gap: its picks were the per-agent pick and the defaults (`apps/mobile/lib/session/local-config.ts`). **What changes:** - `@kortix/sdk` (additive): - `sessionModelCandidates({ session, lastPromptModel, gatewayEnabled })` (pure, root barrel) lists the models a session already runs, most trusted first: 1. a chosen pin, source `explicit` (CLI, SDK, Slack, `PUT /model`) or `repointed` (the platform moved a retired choice); 2. the model of the session's last prompt; 3. a default pin (the default resolved at create). - `latestPromptModel(messages)` (pure, root barrel): the model of the newest user message that records one. - `useRuntimeLocal` / `useSessionModelSelection` take two new optional options, `projectSession` and `lastPromptModel`. The session's models rank after a pick made in this composer for this session and before the per-agent slots and every default. They are never written to storage. - Web: - `session-chat.tsx` passes the session row and the last prompt's model. The transcript seed is removed: it was skipped whenever the account had a default model, and it leaked one session's model into others. - The instant session shell (`instant-session-shell.tsx`, through `ComposerChatInput`) passes the session row. A booting session shows the same model. - Mobile: the thread composer ranks a pick made in this thread first, then the session's models, then the per-agent pick. A pick made in a thread now belongs to that thread. It is still saved as the agent's pick for sessions without a model of their own. - Docs: - `content/docs/sdk/sessions.mdx` states that the web and mobile apps open a session on its saved model. - `content/docs/sdk/reference.mdx` and `packages/sdk/README.md` list the two new functions. **What does not change:** the API, the pin, and how other surfaces send. A model picked in the web for one session still applies to that session's prompts only. It does not rewrite the pin (see the follow-up below). ## Demo video The local web app against the local API, from journey 55 at 0.75× speed. A session pinned the way the CLI pins it opens. fix(share): render a shared session's messages as the session does (#10052) ## Summary A public transcript share (`/share/session/`) rendered messages differently from the session chat: - **Assistant replies:** code fences, lists, and paragraphs collapsed into one inline code run. - **User prompts:** rendered as markdown in a `bg-sidebar` bubble. Root cause: `getPublicSessionMessages` (`apps/api/src/shared/public-session-share-view.ts`) called `compactMessage` in its one-line digest mode. fix(desktop): right-click shows the platform menu: spelling, edit, link and image (KRTX-2555) (#10051) ## Summary KRTX-2555. Problem: in the desktop app, a right-click on the prompt box, the chat or a link did nothing. People could not paste with the mouse, fix an underlined misspelling, or copy a link or an image. Every browser and native text field has this menu. Cause: the Electron shell handled no `context-menu` event on the app window's `webContents`, so Chromium showed nothing. Fix (`apps/desktop-electron`): 1. `src/context-menu.js`: - `contextMenuTemplate(params, actions)` builds the menu from Electron's `context-menu` params, in browser order: | Where | Items | | --- | --- | | A misspelled word | up to 5 suggestions (or **No Guesses Found**), **Add to Dictionary** | | A link | **Open Link in Browser** (web and mail links only), **Copy Link** | | An image | **Copy Image**, **Copy Image Address** | | A text field | Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Paste, Paste and Match Style, Select All, each enabled from `editFlags` | | Selected text elsewhere | Copy | - `attachContextMenu(webContents, …)` shows it on every right-click; an empty area shows nothing. 2. Wired on the app window (`main.js`) and the Quick Entry bar (`quick-entry.js`). 3. A page element with its own menu calls `preventDefault` on `contextmenu`; Chromium then sends the shell no event, so the page's menu still wins. 4. Docs: `apps/desktop-electron/README.md` ("Right-click menu", plus a parity-table row) and `apps/web/content/docs/clients.mdx` (Desktop app). **Release note** (ships with the next desktop build): "Right-click in the desktop app now shows the menu you expect: paste, spelling fixes, and copy for links and images." ## Demo video No video. feat(session-log): cap the restore at 24 MiB; over it the box boots with the D3 note alone (#10043) ## Summary A session-log restore held the whole log in memory on both sides, with no cap. Measured on a real Platinum pi box (2 vCPU, 3.9 GB): a synthetic 38.5 MB log (1,000 tool results of 40 kB) peaked the daemon at **1.57 GB RSS** (+1.45 GB, ~38x the log) and raised the API by ~330 MB. This was the last blocker before `session_log_restore` can default on in prod (dev runs it on since #9986). Fix (option (a) of the plan, no paging): - **API.** `SESSION_LOG_RESTORE_MAX_BYTES` (`apps/api/src/config.ts`, default **24 MiB**) bounds what the box pulls: `octet_length(record::text)` of the live messages **plus 2/5 of** `bytes` of the session's live `session_log_blobs` (full texts over 256 kB, attachments), one sum (`sessionLogRestoreBytes`), in the claim transaction under the session lock, before any record leaves Postgres. The size query reads the records inside Postgres only. Above it `POST /v1/projects/:p/sessions/:s/log/restore` still claims the generation and answers **413** `session_log_too_large` (`SessionLogRestoreTooLarge`): every thread without messages, every rev, `seq_max`, `bytes`, `limit`, `messages`. No record leaves Postgres. The claim is kept so the new box fences an old one and journals above every stored seq. - **kortixd** (`shared/session-log-boot.ts`). On that 413 the box writes the log's root with the D3 note alone (above `seq_max`), keeps no other thread, persists every stored id (`revs`) as unwritten so later boots do not read the store as behind (no re-claim loop), journals at the claimed generation, and patches the session `restore_grade: 'partial'`, `ext.kortix.data.restore.dropped.message = `. The note tells the agent the size and the limit. A 413 with another body (a proxy) claims nothing: no restore, as a 404. - **Switch preflight.** `POST …/log/switch-preflight` passes `restore: false` for a log over the cap, so it answers `restores: false` with `history` as the first loss (`session-log-switch.ts`; `capabilities.ts` and `wire.ts` docs). - **SDK / web.** `sessionLogRestoreNotice` gets kind `message` (not yet on npm: 0.13.57 lacks the function, so the union change is additive). The banner reads "Missing: N earlier messages. The agent was told what is missing." `missingMessage` in all 9 locales. - **Note text.** The agent's note labels sizes in MiB / KiB / bytes (`28.7 MiB`, `24 MiB`) and never rounds up. - **Cap choice.** Prod restore bundle sizes (prototype bench from the 2026-10-09 read-only aggregates): p50 0.06 MB, p90 0.9 MB, p99 3.7 MB, p99.9 15 MB, longest 37 MB. 24 MiB is 1.6x p99.9 and keeps the daemon peak under ~1 GB on a 4 GB box. Sessions above it lose the agent's history (the transcript keeps it). - **Docs.** Harness README "Memory, and the cap" (+ the default-on blocker paragraph replaced), `wire.ts` contract doc, `/docs/work/sessions` (Continue a lost session), `/docs/project` flag table, flag registry note. ### Blobs: one cap, weight 2/5 (measured) Real Platinum pi box, 60 synthetic 500 kB images (30 MB of blobs, 83 kB of records). Uncounted, the restore answered 200: daemon 111 MB → **566 MB peak** (+455 MB, ~15x the blob bytes), API +~50 MB (the box reads them one by one). Records cost ~38x (38.5 MB → +1.45 GB). So blobs count at `SESSION_LOG_BLOB_WEIGHT` = **2/5** (15/38 ≈ 0.39, rounded up): `bytes` = records + ceil(blobs × 2/5), and the 24 MiB cap means about the same daemon peak (~1 GB) for both. feat(sessions): /workspace on a Platinum volume behind the workspace_volume flag (#10047) ## Summary Step 1 of stateless sandboxes: `/workspace` on a Platinum volume, behind the operator-only project flag `workspace_volume` (off by default). With the flag on, a new Platinum session gets volume `kws-` (`sync_mode: git`), created at the control plane of the box's region and mounted at `/workspace` in the sandbox create, so the mount exists before kortixd starts. Boxes still stop and resume in place. Nothing deletes a box. kortixd fills the empty volume on the first boot with its existing Git/S3 transports and adopts the checkout on every later boot. The point of step 1 is the measurement and the consequences list below. The headline: a box that is replaced (lost box → `POST /recover`) mounts the same volume, adopts the checkout in 63 ms with committed **and** uncommitted files intact, and the agent continues the conversation (session log restore). That is the step-2 boot path, working by hand today. ## Demo video Local stack: Settings → Feature flags lists `workspace_volume` read-only ("Managed by Kortix") while it is on. Then the session page of a flag-on session whose box was deleted and replaced: the agent, on the fresh box, recalls the earlier turn and reads `dirty2.txt`, an uncommitted file that exists only on the volume. The red "Internal server error" toast is the audit route on my local shared database, which lacks migration `20261015232617027_scheduled_monthly_usd` (`column "scheduled_monthly_usd" does not exist`); this PR touches no audit or billing code. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d231797-8f6e-44cb-8b86-6f084dff2888 ## What changed **API** - `platform/services/workspace-volume.ts` (new): resolve, open, mount and delete a session's volume. - The session records `workspace_volume: { name, location }` in `project_sessions.metadata` (server-managed key) **before** the volume is created, in one statement that keeps an existing record. A crash in between leaves a record the next boot completes (open-or-create), never an unrecorded volume. - A session that has a volume always gets it back, whatever the flag or the kill switch says. A session without one gets one only at a provisioning where the flag is on. The flag is read per session, never per box. - Every volume call goes to the control plane of the volume's region (`platinumRegionControlPlane`; `null` = home region = global origin). - `session-sandbox.ts` `prepareAttemptVolumes`: mounts the volume, pins `location` to the volume's region with `locationRequired` (no home-region fallback: the box could not mount the volume there), locks provider failover to Platinum, reserves one of the 8 mount slots from Files drives, drops `KORTIX_SESSION_BRANCH_RESTORE`, sets `KORTIX_WORKSPACE_VOLUME=1`, adds a `workspace-volume` mark to `provisionTimeline`. - Session delete: `attemptArchivedBoxRemoval` deletes the volume after the box removal is confirmed, **only when the session is deleted** (`deletedAt`). `volume_busy` is waited out for ~10 s (a sandbox DELETE answers before the box releases its mount). `deleteSession` also stamps the removal intent for a session that has a volume but no box. - Failure policy: **fail clearly, never fall back to the box disk** (see below). A volume that does not open fails the boot with a `[workspace]` storage message (category `drives-unavailable`). Platinum not answering is transient (the next `/start` retries it); a refusal such as `quota_exceeded` is not. - Kill switch: `KORTIX_WORKSPACE_VOLUMES=off` gives no new session a volume. Sessions that have one keep it. **kortixd** - `KORTIX_WORKSPACE_VOLUME=1` → `workspaceVolume`. `adoptOrClearBakedCheckout` never clears a non-empty `/workspace` on a volume: a `.git` whose adoption marker does not match under `KORTIX_SESSION_BRANCH_RESTORE`, a fresh checkout that is not `KORTIX_BASE_SHA`, or files without a `.git` (ignoring `lost+found` and `.kortix-*` stages) fail the boot loudly (`workspace_volume_clear_refused`) and keep the files. - `/kortix/health` → `workspace_provider.volume`. **Image entrypoint**: removes the empty, root-owned `lost+found` of the volume root. Without it the checkout swap fails with `EACCES: permission denied, rm '/workspace/lost+found'` (seen on the local stack with the previous image). **Flag plumbing**: `@kortix/api-contract` map, `@kortix/sdk` `FeatureFlagKey` + `FEATURE_FLAG_KEYS` (additive), web flag hook, 9 translation catalogs, CLI help, docs flag table, test fixture comment. ### Why fail, not fall back 1. A silent fallback creates a session the user believes is durable and is not. Step 2 deletes boxes; a box-disk session that slipped through would lose its files then. 2. The removed design's volume → artifacts → standard ladder made the boot path unmeasurable and the state unknowable per session. One rule per session ("has a record ⇒ always mounts it") is the whole state machine here. 3. Platinum also serves the box itself: when the volume API is down, the box create usually is too. The fallback would rarely save a session. 4. The flag is operator-only on internal projects, so a failure is seen and acted on. A transient failure is retried by `/start` (tested). ### Decisions recorded - `sync_mode: git`: a single-writer working copy. `drive` mode pushes other mounts' commits into the running filesystem file by file (`vol/driveSync.ts`); a session has one writer, so that adds a reconcile loop and nothing else. Git mode commits every ~5 s, on `sync`/`fsync`, and at stop. - **Option C (`fork`) is not blocked by `volume_busy`.** Measured on dev: `POST /v1/volumes//fork` → 201 with the source mounted by a running box, and → 201 with the box stopped (mount `parked`). The doc's "a clone or fork found mounted volumes" did not fire. `DELETE` does refuse with `volume_busy` for a running **and** a stopped box. - Volumes are region-local: the global origin answers `404` for a us-east volume, and `DELETE ?missing_ok=true` there answers `204` and deletes nothing. The same name can exist in both regions as two volumes. Hence the recorded region. ## Type of change - [ ] Bug fix - [x] New feature - [ ] Refactor / chore - [ ] Docs / skills - [ ] Infrastructure / CI - [ ] Security fix - [ ] Breaking change ## How was this tested? Bun 1.4.3, worktree `workspace-volume` merged with `origin/dev` (`92b1704f5f`). Targeted runs only (macOS rule). 1. **First check on dev Platinum, plain API calls** (before any code): volume created against `api.platinum.dev` (eu-west, 469 ms) and `us-east.api.platinum.dev` (750 ms); a sandbox in each region mounted it at `/workspace` (ext4 `/dev/vdb`, 98 G); file written, `git commit`, `pt-vol commit`, stop (1.46 / 1.53 s), start (1.22 / 1.15 s); file and `git log` read back in both regions. Probe sandboxes and volumes deleted. 2. **kortixd** (TDD: 7 new assertions failed first): `materialize-repo` + `config` + `workspace-provider` tests **84 pass, 0 fail**; full `pnpm test` **2,312 pass, 0 fail**; `tsc` clean. 3. **API**: `typecheck` exit 0; `lint` exit 0; `pnpm test -- --db-only integration-workspace-volume` **9/9** (operator-only flag 403; record once + region pin; home vs us-east origin; flag off / kill switch / forged record → no call; kill switch never removes a volume; quota 403 not retried and not transient, 503 retried 3× and transient; create body drops `KORTIX_SESSION_BRANCH_RESTORE`; removal lane deletes a deleted session's volume at its region and retries `volume_busy`; a session that is not deleted keeps its volume). Full unit suite: 1 failure, a source tripwire on the `providerLocked` line format, fixed; then the touched files: `unit-feature-flags` 45/45, failover wiring 4/4, provisioning-error 23/23, archived-box-removal 2/2, platinum-create-dedup 18/18. 4. **SDK** (TDD): key-list test failed first, then `test` exit 0, `typecheck` exit 0, `smoke:install` OK. **api-contract**: 381 pass. **CLI** `typecheck` exit 0. **Web**: `eslint src/lib/use-project-feature-flags.ts` clean; i18n check `ok` for 9/9 catalogs. 5. **Real sessions on the local stack with real Platinum boxes** (`kortix-default-52e9083989b5`, daemon `ba01c7b9…` = this branch). Tool output read from `/kortix/runtime/messages`, files read with Platinum `exec`: | Session | Region | Turn (from transcript) | Stop → resume | Files after resume | Agent continues | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | OpenCode | eu-west | `notes/hello.txt`, commit `1e13edd` | commit at +867 ms, `repo_ready` +2.48 s | committed + 2 uncommitted (incl. 50 MB blob) | commit `faf8aa0` | | pi | eu-west | `notes/pi.txt`, commit `cc96651` | commit at +1,169 ms, `repo_ready` +2.17 s | committed + uncommitted | commit `a336ecf` | | OpenCode | us-east | `notes/us.txt`, commit `6771ecc` | commit at +864 ms, `repo_ready` +2.14 s | committed | commit `5f5a815` | | pi | us-east | `notes/pi-us.txt`, commit `bf424e9` | commit at +934 ms, `repo_ready` +2.14 s | committed + uncommitted | commit `e364755` | Plus, on the eu-west OpenCode session: - daemon reboot (`kill -TERM` kortixd): warm adoption 41 ms, `switched to existing session branch`, dirty file kept; - `POST /restart`: in place, workspace intact; - **box deleted at Platinum → `POST /recover` → `/start`**: new box `sbx_…AS23` mounted the same volume, adoption 63 ms, committed + uncommitted files + the 50 MB blob intact, `KORTIX_WORKSPACE_VOLUME=1`, no `KORTIX_SESSION_BRANCH_RESTORE` in the daemon env; fix(kortixd): pi relays the /summarize turn under its compaction id; the id-less durable rule goes (#10033)

## Summary

Session Log Plan follow-up to P2.11 (#9905). pi `compact()` (`POST
/session/:id/summarize`) now relays `turn_begin` and the turn end with
the compaction marker id, as OpenCode does. apps/api binds the id to the
open `/summarize` turn (`adoptRuntimeSandboxTurn`), and
`markDurableTurns` marks a compaction's turn by message id only. The
P2.11 id-less rule (the earliest open id-less turn by time) is deleted:
it marked the wrong turn in 3 known cases (a refused `/summarize` still
open, a re-sent compaction, a box clock ahead on a replay). OpenCode
used the same rule only as a fallback when its id bind failed; that turn
now stays unmarked instead of a guess.

- `apps/kortix-sandbox-agent-server/src/harness/pi/runtime.ts`: only the
compaction that `compact()` starts is a turn: `onTurnBegin(marker)` at
its start, `onTurnEnd(marker)` at its end. `idle` on success, stop, or
one of pi's two refusals; `error` with pi's reason when the summary call
fails. Auto compactions (threshold, overflow) and an extension's
`ctx.compact()` relay nothing. A Stop drops a `/summarize` still queued
behind the running turn (no model call).
- Refusals end `idle` on purpose: an `error` end parks the session
(`parkTurnError` → `stopped`), sends a failure push, relays to channels
and records a trigger run as failed, all for a no-op. pi 1.2.0 gives no
code, so `PI_COMPACTION_REFUSALS` matches the exact strings `Compaction
failed: Nothing to compact (session too small)` and `Compaction failed:
Already compacted`; the pi-harness tests fail if a bump rewords them.
The wire summary message keeps the refusal text as its error, so the
client shows it.
- `shared/turn-relay.ts` `turnEndAfterBegin` (used by `pi/boot.ts`): a
turn end is relayed after its begin settled, at most 5 s later. Without
the order, a refused `/summarize` (~0.2 s) could post its end before its
begin, and the late begin would adopt a turn nothing ends; the bound
keeps a hung begin from delaying an end ~31 s.
- `apps/api/src/projects/session-log-ingest.ts`: one update by message
id (assistant `reply_to`, compaction `message_id`); the time-window rule
and its imports are gone.
- Short-context `/summarize`: pi stores nothing. Before: the API turn
had no id and ended ~2 s later through the renewal pass, with no reason
anywhere but the wire. Now: the turn carries the marker id and ends
`completed` (idle) in ~0.4 s; the wire summary message carries
`Compaction failed: Nothing to compact (session too small)`; the daemon
logs `[pi] compaction failed`; the session stays `running`. The session
log has no record (no pi entry to export); the contract has no place for
a compaction that stored nothing, so none is invented.
- The P2.12 flush on a compaction between turns stays: an extension's
`ctx.compact()` has no turn end.
- Harness README: the `/summarize` turn contract and the refusal.

No migration, flag, env var or public contract change. Nothing reads
`log_durable_at` yet.

fix(web): an unresolved command chip can no longer carry attachments out as a prompt (KRTX-1903) (#9995)

## Review in 60 seconds

- **What changed:** an unresolved `/` chip + staged attachment + Enter
no longer sends the attachment out as an ordinary prompt — the composer
refuses with a toast ("Commands are still loading" / "Nothing was
sent…") and keeps the draft and the files. The new pure guard
`planUnresolvedCommandChip` keys off a `commandsResolved` bit each host
passes (`<live query data> !== undefined`), because the `commands` array
is `[]` both while the list loads and when it resolved empty.
- **Why:** `planCommandAttachments` only acts on `plan.kind ===
'command'`; when the command list has never resolved,
`planDraftSubmission`'s lookup misses and the chip degrades to a
message, which carries attachments — reproduced on the local stack
(prompt POST with `pending_prompt.text: "/customize-opencode"`,
`attachment_names: ["krtx1903-note.txt"]`, composer emptied, tile gone).
- **Scope kept deliberately small:** a list that HAS resolved and misses
the chip keeps its documented dead-command fallback on both hosts that
pass a live list (`session-chat.tsx:4650`,
`composer-chat-input.tsx:298`); a chip without attachments still sends
while the list loads. No new per-render affordance: the never-resolved
window is one query round-trip and the submit-time toast names it; the
sibling guard's inline warning exists because its condition persists
indefinitely, this one does not.

## Summary

A `/` command chip staged in the composer plus a staged attachment plus
Enter, in the window where the live command list has **never resolved**,
sent the attachment out as an ordinary prompt. Observed once on a booted
local stack, deliberately reproduced (`POST
/v1/projects/<id>/sessions/warm/claim` with `pending_prompt.text:
"/customize-opencode"` and `attachment_names: ["krtx1903-note.txt"]` —
composer emptied, tile gone). After this PR the same three facts produce
a refusal: nothing POSTs, a toast says why, and the chip + file stay
staged.

Root cause: every submit path (editor Enter keymap, Send button, prefill
effect) routes through `handleSubmit` → `createSubmitLatch` →
`dispatchSubmission`, so the keyboard path already ran
`planCommandAttachments` — the hole is one step earlier. That guard only
acts on `plan.kind === 'command'`; when the `commands` list has never
resolved, `planDraftSubmission`'s `commands.find` misses and the chip
degrades to a **message**, which carries attachments fine. The degraded
plan sails past the guard.

The fix: the composer cannot recover the loading bit from its `commands`
prop (`[]` means both loading and absent), so each host states it.
`Composer` gains `commandsResolved?: boolean`, default `false` — a host
that never resolves a list cannot vouch for a chip. The two hosts that
pass a live `useRuntimeCommands` list pass
`commandsResolved={agentCommands !== undefined}`
(`session-chat.tsx:4650`) and `commandsResolved={commands !==
undefined}` (`composer-chat-input.tsx:298`) — the raw query state of the
same hook instance whose (agent-filtered) list the composer consumes.
`dispatchSubmission` consults the new pure
`planUnresolvedCommandChip(...)` below the question-lock reroute (an
answer takes only the text and hands the files back to the stash, so
there is nothing there to lose) and before anything is sent or cleared:
refuse iff chip + never-resolved list + ≥ 1 attachment, keeping the
draft and the files, with a toast naming both facts. Refusal scope is
deliberate: a list that **has** resolved and misses the chip keeps its
documented dead-command fallback (`/name args` as an ordinary message —
see `draftWillRunCommand`'s doc comment), and a chip without attachments
still sends while the list loads.

Closes KRTX-1903

fix(api): purge a project's connector rows when the project is purged (KRTX-1907)

## Review in 60 seconds

- Purging a project (`DELETE /v1/projects/:projectId`) **archives** the
project row (`status: 'archived'`), so the database's
`connectors.project_id` FK cascade never fires: the project's connector
rows outlived the purged project, and `GET
/v1/connectors/projects/:projectId/connectors` kept serving them
indefinitely — journey `conn-oauth-connect-readonly` saw the row on
every poll for ~2 minutes after the purge, until an explicit connector
DELETE cleared it.
- This PR makes the delete route **purge the project's connector rows
before the archive** (after it the project answers 404, so a failed
purge could never be retried). Session connector bindings RESTRICT on
the connector, so they go first, in one transaction; the database then
cascades the rest of the connector family (connections, credentials,
policies, actions). `connector_calls` and event-subscription references
keep their rows with the connector reference nulled, as before; a purge
failure answers 500 and leaves the project active, mirroring the
existing repo-delete step's retry contract.
- Red-first tests: a new real-PostgreSQL integration test drives the
delete route with the full connector family seeded and asserts every row
is purged (red before the fix: all five row sets survived the delete);
the step-order unit test now pins the four-step order and adds the
purge-failure fault path; PROJ-8 (black-box over real HTTP) now creates
an HTTP connector on the project before the delete and asserts the
purged project lists zero connectors.
- No web code changed, no schema change — the deletion happens where the
project delete already runs.

No demo video: code-only change — the fix is API-level; the before/after
evidence below is API responses on the local stack.

**Risk:** low — the only new behavior is deleting rows the user already
asked to purge; projectId-scoped deletes cannot touch other projects'

fix(db): retry a statement whose connection never established (KRTX-2510) (#10023)

## Review in 60 seconds

- `packages/db/src/client.ts` — `createDb` now gives every awaited
statement **one fresh attempt on a new connection when its connection
never established** (`connectRetry` layer, outermost so a retried
attempt goes through the same preparation and instrumentation as the
first — including the API pool's always-armed statement hook, which the
wiring tests pin). postgres.js has no driver-level retry: when a connect
attempt exceeds `connect_timeout` (prod: 10 s), the statement that drew
the socket rejects with `Error: write CONNECT_TIMEOUT <db host>:5432`,
drizzle wraps it as `Failed query: <SQL>`, and the SQL in the alert is
whatever statement was the victim — not any real query problem. The
statement provably never reached the server, so one retry cannot
double-execute anything. Transactions are deliberately not retried:

fix(db): guard postgres.js nextWrite against a socket closed mid-write (KRTX-2511) (#10019)

## Review in 60 seconds

- postgres.js 3.4.9 killed the prod API process: a connection that
closes mid-write leaves `socket = null` while a small (<1024 B) write's
`setImmediate(nextWrite)` is queued (and any query dispatched to the
dead connection afterwards — the pool hands a released connection back
out after its backend died — queues a fresh one); the immediate then
dereferences the nulled socket and the uncaught `TypeError` kills the
process. Better Stack recorded it as fatal/uncaught at `nextWrite`
(`src/connection.js:255:15`) right after a `write CONNECTION_CLOSED`
breadcrumb.
- Fix: `patches/postgres@3.4.9.patch` — the upstream-approved guard (PRs
#1168/#1176, still unmerged; 3.4.9 is the newest release) wired through
`pnpm.patchedDependencies`: `nextWrite` returns false and drops the
buffered chunk when the socket is gone, so the write degrades into the
connection's normal `CONNECTION_CLOSED` handling instead of an
uncatchable throw. Patched in the `src` (Bun/ESM, our runtime) and `cjs`
builds.
- Regression test `packages/db/src/postgres-write-guard.test.ts` drives
the real postgres.js over a real TCP socket against an in-process fake
PostgreSQL server through the exact crash sequence (reserve → mid-write
close → release → re-reserve → small query): red on unpatched 3.4.9 with
the production stack trace, green with the patch.
- Known upstream limitation kept, not widened: the query whose write was
dropped may not settle until the pool recycles the connection (upstream
issue #1208 tracks the deeper pool-reuse bug). The scope here is
stopping the uncatchable process kill; the application already treats
`CONNECTION_CLOSED` as a retryable connection error.
No demo video: code-only change (dependency patch + regression test; the
proof is the red→green run below).

**Risk:** low — the guard only changes behavior in the state that
previously crashed (`socket === null`); with a live socket `nextWrite`

## Summary

The prod API process died once at 2026-10-16 06:10:57 UTC with an
uncaught
`TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'socket.write')` thrown
from
postgres.js `nextWrite` (`src/connection.js:255:15`). The breadcrumb
right
before the crash shows a reconcile aborting with `write
CONNECTION_CLOSED`
against the project's Supabase database host — the server closed the
connection mid-write. The process had been up for ~2 days; the crash
took the
whole API down until the platform restarted it.

Root cause, in the dependency (not our call sites):

1. postgres.js queues small (<1024 B) writes: `write()` schedules
`setImmediate(nextWrite)`; `nextWrite` calls `socket.write(chunk, fn)`.
2. `closed()` clears that immediate but sets `socket = null`.
3. A query dispatched to the dead connection afterwards (the pool
re-offers a
   connection released after its backend died; reserved connections and
`sql.begin()` transactions keep writing too) schedules a fresh immediate
whose `socket.write` dereferences `null` → uncaught `TypeError` →
process
   death. `execute()` checks only `terminated`, never the socket.

This is a known upstream bug with no released fix (3.4.9 is the latest
version): porsager/postgres #1066 (Bun + Supabase — our exact stack),
#1154
and #1208; the approved guard PRs #1168/#1176/#1209 are still unmerged.

The fix is the smallest approved upstream shape, applied as a `pnpm
patch`:

- `nextWrite` returns `false` when `socket` is null and drops the
buffered
  chunk (the drop also keeps a stale partial message from leaking into a
  reconnected socket, which the upstream PRs leave behind).
- A dropped write degrades into the connection's normal
`CONNECTION_CLOSED`
handling; with a live socket the function is byte-identical to upstream.
- Wired through the repo's existing `pnpm.patchedDependencies` mechanism
(`patches/postgres@3.4.9.patch`), so a fresh `pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile`
  applies it; recorded in the learnings ledger.

fix(sdk,web): announce a turn that ends after you leave its session page (KRTX-2524) (#10020)

Fixes [KRTX-2524](https://linear.app/kortix/issue/KRTX-2524). Found
while verifying KRTX-2520 (the desktop Dock badge, #10015).

## Problem

1. In one window (web or desktop), start a turn in session X.
2. While it runs, open another page in the same window (the project
home, another session).
3. X's turn ends. Nothing announces it: no toast, no favicon dot, no
Dock badge.

## Cause

- Only the session page's live event stream announces a turn end
(`handle-session-event.ts`, `notifyTurnEnd` on busy→idle).
- One stream per window (`useSession`: "one active session at a time").
Leaving the session cleans up its effects (the route stays in a hidden
`<Activity>`, `session-route-cache.tsx`), so the stream subscription
ends.
- `turn-broadcast.ts` only relays what some tab's stream announced.
- No project-level source can stand in: the sidebar list carries no turn
signal (`running` = box up), and the `notification_center` inbox
`turn_done` rows are flag-gated (off by default), polled every 60 s, and
never call `markTurnComplete`.

## Fix

**SDK (source of truth)**
- `core/session/turn-end-watch.ts` (framework-free): follows the
handed-over turn until no turn is open, from two sources with one
verdict:
- pushed: `kortix.control.turn` frames on the session's control stream
(`GET …/events?channels=control`, the connection the page already
shared). A hidden desktop window throttles timers (Chromium; macOS App
Nap); a stream frame still arrives.
- polled: `GET …/turn` as the backstop, only while that stream is not
live (`sessionStreamConnected`), like the session view's own polls. 1 s,
then 5 s, 15 s after 5 min; stops after 12 h.
- Outcome from `last_ended`: `completed`/`unknown` → completed; a named
cause → failed; an abort or a requested stop → silent (the server push
rule). A hand-off without an open turn token waits up to 60 s for the
turn to appear. 401/403/404 end the watch.
- `react/turn-end-handoff.ts` + one call in `useSession`: hand the
running turn over when the view's effects clean up, take it back when
they run again. The page's stream and the watch never both announce. The
hand-off reads the state of the last commit, so a session switch in one
mounted page hands over the session it left.
- The watch raises the existing `notifyTaskComplete` /
`notifySessionError`, now with `projectId` and (completion)
`watchedSinceMs`. `/turn` is read with `showErrors: false`. No
`onNotify` sink (mobile) → no watch. `resetIdentityState()` ends every
watch.
- `getSessionTurn(projectId, sessionId, options?)`: optional `{
showErrors }` (additive). No new public export.

**Web**
- `notifyTaskComplete` skips a watch completion when this tab already
showed one for the session after `watchedSinceMs` (another tab's stream
relayed it). The relay gate folds an end this tab just showed itself.
- A watch completion or error links to the session's own project, not
the route on screen.

**Docs**: `sdk/react.mdx` (Turn-end notifications), SDK README
(`onNotify` events), `work/sessions.mdx` (In the app: toast + tab dot
need no flag).

## Verification

**Unit tests (written first, each seen RED; a mutation of each rule
turns its test red)**
- `packages/sdk/src/core/session/turn-end-watch.test.ts`: 24 tests
(verdict rules; release; in-flight drop; replace; retry; 401/403/404;
start window; slow cadence; ceiling; two sessions; push source: end with
no timer tick, replayed end at subscribe, poll stands down while live,
release unsubscribes).
- `packages/sdk/src/react/turn-end-handoff.test.ts`: 10 tests rendering
the hook with `react-test-renderer` and asserting the host `onNotify`
payload (unmount mid-turn → `task-complete`; failure → `session-error`;
idle; remount reclaims; session switch; disabled; no sink; sign-out;
silent 500; end delivered by the real control stream through a fake
transport, 0 `/turn` reads).
- `apps/web/src/lib/web-notifications.test.ts` (+4),
`turn-broadcast.test.ts` (+1).

**Gates**
- `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk typecheck` → exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk test` → 392 files, 6452 tests, 0 fail (dev
baseline: 390 files, 6418).
- `pnpm --filter @kortix/sdk run smoke:install` → `✔ install smoke test
passed`.
- `bun test --isolate src/lib src/features/notifications src/components`
(apps/web) → 0 fail.
- `npx eslint` on the touched web files → exit 0. `tsc --noEmit -p
apps/web`: 0 errors in touched files.

**Browser: real session, local stack (web :19300, api :19308, tunnel,
real sandbox), agent-browser.** Send a `sleep 40` prompt from the
project home → session page → wait for `GET /turn` to show the turn open
→ `history.back()` → wait for the server to close the turn. A spy on
`BroadcastChannel('kortix-turn-complete').postMessage` counts
announcements.

| Run | Broadcasts | Toast | Favicon dot |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before (dev `useSession`), left the page | 0 | none | no |
| after, left the page | 1, 174 ms after the end was seen | "Task
complete · Run sleep 40 then reply DONE · Open session" | yes |
| after, stayed on the page | 1 (the stream) | none | no |
| after, left and came back mid-turn | 1 (the stream) | none | no |

**Desktop: the real app, no Playwright (focus is real).** A wrapper
entry loads the shipped `apps/desktop-electron/src/main.js` (with
#10015's badge) and takes file commands. Flow: project home → send →
session page → `history.back()` → `app.hide()` (`document.hidden: true`,
`hasFocus: false`) → the turn ends → `lsappinfo info -only StatusLabel
<pid>`.

| Run | Dock label while hidden, after the end | Broadcasts | Shown on
the project home | After opening the session |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| control (dev `useSession`) | `""` for 60 s | 0 | `""` | `""` |
| after (2 runs) | `"1"` within 0.2 s of the end being seen | 1
(`hidden: true`) | `"1"` | `""` |

The API log for a run shows only the page's own `/events?tab_id=…`
connection: the watch joined it, and its `/turn` poll made no reads.

A first, timer-only version of the watch passed under Playwright (which
emulates focus) and in one real hidden run, but announced nothing for 64
s in another real hidden run. That is why the watch now follows the
control stream.

## Not covered / follow-ups

- A turn started elsewhere (trigger, another device) for a session never
opened in this window: the notification center inbox covers it (flag
on).
- KRTX-2434: a session page still mounted in a hidden tab whose SSE
drops silently. Same symptom, different path (the page owns the turn).
Not changed here.
- Mobile: no `onNotify` sink, no watch, no change.
- The desktop Dock badge itself ships with the next Desktop build
(#10015); this PR's web/SDK part reaches it through the existing
`set_badge_count` bridge.

fix(api): answer a non-uuid review item id like a miss, not a 500 (KRTX-2442) (#10013)

## Review in 60 seconds

- **The bug:** any client could send an arbitrary string where a review
item id is expected — `POST /v1/projects/:id/review/items/{id}/act` and
`POST /v1/projects/:id/review/bulk` validate the id as `z.string()`. A
non-uuid value reached Postgres' `uuid` column and the query died with
`22P02: invalid input syntax for type uuid: "nonexistent-item"`, wrapped
by drizzle into `DrizzleQueryError: Failed query`, which the route
surfaced as an opaque 500. Better Stack pattern `f457fabc…` (API dev,
app 2347088): 5 occurrences in 2 minutes from one probe — 3 selects (the
act route's `getReviewItemById`) + 2 updates (`bulkApplyVerdict`).
- **The fix:** guard the three helpers every such call flows through in
`apps/api/src/projects/review-items.ts` — `getReviewItemById` and
`applyVerdict` return `null` for a non-uuid id (the route's existing
null-check answers 404), and `bulkApplyVerdict` drops the non-uuid ids
before the `inArray` so the rest of the batch still applies (`{updated:
0}` when nothing usable remains). This is the exact contract
`getInboxItem` already keeps — "null for … an id that is not a uuid" —
extended to the paths trunk's earlier hardening missed. No route,
schema, or SDK change; the Slack and Teams interactivity handlers
already answer a `null` item with their graceful notices, so they pick
the fix up for free.
- **Proof:** new real-Postgres regression test
`integration-review-items-nonuuid.test.ts` failed 4/4 on trunk with the
production error byte-for-byte (`PostgresError: invalid input syntax for
type uuid: "nonexistent-item"`, code 22P02) and passes 4/4 with the fix.
On the local stack the exact dev probe now answers 404 (act) and 200
`{updated: 0}` (bulk), while a valid item still updates (200, `updated:
1`) and a mixed batch drops only the garbage id. Full attested suite
GREEN at the pushed head:
`{"core":"pass","packages":"pass","db-suites":"pass"}`.

**Risk:** low — three one-line guards in front of existing queries. A
non-uuid id could never match a row (the cast rejects it), so every
guarded call only converts a 500 into the miss-answer the same request
already gets for a well-formed unknown id. Valid uuids are untouched
(`isUuid` accepts them; the DB tests + stack probes prove the happy
path). Worst case would be an over-strict id check, and `isUuid` is the
repo's single shape check that other paths already write with, so ids
that pass on write pass on read.

**Verified:** green attestation at head `ae356f8e9e` (merge of
origin/dev `f09fbeeb42` included) — core, packages and db-suites all
PASS; `pnpm test:verify --rev HEAD --branch krtx-2442-review-uuid` →
`[attest] OK green`. Regression test 4/4 pass after failing 4/4 before
the fix. Local stack: 7 curl probes over the real API (details below).

Nobody's personal accounts run in that turn: not the prompter's, and not the creator's (the prompter would drive them). The creator's next turn restores their own and removes the stamp. ## Summary

`GET /v1/projects/:id/apps` (and its sibling routes) re-resolve the same
authorization rows several times inside one request, each with its own
pool
checkouts on a per-instance pool (`DB_POOL_MAX=6`) chronically near
saturation:

- `resolveShareSubject(userId)` — the group-membership → share-subject
read —
ran once per **independent helper**: the Apps list path ran it 3× per
request
(visibility filter, openable set, then the link slugs' visibility
re-check);
  measured on the 2026-10-14/15 burst (KRTX-2341).
- `loadAppAccessGrantsFor(appIds)` ran the same grant query twice when
the
  caller passes the same id set twice (list → openable re-resolution).

This PR wraps both in the repo's existing per-request `requestMemo`
(existing: `apps/api/src/lib/request-context.ts`), so each request does
**one** read no matter how many helpers need the value:

- `share-subject:<userId>` — 3 subject queries → 1 per `/apps` request
- `app-access-grants:<sorted app ids>` — 2 grant queries → 1 per request

Both helpers keep their cross-request fresh-read contract untouched: the
first
read of every request is still a fresh DB read, so a membership or grant
added
between two requests still authorizes (or denies) the second one. The
memo is
request-scoped only — no TTL, no cross-request cache.

Why it matters: on 2026-10-14/15 a tenant burst (six pollers, ~5–6
req/s)
saturated the per-instance pool — requests held connections while queued

feat(billing): credits everywhere for what you hold or spend; instant upgrade, scheduled downgrade with preview; fix skipped first renewal (#10007) ## Summary Two problems, reported from the Billing → Plan page: 1. Balances and spend showed in `$` although the product sells credits. 2. Changing the credits tier looked like it did nothing: an upgrade added only prorated credits with a toast that named the new monthly amount; a downgrade showed the new price at once while nothing else changed, with no date. While verifying plan changes against Stripe test mode, a **production renewal bug** surfaced (item 3). ### 1. Credits everywhere for what the account holds or spends; prices stay in `$` ```text held / spent → credits balance, buckets, usage, session/turn cost, cost explorer, ledger, gateway spend/budgets/caps, auto-top-up threshold, 402/out-of-credits, emails, admin balance/burn paid (price) → $ plan price, top-up purchase, auto-top-up amount, license, model list prices wire → USD API JSON fields and CLI --json unchanged; inputs convert credits ÷ 100 ``` - One formatter, `formatUsdAsCredits` (`packages/shared`): whole credits from 10, two decimals below, `<0.01` for a non-zero sub-cent turn. - The 402 message reads `Balance: 1,250 credits, required: 3 credits`. Web, mobile and Slack/Teams parse both the old `$` and the new form (`parseBalanceUsd`), so mixed versions coexist during a deploy. - Bugs fixed on the way: - mobile showed USD values as credits (a $12.50 balance read `13`); - the free-tier reset ledger row said `2 credits` for 200; - the ledger table showed raw USD under a "Credits" header. ### 2. Plan changes: instant upgrade, scheduled downgrade, preview first ```diff setPlan(monthly_usd) - cut → Stripe quantity now, plan_monthly_usd = new # UI showed the new price at once + cut → Stripe quantity now (no proration), plan_monthly_usd unchanged, + scheduled_monthly_usd = new, applied by the renewal # "Downgrade on Nov 16" + keep → the amount in effect again cancels a scheduled cut raise → charged now (prorated), credits added now + over a scheduled cut: restore the amount in effect first, then charge from it + result.change = raised (charged_usd, credits_added) | scheduled (effective_at) | kept | none +POST /v1/billing/plan/preview → { change, due_now_usd, credits_now, effective_at } (Stripe proration preview) +account-state.subscription.current_period_end (was always null → UI said "Active", never "Renews") +account-state.subscription.scheduled_change (credits cut: from/to monthly_usd, ISO effective_date) ``` The UI uses it: - **Upgrade:** "Pay $299.59 today … 29,959 credits are added now" and the button "Pay $299.59 and upgrade". - **Downgrade:** "No charge and no refund … until Nov 16" and the button "Downgrade on Nov 16". After it, a notice with "Keep current plan" and "→ $300/mo from " in the plan summary. - **Toasts** report what happened. SDK (additive): `previewBillingPlan`, `useBillingPlanPreview`, `PlanChange`, `PlanChangePreview`, and new optional fields on `SetBillingPlanResult`. Snapshot diff: 12 additions, 0 removals. ### 3. Production bug: the first renewal after a Checkout activation was skipped Stripe dates a `subscription_cycle` invoice by the period that **ended**. Its `invoice.period_start` is the instant activation already stored as `last_renewal_period_start`. So the renewal returned "already processed": the account got no monthly credits for month 2, and a scheduled cut was not applied. This dates from `58c7c1fbac` (2026-07-01). The fix keys the renewal on `invoice.period_end`, the start of the period it opens. A redelivered invoice stays idempotent: it has the same `period_end`, and `wallet.reset` is keyed on the invoice id. Learnings entry: `2026-10-15T235708Z-key-a-stripe-renewal-on-the-period-the-invoice-opens`. A read-only aggregate on prod shows affected accounts. The per-account audit against Stripe invoices, and any compensation, are a follow-up and are not in this PR. ## Evidence **Stripe test mode, test clock, synthetic account** (local stack; script drives the real API): | Step | Result | |---|---| | subscribe $100 | plan 100 | | raise → $300 | `raised`, charged $200, +20,000 credits | | cut → $100, then the `subscription.updated` webhook | `scheduled` for the renewal; DB `300.00 / 100.00`; plan still $300 | | keep $300 | `kept`; scheduled cleared | | cut → $100, then raise → $500 | preview and charge $200 (from $300, not $100) | | cut → $200, clock past the renewal | **before the fix:** renewal invoice paid, no ledger row, log `Renewal already processed`. **After:** plan 200, scheduled cleared, ledger `Monthly renewal: 20000 credits + 50000 rolled over` | **Browser** (agent-browser, local stack, same account): | Billing page | Upgrade preview | Downgrade scheduled | Credit ledger | |---|---|---|---| | ![billing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52cb5f22-cae1-48b2-84e2-89c0c0be9179) | ![raise](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6141a692-0013-4764-a975-e23f3087cd98) | ![cut](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af63959-aa2d-46a5-b4e9-7740405ab2e5) | ![ledger](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5edf5911-5e3d-4548-a149-15034ff90b6a) | - Upgrade click: `POST /v1/billing/plan` → 200. The toast read "Upgraded to $500 / month · Charged $299.59. 29,959 credits added." The balance went from 70,000 to 99,959 credits. - "Keep current plan": `POST /v1/billing/plan` → 200. The toast read "Plan kept"; the DB has `scheduled_monthly_usd` null. - Credit ledger: one browser pass caught a double conversion, which showed 100× amounts. It is fixed in `e3f262dc6d`. **Tests:** `pnpm test` on `f7d05f8c1a` (after merging `origin/dev` `baf07ba78c`): | Lane | Result | |---|---| | core: api-cli-flows | pass, including new BILL-20 | | route-coverage | 0 uncovered | | sdk, flow-runner-unit, worktree-unit | pass | | db-suites | 318/319. `tests/migration/credit-rpc-overloads.test.ts` "two concurrent grants" timed out under load (swap full). Alone: 14/14 pass in 6.8 s. The previous full run on this branch was 319/319. Not touched by this diff. | | packages | fails on tests that fail identically on `origin/dev` `baf07ba78c`: strict i18n audit (the same 10 Slack/Teams card findings, 0 unresolved keys), hero fold, 2× `isSettingsTabAllowed`, palette "apps", and 3 module-mock `SyntaxError`s (`sandbox-tab.empty-new`, `channels-view.email`, `model-consumers`). I reproduced the last three on a clean `origin/dev` checkout. | Per-file runs of the changed suites: - API: `set-plan` 24, `webhooks` 81, `renewal-rollover` 8, `account-state` 16, `account-write-owner` 16. - Shared formatter: 21. - SDK billing: 43 + 7 hooks; surface snapshots additive. - Web: billing 438, `plan-card` 23, admin 62, gateway 79, `audit-display-helpers` 50. - API, SDK and web `tsc`: 0 errors. API lint: clean. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way for code and UI. The migration only adds a nullable column (`credit_accounts.scheduled_monthly_usd`), which old code ignores. The renewal fix changes the meaning of `last_renewal_period_start` to "the period the last renewal opened". Old rows hold an earlier instant, so the next renewal still processes. A revert of the fix brings the first-renewal skip back. **Blast radius:** billing. - Every Stripe plan change and every renewal. - Every surface that shows a balance or a cost: web, mobile, CLI, emails. - The 402 message text. The parsers accept both formats. - Prod: the renewal fix should ship with the next release. That release also carries credits-only billing and the BYOK fee, so the customer notice goes out first. --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

Check that committed demos match the code they show (#297)

Record every demo with a fixed seed and store a fingerprint of its frames and render settings in demos.json. tests/test_demo_freshness.py re-records each demo on Linux with Python 3.10+ and fails, naming the re-render command, when code changes what a demo shows. All demos are re-rendered with the seed.

Closes #295

Hash characters by character_id so --seed reproduces every effect (#296)

EffectCharacter hashed by memory address, so active_characters ticked in a different order on each run and burn and thunderstorm drew their random numbers in a different order under the same seed.

Closes #294

Reuse 3D frame preparation and wireframe topology (#293)

## Resulting behavior

Reuse transformed/projected geometry within two-sided `Textured`
rendering and build immutable wireframe edge adjacency once, on first
use. Filled-only meshes pay no topology construction or retention cost.
Front/back fill buffers remain independent; camera, light, gradients and
body transforms are still read every step.

Closes #279

## Validation

1,706 focused tests passed on a combined checkout of this change and the
mount/lifecycle review fixes. Ruff formatting/lint, Pyright, pre-commit
hooks and the strict MkDocs build passed.

Measured against `e7e8d1d7` on Python 3.14.3 using the repository
harness: medium input, 80x24 canvas, centered text, 7 samples, 2
warmups, seed 1337. Traced-memory checks used 1 sample and no warmups
because tracing is expensive; their timings are not compared.

| Scenario | Build time | Render time | Total time | Peak traced memory
| Frames |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| globe | -5.58% | -8.80% | -8.80% | +5.02% | 481 |
| wireframes | -5.52% | -3.22% | -3.23% | +0.71% | 421 |

Both scenarios preserve frame counts, output lengths, and SHA-256
signatures:

- Globe: 481 frames, 7,886,754 characters,
`73c0b03a6e111469dae914ebab3a961b3dcc4e78534f82c910c384e3580b0b1c`.
- Wireframes: 421 frames, 3,667,814 characters,
`ca8eb98dba7126c2e4f9254fc0315b36b3e478a7d3f4a101fe0a8405046e6d75`.

Profiling found 960 transform/projection preparations for the globe's
480 animated frames; front/back rendering now shares those preparations.
Wireframe topology is also invariant across frames and is now built
once. Static-scene caching remains deferred: the moving examples offer
no static hits, and supporting mutable camera, light and gradients needs
a broader invalidation contract.

## Limitations

Results are local and advisory. Sharing front/back preparation retains
both fill buffers during the frame, accounting for the globe's
peak-memory increase. Edge adjacency retains memory proportional to a
mesh's edges only when used. No rendered-scene cache is introduced. CI
passed.

Add filled surface looks to Space3D bodies (#260)

## Resulting behavior

Before: a `Space3D` body could only carry the effect's own mounted
characters, which leave gaps on a solid.

After: `body.draw(look)` fills every covered cell of a body's shape. The
space draws surfaces with characters it creates and manages, one per
covered cell, so the effect's own characters are never used.

- Looks: `Shaded(gradient, symbols)`, `Solid(symbol, gradient)`,
`Textured(text=None, gradient, back="hide" | "dim", back_color)` and
`Wireframe(color, hidden_color)`. Gradients default to the TTE brand
colors.
- `body.draw(look, faces={tag: look})` gives faces their own looks.
`body.erase()` stops drawing, and `body.surface_characters` returns the
cells showing the body after the last step.
- Each `Space3D.step()` draws every drawn body into one depth buffer, so
overlapping bodies hide each other correctly. Pooled characters are
reused, cells a body leaves are hidden, and unchanged cells keep their
visual.
- Surface cells are layered by depth, one below a mounted character at
the same depth, so text mounted on a drawn body reads on top of it.
- `Textured` maps each face into the text at about one character per
cell for boxes, cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and spheres, starting
at the left edge of the front. Faces without a layout (caps, polyhedra,
torus) are shaded in `back_color`. With `back="dim"` the far side shows
through the text's spaces.

How: `geometry3d.rasterize` got faster without changing its results. It
skips faces that cover no cell center before transforming their normals,
works each triangle's barycentric weights out once per row, and reuses
`Coord` objects through a bounded cache. `Body` caches shading per face,
and the space caches `ColorPair`s so unchanged cells are found by
identity.

Closes #259

## Validation

- `pytest -n auto tests/engine_tests tests/utils_tests
tests/effects_tests`: 7970 passed, with 23 new surface tests and a
geometry3d cache test.
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check` and `pyright` pass on the touched
files. `mkdocs build --strict` passes.
- Per-frame cost of `Space3D.step()` with one body turning, on an 80x24
canvas (Python 3.13, one core):

| Body and look | Per frame | Cells drawn |
|---|---|---|
| `Cube(24)` `Shaded` | 2.3 ms | 420 |
| `Sphere(12)` `Shaded` | 3.1 ms | 232 |
| `Torus(14, 5)` `Shaded` | 5.0 ms | 340 |
| `Prism(6, 14, 14)` `Textured` | 2.0 ms | 278 |
| `Cylinder(14, 12)` `Textured(back="dim")` | 3.5 ms | 284 |
| `Cube(24)` `Wireframe` | 0.7 ms | 151 |

## Limitations

- Cost follows mesh faces more than covered cells. The default sphere
and torus have about one face per cell, so the torus costs about 5 ms a
frame. Filling spheres and cylinders analytically per cell, and picking
tessellation from projected size, would cut this. Both were left out of
scope in #259 and can come in their own issue.
- Text on a face seen at a steep angle skips letters, because each cell
samples one text character.

Clip exported glyphs to their cells so cleared cells leave no specks (#245)

## Resulting behavior

Before: GIF and WebP exports and the docs demos (for example

terminals clip glyphs. Drawing only changed cells now matches drawing
every frame from scratch exactly. The widest glyphs (`#`, `%`, `W`) lose
under a pixel of faint edge. Glyph masks are cached, and all 77 docs
demos are re-rendered (84.4 MB, down from 86.1 MB).

fix(llms): send max_completion_tokens for gpt-6 ids on OpenAI-compatible endpoints (#15137)

The reasoning-era model-id matcher only covered o1/o3/o4 and gpt-5, so
gpt-6 requests (gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-6-1-sol) kept max_tokens and
OpenAI/Azure rejected them. Widen the gpt pattern to gpt-5 through gpt-9,
keeping the version digit single so Azure's gpt-35-turbo stays out.

chore(vscode): fix integration test runner on macOS (#15088)

* chore(vscode): fix integration test runner on macOS

Bump @vscode/test-electron to 3.1.0, which resolves the macOS executable
from Info.plist. VS Code 1.110+ renamed Contents/MacOS/Electron to Code
and dropped the compatibility symlink, so 2.5.2 failed every run with
`spawn .../Contents/MacOS/Electron ENOENT`.

Also pass a short --user-data-dir on macOS. VS Code puts its IPC socket
in the user data dir, and the default .vscode-test/user-data overflows
the 103-char unix socket limit from deep checkouts such as worktrees
(`listen EINVAL ... 1.14-main.sock`). Linux and Windows keep the default.

* test(vscode): drop the macOS E2E executable fallback

@vscode/test-electron 3.1.0 resolves the macOS executable from the app
bundle's Info.plist for both Stable and Insiders, so downloadAndUnzipVSCode
now returns Contents/MacOS/Code directly and the Code / Code - Insiders
fallback never runs.

The Cloud sessions copy said "your editor". Name the editor the user is
actually in instead: "VS Code", "Cursor", "PyCharm" and so on.

The extension already gets the product name from the host bridge
(getHostVersion's platform); fetch it once and pass it to the webview as

JetBrains edition, "Visual Studio Code" -> "VS Code") and falls back to

HostRegistryInfo already holds getHostVersion's platform from startup, so

test now asserts the visible text instead of reusing the function it tests.

fix(prompt-management): expose global prompts from editors (#21673)

<!-- Template from
https://github.com/kubevirt/kubevirt/blob/main/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md?-->

### What this PR does

Before this PR:

The Agent and Assistant editor prompt tabs listed only linked prompts,
so global prompts available in the composer appeared missing and had no
management path from the editor.

After this PR:

The prompt tabs identify the current Agent/Assistant scope, explain
where global prompts are managed, and show a persistent Manage Global
Prompts button, including for an empty linked list. It opens Settings →
Prompts only after the editor has saved its current values and
successfully closed. Failed saves and invalid required names keep edits
visible. Edits made during a pending close cancel that navigation
attempt; repeated management clicks wait for outstanding writes and
persist any reversion to the original values before navigating. Explicit
Close retains the existing failed-edit discard option. Composer behavior
and prompt visibility/binding rules are unchanged.

<!-- (optional, in `fixes #<issue number>(, fixes #<issue_number>, ...)`
format, will close the issue(s) when PR gets merged)*: -->

Fixes #19754

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

The following tradeoffs were made:

Keep the existing scoped list and link to the existing settings
management surface. Navigation stays in each edit dialog and is passed
to the shared tab as a callback. The close-before-action hook accepts
asynchronous close results and skips navigation when closure is refused.
The autosave hook exposes its pending drain so both editors await
outstanding writes before checking whether the current form is
unchanged. Both persist from live form values and advance their saved
baselines on successful writes; the Assistant baseline uses a captured
form snapshot rather than waiting for a resource refetch. After
flushing, closure rechecks both the form snapshot and its remaining
diff. This preserves reversions and prevents an unchanged-form shortcut
from bypassing an in-flight write.

The following alternatives were considered:

Showing global and linked prompts together would require distinguishing
management and binding actions in the same list. The existing settings
page already supports scope badges and editing.

Links to places where the discussion took place: <!-- optional: slack,
other GH issue, mailinglist, ... -->

https://github.com/CherryHQ/cherry-studio/issues/19754

fix(doc): read the text boxes, footnotes and endnotes of a legacy .doc (#20636)

### What

Both places that read a legacy binary `.doc` keep only the body:

```ts
const extracted = await new WordExtractor().extract(buffer)
return extracted.getBody().trim()      // attachmentTextExtraction.ts
const text = extracted.getBody().trim()  // DocReader.ts
```

A `.doc` does not keep everything in the body stream. Text boxes,
footnotes and
endnotes live in streams of their own, and `word-extractor` exposes each
of them
(`getTextboxes()`, `getFootnotes()`, `getEndnotes()`). Word puts all of
them on
the page, so a reader that takes the body alone silently drops every
callout,
pull quote, sidebar and footnote.

Measured against word-extractor's own test fixtures:

| fixture | kept today | dropped today |
|---|---|---|
| `test16.doc` | `Text box document test`, `Paragraph 1..3` | `First
text box, regular`, `A shape with text inside`, the linked second/third
boxes, `Vertical text box added too`, `Header box 1`, `Header box 2` |
| `test13.doc` | `Endnotes and footnotes test`, `Paragraph 1..2` | `This
is a footnote`, `This is an endnote` |

Six text boxes out of a six-text-box document, and both notes out of a
document
whose title is "Endnotes and footnotes test". Nothing is logged; the
knowledge
base just never sees that text.

It is also inconsistent with the sibling formats: `.docx` goes through
mammoth,
which renders footnotes, so the same document saved in the newer format
keeps
what the older one loses.

### How

One shared helper, `src/main/utils/legacyDoc.ts`, used by both call
sites (they
already pointed at each other in a comment). It appends the three extra
streams
to the body.

Two things stay out, deliberately:

- **Comments** (`getAnnotations()`) — remarks *about* the document
rather than
  part of it.
- **Headers and footers** — they repeat page furniture on every page. A
text box
*anchored* in a header is kept: `getTextboxes()` returns it once rather
than
  once per page, and a banner or a sidebar is content.

### Tests

`src/main/utils/__tests__/legacyDoc.test.ts` — text boxes are kept,
footnotes and
endnotes are kept, a body-only document is unchanged, and an empty
document still
yields `''`. The existing `.doc` case in
`attachmentTextExtraction.test.ts` grew
the extra streams.

```
$ vitest run --project main src/main/utils/__tests__/legacyDoc.test.ts \
    src/main/ai/messages/__tests__/attachmentTextExtraction.test.ts
Tests  16 passed (16)

# same tests with the helper returning getBody() only
× keeps the text boxes, which a .doc stores outside the body
× keeps the footnotes and endnotes
× extracts .doc via word-extractor (buffer)
Tests  3 failed | 13 passed (16)
```

The two that pass on both sides are the guards: a body-only document
must not
grow separators, and an empty one must still be empty.

The two fixtures above were also run through the real helper (no mocks)
while
preparing this, which is where the table comes from; they are not
committed,
since the unit tests cover the behaviour without carrying binaries into
the repo.

`oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json` are
clean.

chore(deps): cargo update and bump zip to 9 for the symlink advisory (#14577)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/813
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`zip` before 9.0.0 applies Unix permissions through extracted symlinks
without checking the target stays inside the destination
(GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp). mise extracts downloaded `.zip` tool archives
with `ZipArchive::extract` (`mise_util::file::unzip`), so this moves
mise's own `zip` dependency to 9.x. `cargo deny check` was failing on
the advisory in CI for every open PR.

Per the maintainer's call this PR also runs a full `cargo update` rather
than keeping the lockfile focused. It is run with
`CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_RUST_VERSIONS=allow` so the resolver does
not fall back to older Rust-1.88-compatible crates (a plain `cargo
update` downgraded `aws-sdk-s3` and pulled in an `lru` version with
RUSTSEC-2026-0253). Changes beyond the lockfile:

- `zip` 8 → 9 in the three manifests that declare it. `ZipFile::name()`
now returns a `Result`, so the two SLSA content-check errors that print
an entry name fall back to `<unreadable name>`.
- `rattler` 0.53 → 0.54 and `rattler_conda_types` 0.56 → 0.57, which the
updated `rattler_solve` requires. The conda backend's test helper builds
a `PackageRecord` with the new `BuildString` type.

`xx` is now 2.6.3, which uses zip 9 (jdx/xx#308, #310). `zip` 8.6.0 (via
aube and ubi) and 7.x (via `zipsign-api`) remain in the lockfile where
those crates still pin them; mise does not call their zip extraction.
aube's own bump is jdx/aube#1756 and needs a release before mise can
pick it up.

Validated with clippy (`-D warnings`, `--locked`), the conda and
`mise-util` tests, and a clean `cargo deny check` (advisories, bans,
licenses, sources) with a fresh advisory db.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/815
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Renovate's runs on this repo report `Package lookup failures` for the
perf-runner image (`Could not determine new digest for update`). The
perf workflows pin the image by digest only, so Renovate looks for the
`latest` tag, which `jdx/perf-runner` never publishes (it only pushes
`jdx-perf-v1`), and gets a 404.

The pin now names the published tag as well:

```yaml
image: ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner:jdx-perf-v1@sha256:5263c143…
```

The digest is unchanged, so the image the perf jobs run does not change.
Renovate can now follow the `jdx-perf-v1` tag and open a PR when the
image is rebuilt.

The shared preset automerges digest updates, so this also adds a package
rule that turns automerge off for `ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner`. A rebuilt
image changes the toolchain every perf baseline is measured on, and that
should go through the perf check, not merge on its own.

The `image:` strings that the workflows echo into the report are left as
they were.

Internal change that prepares `system/packages` (about 38k lines of
system package managers) to move into its own crate. Behavior is
unchanged.

Until now the package managers imported mise's config, toolset, and
plugin code directly, so they could not live below those. They now
depend only on `mise-util`, `mise-settings`, and `mise-ui`, plus one
explicit seam, `packages::host`, that mise fills in at startup:

- provisioning ruby for source builds and cask scripts
(`provision_ruby`, `installed_ruby`);
- finding a configured tool, used by `mas` (`tool_bin`);
- listing and loading package plugins (`package_plugin_names`,
`load_package_plugin`).

The implementations live in `src/system/packages_host.rs`.

## Other moves

- `ManagerPackageOptions`, `AppSpec`, `validate_app_declaration`, and
`brew_tap_name` move from `system` into `packages::options`; `system`
re-exports them, so callers are unchanged.
- The package-plugin manager moves from `packages::plugin` to
`system::package_plugin`. It needs `Config` and the toolset, so it stays
in mise.
- The `remove_by!` guard for the apt keyring cleanup moves next to the
re-exports in `system/mod.rs`. It compares against the version of the
crate it expands in, so it has to stay in mise once `packages` moves
out.

fix(vfox): pass each version only its own tool options (#14562)

When a `vfox:` tool lists several versions, each one is meant to get its
own tool options. An option that only the first entry sets reached the
other versions' plugin hooks too:

```toml
[tools]
"vfox:file:///path/to/plugin" = [
  { version = "1.0.0", extensions = "a" },
  { version = "2.0.0" },
]
```

While `2.0.0` was installing, its hooks saw
`MISE_TOOL_OPTS__EXTENSIONS=a`. With the second entry on its own, the
variable is unset.

The vfox backend built the options for a version's hooks from the
config's options for the tool, then layered the version's own request
options over them. The config lookup always took the first entry, so any
option a later entry left out came from the first one. The config layer
is now the entry for that version, picked the way mise already matches a
version named on the command line to its config entry
(`configured_options_for_runtime_request`). When no entry matches, the
first one is still used, as before.

The config layer stays because some paths have no options of their own.
`mise uninstall vfox:…@1.0.0` builds its request from the argument
alone, and the plugin's uninstall hook still needs the options
configured for `1.0.0`. Dropping the config layer broke that case in
`test_vfox_tool_options`.

#14537 fixes the same problem for `github:`. `http:` and `s3:` already
install from each version's own options.

## Validation

- New `e2e/backend/test_vfox_multi_entry_options`: a local plugin
records `MISE_TOOL_OPTS__EXTENSIONS` per version, with `extensions` set
on `1.0.0` only.

2026.10.11 (`2.0.0` sees `opentelemetry`) and passes with this branch.
`test_vfox_tool_options`, `test_vfox_install_env` and
`test_vfox_pre_uninstall` pass too.
- `backend::vfox`, `toolset::tool_request_set` and `config` unit tests
pass, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets
-- -D warnings`.
- `test_vfox_backend_npm` fails in that container with both the released
binary and this branch, because the container has no `npm`.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/794

`[bootstrap.repos]` could not vary a checkout by branch, and every clone
was a full one. Now `url` and `ref` render as templates, like the
checkout path already does, and `filter`, `depth` and `submodules` shape
the first clone.

```toml
[vars]
branch = "main"

[bootstrap.repos]
"~/src/large" = { url = "git@github.com:example/large.git", ref = "{{ vars.branch }}", filter = "blob:none", depth = 1 }
```

`mise bootstrap repos apply` then runs `git clone --branch main
--filter=blob:none --depth 1 …`. Previously the literal `{{ vars.branch
}}` went to git, and `filter`/`depth` were ignored with an "unknown
field" warning.

- `url` and `ref` render from `[vars]` or the process environment
(`env.NAME`); values set in a config's `[env]` table are not available,
as with the checkout path. `exec()` is still unavailable, and reading a
var never prompts.
- `filter` is passed as `--filter=<spec>`, `depth` as `--depth <n>`, and
`submodules = true` as `--recurse-submodules`.
- These options affect only the first clone; an existing checkout keeps
the shape it was cloned with.
- `depth` must be at least 1 and cannot be combined with a commit SHA or
`refs/…` `ref`, which a shallow clone can't check out. An empty or
`-`-prefixed `filter` is rejected.
- `lfs` from the discussion is not included; it needs git-lfs and
separate handling.

fix(deps): rerun providers when mise recreates the venv (#14532)

With `python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source"` (or `_.python.venv = {
create = true }`), deleting `.venv` left the uv, pip and poetry deps
providers fresh once mise recreated the venv in a later process, such as
shell activation or `mise env`. `uv sync` never ran, so the new venv
stayed empty, and `[deps.uv] auto = true` did not catch it either.

```toml
[settings]
python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source"

[deps.uv]
auto = true
```

```console
$ rm -rf .venv
$ mise env >/dev/null   # recreates an empty .venv
$ mise deps install uv --explain
```

- Before: `Status: fresh (outputs are up to date)`, and `mise x --
python -c 'import six'` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- After: `Status: stale (output created since the last run)`, and `mise
x` runs `uv sync` first.

The marker for a venv that mise created lived in memory (#7770), so only
the process that created the venv saw it. It is now a file under
`$MISE_STATE_DIR/deps/stale-outputs/` holding a generation. Each
provider that tracks the venv records the generation it ran against in
its deps state, and stays stale until it has run against the current
one. With `status.show_deps_stale` on, shell activation now warns after
it creates a venv, until deps runs.

Tradeoffs: markers are never deleted, one small file per venv path mise
has created. After a manual `uv sync`, the next `mise deps` reruns the
provider once.

## Validation

- Locally: the e2e test `test_deps_venv_created_by_mise` passes. It
covers a venv recreated in a later process, and two providers sharing it
that run separately.
- CI: the build, lint and e2e jobs pass, and so do the Windows unit,
lint and e2e jobs.
