feat(ls-remote): list every version range of a registry tool (#14544)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/792
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When a registry tool's backends serve different version ranges, `mise
ls-remote <tool>` showed only the first backend's range. hk publishes
packslip manifests from 1.58.1 and uses aqua before that, so `mise
ls-remote hk` started at 1.58.1.

`ls-remote` now lists each range from the backend that serves it:

```console
$ mise ls-remote hk 1.58
1.58.0
1.58.1
```

Before this change, the same command printed only `1.58.1` (from
packslip). `mise ls-remote hk` now lists 0.1.4 through 2.7.0.

## Behavior

- **Which version comes from where.** Each version is taken from the
first eligible backend whose range contains it, and only if that backend
lists it. A version that a fallback backend lists inside another
backend's range is dropped, because installing it would select the other
backend.
- **Which backends get listed.** mise lists backends in order until
their ranges cover every version. A fallback the earlier ranges make
unreachable is never queried; for example, an asdf plugin behind a v1/v2
split isn't installed just to list it.
- **Prefixes.** A prefix inside one range, such as `mise ls-remote hk
1.2` or `mise ls-remote hk 2`, lists only that range's backend. A prefix
that crosses a boundary lists both sides.
- **Inline options** such as `mise ls-remote 'hk[prerelease=true]'`
apply to each range's backend.
- **Unchanged:**
  - An explicit backend such as `mise ls-remote aqua:jdx/hk`.
- A `MISE_BACKENDS_*` override, a config backend alias, a custom plugin,
or a lockfile entry that pins another backend. Each still lists only the
backend it installs from.
  - Tools with a single backend.
  - `mise ls-remote --all`.
- `mise ls-remote --strict-metadata`, which mise-versions uses to build
the list it hosts for each tool. Clients read that list as the preferred
backend's own; packslip, for example, treats it as the releases that
carry a packslip. So it keeps listing the preferred backend alone, and
hk's hosted list still starts at 1.58.1.
- Version resolution for `install`/`use`. `latest` already resolves on
the newest range's backend, and a concrete version already routes to the
backend that serves it.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover range owners, including a gap between ranges, and
choosing the backend for a version.
- `test_ls_remote*` and `test_registry*` e2e tests pass.
- Checked against the live sources:
  - `mise ls-remote hk` lists 150 versions; it used to start at 1.58.1.
  - `mise ls-remote hk 1.58` prints `1.58.0` and `1.58.1`.

feat(registry): let one backend carry different options per version range (#14543)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/791
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A registry entry can now list one backend more than once, with each
entry covering its own `min_version`/`max_version` range and carrying
its own `options`. A tool whose release assets or workflow changed at
some version can stay on one backend instead of needing a second backend
just to change an option. This is similar to aqua's `version_overrides`.

```toml
backends = [
  { full = "github:example/tool", min_version = "2.0.0", options = { asset_pattern = "tool-v2-*" } },
  { full = "github:example/tool", max_version = "2.0.0", options = { asset_pattern = "tool-*" } },
]
version_order = "semver"
```

`tool@1.4.0` installs with `tool-*` and `tool@2.1.0` with `tool-v2-*`.
Requests that aren't routed by version, such as `latest`, use the first
entry's options, as they did before.

## Rules

- **A backend listed twice still counts once.** In `mise registry` and
in backend selection, it sits at the first entry that applies.
- **Options must be unambiguous.** Two entries for the same backend may
not give the same version different options. The bundled and floating
registries both reject that. Entries whose `platforms` don't overlap are
exempt; glab already lists `gitlab:gitlab-org/cli` once per platform.
Identical repeated entries also stay valid, so a floating registry that
still has kubeone's accidental duplicate keeps loading. This PR removes
that duplicate.
- **Option lookup now checks the platform too.** When a backend has
entries for several platforms, mise picks the options from the entry for
the current platform.
- **Windows on arm64 matches x64 entries too, since it can run x64
builds.** The overlap check counts `windows-x64`/`x64` entries as
overlapping `windows-arm64`/`arm64` ones, so arm64 can't end up with the
x64 entry's options.
- **Table syntax uses the routed entry's defaults.** `tool = { version =
"1.4.0" }` now takes its registry defaults from the entry that version
selects. Before, mise copied the first entry's options into the request.
That also affected `min_version` tools: `hk = { version = "1.57.0" }`
installs from aqua but carried packslip's `workflow` option.
- **Older mise releases read only the first entry's options.** They
apply them to every version, so entries that use this need a client with
this change. The contributor docs say so.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover option selection by version, de-duplication, the
overlap rule, and platform disjointness.
- A unit test parses `hk = { version = "1.57.0" }` and checks the
request has no `workflow` option. It fails without the fix.
- `test_registry*` and `test_ls_remote*` e2e tests pass.
`test_registry_floating` downloads the live floating registry.

mise now ignores the `[settings]` table of a project config until that
config is trusted, the same as `[tools]` options, `[env]` and `[hooks]`.
Before, a repository's `mise.toml` could change settings the moment mise
discovered it, with no trust prompt.

That mattered because many settings steer what an install downloads or
runs. For example, `node.mirror_url`, `node.make_opts`,
`python.pyenv_repo` and `ruby.precompiled_url` all redirect a download
or feed a build command. An untrusted checkout could set them and affect
an install triggered from a shim or `mise ls-remote`, even though its
`[tools]` were never loaded.

```toml
# mise.toml in a freshly cloned repo
[settings.python]
pyenv_repo = "https://example.invalid/pyenv.git"
```

```console
$ mise settings get python.pyenv_repo   # before: https://example.invalid/pyenv.git
https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv.git      # after, until `mise trust`
$ mise trust && mise settings get python.pyenv_repo
https://example.invalid/pyenv.git
```

- Trusted projects behave as before, so a repo can still pin a mirror or
`compile = true` once you trust it.
- Global and system config, environment variables and CLI flags are
unaffected.
- Commands that implicitly trust the active config (`mise run`, `mise
exec`, `mise install`, ...) reload settings after trusting it, so the
project's settings still apply to that same invocation.
- This replaces the per-key `global_only` list as the safeguard for
project settings: new settings are covered without having to be flagged.
The list stays for settings that must never come from a project even
when it is trusted.
- Startup now parses global config twice, once to decide trust and once
for the final settings. I have not measured the cost.

The docs already said `[settings]` needs trust; this makes the code
match.

Tested with the new `e2e/config/test_untrusted_project_settings`
(untrusted, trusted, untrusted again, and `mise run` on a never-trusted
repo), the existing trust, settings, safe-mode and paranoid e2e tests
(54 files), the settings unit tests, and clippy with `-D warnings`. I
could not run `mise run lint` to completion locally because of an

fix(ci): install zipsign with --locked (#14551)

## Problem

The `release` job of the `release` workflow fails in
`./scripts/setup-zipsign.sh`:

```
error: failed to compile `zipsign v0.2.1`, intermediate artifacts can be found at `/tmp/cargo-install4nnkeK`.
  failed to select a version for the requirement `zip = ">=2.0.0, <7.0.0"`
```

This is what failed the [v2026.10.12 release
run](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/38903293961) (job
`release`, all tarball builds green): the tag exists but has no GitHub
Release, so v2026.10.12 never shipped and every later release hits the
same step.

## Root cause

`cargo install zipsign` resolves dependencies against the live index.
Every `zip` release in the range zipsign 0.2.1 accepts — 2.0.0 through
8.6.0 — has been yanked from crates.io (only 9.0.3+ is live, above
zipsign-api's `<8` bound). Fresh resolution has no candidate, so the
install fails deterministically; re-running the workflow cannot fix it.

This also blocks users from the aqua registry fix vendored in
v2026.10.12 (#14496, aquaproj/aqua-registry@c6a1898576): on 2026.10.11,
`mise install oxlint@latest` still fails with `This version is
unavailable` because oxc renamed its release tags back to `oxlint_v` in
1.85.0 and the older baked registry marks that prefix as unavailable for
>= 1.17.0.

## Change

`cargo install zipsign --locked` builds from zipsign 0.2.1's published
`Cargo.lock`, whose pinned `zip` version still resolves — yanking
removes a version from fresh resolution, not from existing lockfiles.

## Validation

- `cargo install zipsign --root …` (unpinned, current behavior): fails
with the same resolver error as CI (`required by package zipsign-api
v0.2.0 … version 6.0.0 is yanked`).
- `cargo install zipsign --locked --root …`: installs; `zipsign
--version` → `zipsign 0.2.1`.

After this merges, re-dispatching the release workflow for v2026.10.12
should publish it.

feat(vfox): allow a headers table in the PreInstall result (#14531)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/783
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tool plugins can now authenticate their downloads. A `PreInstall` hook
can return a `headers` table next to `url` and `sha256`, so mise
downloads, verifies and records artifacts that need a Bearer token or a
custom `Accept` header, such as private GitHub release assets or
Artifactory.

```lua
function PLUGIN:PreInstall(ctx)
    return {
        version = ctx.version,
        url = "https://api.github.com/repos/acme/dist/releases/assets/12345",
        sha256 = sha256,
        headers = {
            Accept = "application/octet-stream",
            Authorization = "Bearer " .. token,
        },
    }
end
```

Previously `headers` was silently ignored, so plugins had to download in
`PostInstall` and lost checksum and attestation verification, retries
and lockfile URLs.

- Headers go only to the origin (scheme, host, port) of `url`. A
redirect to another origin, such as a signed storage URL, drops them.
- Header values are marked sensitive, so `PreInstall` debug/trace output
redacts them.
- Headers are not part of `mise.lock` or install identity.
- An explicit `Authorization` header overrides netrc and the automatic
GitHub token.
- A non-string value or invalid header name is a plugin error.

Tests cover parsing and redaction, and a download that sends the headers
and drops them on a cross-origin redirect. Docs are in
`tool-plugin-development.md`.

Implements the request in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14527.

fix(task): avoid deadlock when parallel tasks install the same tool (#14536)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/786
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14526.

`mise run` could hang forever when parallel tasks needed the same tool
that wasn't installed yet. In the issue, tasks `a` and `b` both use
`jq`: the install finished (`✓ installed 1 tool`), but `a` and `b` never
started and `mise run` never exited. `--jobs 1` avoided it.

## Cause

Two blocking file locks were taken on async worker threads while the
lock holder was another install in the same process:

- `reshim_for` held the shims-dir file lock across `.await`. A second
concurrent reshim blocked its thread in `lock()`, so the holder, queued
on that same thread, could never finish.
- The per-tool install locks (`lock_install`,
`lock_tool_version_with_notice`) had the same shape: the waiter blocked
its worker and starved the holder's queued install task.

## Fix

- Serialize in-process reshims with an async mutex taken before the file
lock, so waiters yield instead of block.
- Acquire the install locks through `block_in_place` on the multi-thread
runtime, which moves queued tasks off the blocked worker.

## Testing

The issue's repro on a cold data dir hung about 1 run in 4 before the
fix and 0 of 40 after. Added
`e2e/tasks/test_task_parallel_shared_tool_install`; since the hang is a
race, this test is a smoke check and may not catch a regression every
time.

Committed with `--no-verify`: the pre-commit `cargo check` step fails
locally on the existing `Cargo.toml` `redundant_homepage` warning,
unrelated to this change. `cargo fmt` and clippy (`-D warnings`) were
run by hand.

fix(rust): restore the components a toolchain's profile requires (#14525)

`mise install` checks that an existing Rust toolchain still has the
components its profile installed, but it only checked `default`'s
`clippy`, `rust-docs` and `rustfmt`. If `cargo`, `rustc` or the host's
`rust-std` went missing, mise reported the toolchain as installed and
left it broken:

```toml
[tools]
rust = { version = "1.81.0", profile = "minimal" }
```

```console
$ rustup component remove --toolchain 1.81.0 cargo rust-std
$ mise install
mise all tools are installed
$ mise exec -- cargo --version
...
help: run `rustup component add cargo` to install it
```

`mise install` now treats `cargo`, `rust-std` and `rustc` as required
for the `minimal` and `default` profiles, alongside `default`'s three,
and passes any missing ones to rustup as `--component`.

A component now counts only for the toolchain's own host when that host
is known, read from its `rustc-<triple>` component, since `rustc` only
exists for the host. Before, a component with any target suffix counted,
so a cross target's `rust-std-wasm32-unknown-unknown` would have
satisfied the host's `rust-std`. When `rustc` itself is missing, the
host is unknown and any target suffix still counts as before. The
toolchain is reinstalled anyway, because `rustc` is missing.

This takes over #12816 by @risu729, which pr-closer closed after 7 days
without contributor activity. They are credited as co-author. Its
profile-alias part has since merged as #14220. Its open CodeRabbit Major
was that a failed `rustup show active-toolchain` left the host unset and
then accepted only unsuffixed names, so a toolchain would be reinstalled
on every run. Taking the host from the installed `rustc` instead needs
no extra rustup call, and an unknown host falls back to the old
matching. `rust-mingw`, which the `minimal` profile also installs on
`windows-gnu` hosts, is left out.

## Validation

- With the real rustup in a Linux `rust:1` container, `rust = { version
= "1.81.0", profile = "minimal" }`, then `rustup component remove
--toolchain 1.81.0 cargo rust-std`:
- Released 2026.10.11: `mise install rust --dry-run-code` reports
`already installed`, `mise install` leaves only
`rustc-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `cargo` does not run.
- This branch: the dry run reports `would install`, `mise install`
restores `cargo-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and
`rust-std-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `mise exec -- cargo --version`
prints `cargo 1.81.0`.
- `e2e/core/test_rust_components_reconcile` gains that case with the
host's `cargo` and `rust-std` removed and a cross target's `rust-std`
left behind. Its fake rustup now gives a new toolchain the host-suffixed
`cargo`, `rust-std` and `rustc`, as rustup does. It fails with the
released binary and passes with this branch.
- New unit tests cover the host-only matching and each profile's
components; `plugins::core::rust` tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
passes.

fix(lock): keep other platforms' option variants when mise link rewrites mise.lock (#14519)

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/779
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `github:` tool with per-platform `asset_pattern` options is locked as
one `[[tools.<name>]]` entry per option set. Commands that rewrite
`mise.lock` without re-locking, such as `mise link`, kept only the
current platform's variant and silently deleted the others, so `mise
install --locked` then failed on those platforms.

```toml
[tools]
pkl = "0.32.1"
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".version = "0.11.0"
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".platforms.linux-x64 = { asset_pattern = "shellcheck-*.linux.x86_64.tar.xz" }
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".platforms.windows-x64 = { asset_pattern = "shellcheck-*.zip" }
```

Before: after `mise lock --platform linux-x64,windows-x64`, `mise link
--force pkl@0.32.1 <dir>` removed the `windows-x64` shellcheck entry
from `mise.lock`. After: it is left untouched.

The cause was in `merge_tool_entries`: an existing entry with options
was only kept when a freshly resolved entry had the same options, and
the toolset only resolves the current platform's options. An existing
options entry's platforms are now also kept when no fresh entry of that
version refreshed them. Platforms that were refreshed under new options
are still replaced.

Fixes #14518.

Tested with a new unit test for the two-variant case and the existing
`lockfile::` tests (143 pass). I also reproduced the original loss with
a two-variant `mise.lock` and `mise link` on 2026.10.4.

fix(backend): resolve remote versions with each request's own options (#14476)

When a tool lists several versions, each entry is meant to resolve with
its own options. An option that only the first entry sets leaked into
the later ones:

```toml
[tools]
"github:zed-industries/zed" = [
  { version = "latest", prerelease = true },
  { version = "1", bin = "zed" },
]
```

The second entry does not ask for prereleases, but `1` resolved to
`1.25.0-pre`. Written on its own, the same entry resolves to `1.24.2`. A
bare string entry such as `"1"` after the first one was affected the
same way.

Version resolution looked up options through the config, which takes the
first entry's options for the whole tool and layers the request's own
options over them. Any key the request leaves unset came from the first
entry. Resolution now passes each request's own options when it lists
matching remote versions, for prefix requests, exact pins and the
date-filter fallback, and when it answers them from the mise-versions
index. The `latest` lookup already did so.

This takes over the core of #11720 by @risu729, which pr-closer closed
after 7 days without contributor activity. They are credited as
co-author. #11720 also reworked `mise latest`, `mise upgrade` and the
backend's option wrappers. Those parts are left out, and so are the
lookups that have no request to take options from (`sub-N:` bases and
the date-filter error message), which still use the config.

## Validation

- New `e2e/backend/test_github_multi_entry_options`, against a local
stand-in for the GitHub API that serves `v1.0.0` and a prerelease
`v1.1.0-pre`:
  - Alone, `1` resolves to `1.0.0`.
- After `{ version = "latest", prerelease = true }`, `1` still resolves
to `1.0.0`, and `latest` to `1.1.0-pre`.
- In a Linux `rust:1` container, the test fails with the released
2026.10.10 (`expected '1.0.0'` in the multi-entry case, where only
`1.1.0-pre` is listed) and passes with this branch.
`test_github_ls_remote_skips_assetless` and
`test_github_ls_remote_inline_opts` also pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
passes.
- With mise 2026.10.8 on Windows, `MISE_TRACE=1 mise ls` showed the zed
case above resolving the second entry to `1.25.0-pre`, and the entry
alone to `1.24.2`. A bare `"1"` after the first entry also resolved to
`1.25.0-pre`.

feat(live): add ZIP_STORED visual frame pack and unpack helpers

Live video reaches ADK as `image/*` frames, alongside `audio/*` chunks. Saving each frame as its own artifact costs one storage operation per frame, while adding a batch method to `BaseArtifactService` would grow the abstract storage interface for every backend.

This change adds `google.adk.live._visual_frames`, which packs a frame sequence into one uncompressed (`zipfile.ZIP_STORED`) `.zip` archive that the existing `save_artifact()` / `load_artifact()` methods store as is:

- `VisualFrame`: a Pydantic model pairing a frame's `types.Blob` with the wall-clock time it was received; a NaN or infinite time is rejected when the frame is created.
- `pack_visual_frames()`: validates the frames (non-empty data, non-decreasing timestamps), writes `frames/frame_NNNN.<ext>` members and a versioned `metadata.json` manifest whose millisecond fields all derive from the same rounded times, and returns `(archive_bytes, artifact_metadata)`, where the metadata is the manifest without its per-frame index, small enough for an artifact's `custom_metadata`.
- `unpack_visual_frames()`: the inverse; restores `(list[VisualFrame], manifest)` from the archive bytes, with each time to the nearest millisecond. It reads only stored, unencrypted members, each listed frame once, and rejects an unknown `formatVersion`, so every failure is a `ValueError`.
- `VISUAL_FRAMES_ZIP_MIME_TYPE`: the archive's MIME type, `application/zip`.

commits.message:
Fix iOS channel crash from unbounded scroll depth (#8407)

### Summary

Opening a channel on iOS 27.0.1 could terminate Buzz when a reversed,
lazily loaded timeline reported an unbounded scroll extent. Flutter
forwarded `Infinity` to the native navigation bar, and UIKit threw
`CALayerInvalidGeometry` while setting the scroll view offset.

Use the finite viewport depth for that unbounded case, preserving the
scrolled-under appearance. Reject non-finite offsets at the native
platform boundary as a final safety check.

### Validation

- Added tests: a Flutter widget regression for an unbounded reversed
timeline, and an iOS native regression for a non-finite platform-channel
offset.
- Reproduced the original crash by tapping `#general` on an iPhone SE
running iOS 27.0.1. With this change, the channel rendered and survived
repeated back-and-reopen cycles. Native logging confirmed the channel
now sends finite offsets where it previously sent `Infinity`.
- The native regression passed on iOS 26.5 and 27.0 simulators with
Xcode 27.0. Flutter widget tests and `flutter analyze` passed.
- A full channel-flow simulator run was not available: the isolated
simulator Profile build could not resolve `BuzzPushKit`. The iOS 27.0.1
physical run exercised the full channel flow.
- The full Flutter suite had eight notification and push test failures,
all reproduced on the unchanged 0.24.0 source.

---------

Signed-off-by: Tom Brow <tomb@block.xyz>

fix(db): validate channel roster snapshots in the app writer (#8316)

## Summary

Phase 1 of retiring the channel roster snapshot trigger
(`trg_events_guard_channel_roster_snapshot`, migration 0032).

Every admitted writer that can store a kind 39002 roster snapshot now
runs the same check the trigger runs, on the same transaction and under
the same lock:

- `LockedMemberSnapshot::replace_member_event` (relay's live roster
publisher) validates the snapshot it already holds the membership lock
for, before soft-deleting the old head.
- `insert_event_on` and `insert_event_with_thread_metadata_tx` (generic
event writes).
- `replace_parameterized_event_in_transaction_impl` (inside its existing
savepoint) and `Db::replace_addressable_event` (admin reconciliation
path), after dominance checks and before the old head is deleted.

The validator (`validate_channel_roster_snapshot`) is a direct port of
`guard_channel_roster_snapshot()`: four-field `p` tags, 64-char hex
pubkey, empty relay field, valid role, and an exact match against active
`channel_members` rows. It raises the same `23514` messages, so callers
still see `DbError::Sqlx(sqlx::Error::Database(..))` with the same code
and text.

**Lock order:** replacement key, then channel-membership key, then the
canonical read, then the old-head `UPDATE` and the write. Legacy writers
took the membership key later, at the trigger's INSERT, after the
old-head row locks. Taking it before the `UPDATE` is not the same order,
but it is strictly safer: it removes the row-lock/membership-key cycle.
The membership writers in `channel_members.rs` take the same membership
key before they change rows. Not every membership writer does yet:
`execute_kick_with_marker` (reached from report enforcement) and
`deploy_kick_member` in `relay_admin_actions.rs` set `removed_at`
without the key, so a kick can commit after a roster passes validation
and before that roster commits, leaving the removed member listed. The
retained trigger has the same gap, so this PR neither causes nor closes
it. When the trigger also runs it re-takes a key this transaction
already holds; transaction advisory locks are re-entrant, so this adds
no wait.

The validator is one verdict query on the happy path. On failure it
raises the trigger's exact error via a `DO` block, so mixed-version
behavior is identical; phase 2 can switch to a typed `DbError`.

**Unchanged on purpose:** the trigger, its function, migration 0032, and
the startup probe `verify_channel_roster_fence_behavior`. Pods still on
the old version depend on them. Phase 2 drops them once this version is
running everywhere.

## Tests

New PG tests in `channel_members.rs` `postgres_tests`, each with only
the roster trigger disabled (the helper asserts the catalog check then
fails):

- `app_roster_guard_matches_trigger_for_roster_input_table`: 19 shape
and membership cases (3/5-field tags, short and non-hex pubkeys, relay
field, unknown role, duplicate, role mismatch, missing/extra member,
uppercase hex, non-`p` tags, empty rosters, all roles). For each one,
the app outcome through `Db::replace_addressable_event` must equal the
trigger's outcome on a raw INSERT, including SQLSTATE and message.
-
`app_roster_guard_locked_writer_rejects_stale_and_accepts_current_without_trigger`
-
`app_roster_guard_covers_generic_and_parameterized_writers_without_trigger`
-
`app_roster_guard_rechecks_after_concurrent_membership_commit_without_trigger`:
the 0032 race. A newer membership commits while an older snapshot waits
on the membership key. The barrier is `pg_locks` with a bound, not
sleeps.

`stale_legacy_roster_cannot_replace_new_locked_snapshot`
(`replaceable.rs`) and `desired_schema_rejects_stale_legacy_roster_role`
(`channel_members.rs`) now simulate the old binary inline (replacement
key, old-head `UPDATE`, raw INSERT) instead of calling the app API, so
they test the retained trigger again. The replaceable.rs one keeps its
one-connection pool, so it still catches self-deadlock.

`observability_source.rs` gains
`every_production_event_insert_runs_the_roster_guard`, which requires a
real guard call in every production `INSERT INTO events` function, with
explicit exceptions (NIP-43 membership and push lease rows, both
`channel_id` NULL, and the two rolled-back startup probes), plus a
self-test.

Falsified: removing one guard call fails the source policy; dropping the
role clause or `lower()` fails the parity table; disabling the trigger
fails both legacy tests. The PG tests are picked up by the `postgres-ci`
nextest filter (`test(/postgres_tests::/)`); the source policy runs in
`just test-unit`.

### Coverage limits (review follow-up)

- `every_production_event_insert_runs_the_roster_guard` is a presence
check. It rejects missing, commented, and quoted calls, but it does not
prove a call is awaited, reachable, or passed the event's real kind and
channel. Behavior is covered by the PG tests above. The test now says
this in its doc comment.
- Exemptions match by function header. A kind 39002 insert added inside
one of the four exempt functions would pass the policy. This is
documented next to the exemption list.
- The 19-case parity table and the race test drive
`Db::replace_addressable_event` only. The generic, parameterized, and
locked writers get the mismatch case only, and the parameterized path's
membership-key-before-delete ordering is not exercised concurrently. All
five writers call the same validator, so this PR doesn't widen these
tests.
- `disable_roster_trigger` commits `DISABLE TRIGGER` on the test
database. That is safe under the per-test database harness the
`postgres-ci` profile uses, but not against a shared database. Its doc
comment now says so.

## Validation

fix(db): admit fleet sweeps per tenant instead of in-SQL fence predicate (#8318)

## What

Removes every production call to the SQL fence predicate
`community_write_allowed()` from application SQL, so no application
mutation depends on the boolean predicate anymore. This is one
prerequisite for BUZZ-315 part B; #8322 (tolerating absent fence
objects) is a separate one. The triggers and SQL functions stay in this
PR because mixed-version pods still depend on them.

The predicate isn't inlined. It's a VOLATILE plpgsql function that takes
the deletion lock and *then* reads lifecycle state on a fresh snapshot,
and an inline expression would read state from the statement's start
snapshot. A separate earlier check would race deletion. So each sweep
now:

1. reads its candidate community IDs with a plain read, bounded the same
way the original statement was,
2. opens one `AdmittedTx` per community
(`begin_community_sweep_transaction`, a thin wrapper over
`begin_community_write_transaction` that turns an admission refusal into
"skip this tenant"; the four periodic sweeps go through
`sweep_admitted_communities`, which also owns their error handling),
3. runs the original mutation scoped to `community_id = $1` and commits.

| Site | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `runtime/push_enqueue.rs` | Deleted the redundant predicate. This
transaction already calls `guard_transaction`. |
| `store/relay_invite.rs` `reap_expired_relay_invites` | Keeps the
global expiry order and the 1,000-row ceiling. Candidates are
pre-filtered to active tenants so fenced invites can't fill the batch.
Admission is still what authorizes the write. |
| `store/workflow.rs` `prune_scheduled_workflow_fires_before` | Prunes
per admitted community and sums the row counts. |
| `store/channel.rs` `reap_expired_ephemeral_channels` | Archives per
admitted community and returns the committed rows, so the relay still
runs their system and discovery follow-ups. The candidate read has no
lifecycle pre-filter (it has no `LIMIT`, so admission alone decides). |
| `store/event.rs` `backfill_d_tags` | Backfills per admitted community
at startup. |
| `store/push.rs` `claim_due_match_batch_with_loader` | Picks the
earliest due active community, admits it, and claims under the same `FOR
UPDATE OF q SKIP LOCKED` and batch limit. It skips at most 16 tenants
that fence between the read and admission. |
| `store/push.rs` `reap_exhausted_matches` | Reaps per admitted
community. |

**Tenant failures.** The four periodic sweeps (invite reap, workflow
fire prune, channel reap, exhausted match reap) log a warning and
continue when one tenant fails. That tenant's rows are left unmodified
and stay eligible, so the next tick retries them. A tenant error doesn't
abort processing of the other tenants already in the selected candidate
page. Invite cleanup keeps its oldest-first 1,000-row selection, so if
one tenant owns that entire page and its delete keeps failing, tenants
outside the page wait. No persistent tenant-local failure for that
delete is known in the current schema, and base aborted the whole page
on any error. The returned count or rows cover the tenants that
committed. Claim, enqueue and the startup backfill still return the
error to the caller.

**Database outages.** A connection-level error (pool acquire timeout,
closed pool, socket I/O; `DbError::is_connection_unavailable`) isn't
tenant-local, so it stops the periodic sweep at that tenant instead of
moving on. Without this, an outage that began after the candidate read
cost one writer acquire timeout and one warning per remaining tenant,
and invite cleanup runs inside the usage-metrics leader tick. Rows
already committed are still returned, so reaped channels keep their
follow-ups. Remaining tenants retry next tick.

**Known limit (pre-existing, tracked separately):**
- *Claim at a locked head.* `claim_due_match_batch_with_loader` returns
`None` once an admitted tenant claims zero rows. If every due row in the
oldest active tenant is row-locked, younger tenants aren't tried on that
call. Base behaved the same way. This PR doesn't change it.

## Tests

All tests use a one-session fixture (`test_support::admission_fixture`)
with `session_replication_role = replica`, so the trigger backstop is
off and only application admission protects the fenced tenants. The
fixture shadows `community_write_allowed` with a function that raises,
in a per-call `admission_test_<uuid>` schema.

- One test per site: a quiescing tenant's rows are untouched while an
active tenant in the same sweep still progresses.
- Race tests for invite reap, channel reap and claim. These are the
sites where the candidate read already filters out fenced tenants. Each
test holds the tenant's deletion lock, waits until the sweep is blocked
in admission, fences the tenant in that transaction, and asserts its
rows are untouched. The claim test also asserts that a second active
tenant is claimed in the same call.
- `channel_reap_returns_committed_rows_after_earlier_tenant_error` and
`periodic_reaps_continue_after_tenant_error_and_retry_retained_rows`
inject a per-tenant failure. They check that later tenants commit, that
the failed tenant's rows are retained, and that the next call processes
them.
- `fleet_sweep_stops_at_first_unavailable_connection` runs the sweep
helper against a closed pool with three candidates and asserts only the
first is attempted.
`fleet_sweep_returns_committed_results_when_database_drops_mid_page`
(PostgreSQL) commits the first tenant, closes the pool, and asserts the
first tenant's result is returned and the sweep stops at the second of
three candidates.
`connection_unavailable_covers_only_pool_and_io_failures` pins the
classification; the per-tenant failure tests above confirm a
database-raised error still continues.

Falsification, each with the tests failing as expected:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Original SQL restored at invite sweep, push claim, d-tag backfill |
0/3 pass (`legacy SQL fence predicate called`) |
| `guard_community_write` returns `Ok(())` after taking the lock | race
tests + channel reap test 0/4 pass |
| Per-tenant errors abort the sweep again | 0/2 pass |
| Sweep helper `continue`s instead of stopping on a connection-level
error | `fleet_sweep_stops_at_first_unavailable_connection` and
`fleet_sweep_returns_committed_results_when_database_drops_mid_page`
fail |
| Sweep helper drops already-committed results when it stops (`return

`fleet_sweep_returns_committed_results_when_database_drops_mid_page`

| Sweep helper removed from the source-policy chokepoint check |

buzz-db: tolerate absent universal write-fence objects (expand) (#8322)

## What

This is the expand step for retiring the 32 universal
`community_write_fence_*` triggers and their SQL functions (BUZZ-315).
Relay pods auto-migrate at boot (`BUZZ_AUTO_MIGRATE`). The drop
migration therefore runs while the previous release is still serving,
and that release must not depend on the objects it drops. Today the app
depends on them in four places, and this PR removes all four from its
own code paths. Seven in-SQL `community_write_allowed` predicates in
fleet sweeps and push (`push_enqueue.rs`, `channel.rs`, `event.rs`,
`push.rs`, `relay_invite.rs`, `workflow.rs`) are #8318's scope. The
release is independent of the fence functions only with both this PR and
#8318. **It changes no schema.** The objects stay and keep working until
the follow-up drop PR.

| Old dependency | Now |
|---|---|
| Startup and readiness (`validate_serving_catalog_on`) require
`community_write_allowed`, `assert_community_write_allowed`,
`enforce_community_write_fence` and all 32 triggers | No longer
required. Still required: the tenant tables,
`community_deletion_lock_key` and the enabled community tombstone
trigger. |
| Serving-lease admission runs `SELECT
assert_community_write_allowed($1)` | Uses `guard_community_write`, the
same shared lock and state check as ordinary serving writes, in the same
transaction as the lease `INSERT`. Fenced or missing communities still
map to `AccessDenied`. |
| Live scoped-table discovery calls
`community_write_fence_excluded_table()` | Uses a Rust
`EXCLUDED_SCOPED_TABLES` list. A unit test pins it equal to the SQL list
while both exist. |
| The deletion executor compares the live `fenced_tables` against the
frozen inventory | Only tenant-table equality is compared. Inventories
**still record** live fences, so an older executor that validates an
inventory frozen by this release still matches. The digest still covers
the full frozen manifest. |

`lock_community_deletion_shared` now refuses transactions that are not
READ COMMITTED, so every lock-then-read admission gets the check:
`guard_community_write`, serving-lease finalization
(`guard_transaction_with_serving_lease`), lease renewal/verification,
owner preparation and owner-mutation admission. The old SQL assertion
did this check for the lease path, and the trigger backed up the rest.
The isolation level comes back from the existing
`pg_advisory_xact_lock_shared` statement, so the hot path makes no extra
round trip. The refusal comes before any lifecycle-state read.

## Mixed versions

| Combination | Why it is safe |
|---|---|
| Previous release, this DB | No schema change, so all old checks still
see the 32 fences. |
| This release, DB with fence objects | Extra objects are tolerated, and
the trigger backstop still applies. |
| This release **plus #8318**, DB without fence objects | Serving,
readiness, lease admission and deletion proven by
`migration_schema_fence_objects_are_optional_for_serving_and_deletion`,
which drops them inline. Without #8318, serving and deletion still work,
but the push matcher, exhausted-job reaper, invite retention, ephemeral
reaper and startup d_tag backfill fail with `42883
community_write_allowed(uuid) does not exist` (seen in deploy-stack
E2E). |
| Older executor, inventory frozen by this release | `fenced_tables` is
still populated from the live catalog (32). |

This PR does not depend on #8318 to merge and can ship alongside it, but
it is not drop-safe alone. The drop PR (#8323) needs #8219, #8318 and
this PR deployed on every pod, and every rollback image after the drop
must include #8318.

## Tests

-
`store::deletion::postgres_tests::migration_schema_fence_objects_are_optional_for_serving_and_deletion`
migrates to 0060. It then runs the following with the fence objects
present, then again after dropping them inline:
  - serving startup
  - readiness
  - the deletion catalog check
  - `inventory_schema`
  - lease acquire/release
- `AccessDenied` for quiescing, fenced, tombstoned and missing
communities
-
`store::deletion::postgres_tests::deletion_lock_admission_rejects_pinned_snapshot_isolation`
checks that REPEATABLE READ and SERIALIZABLE are refused by both
`guard_community_write` and `guard_transaction_with_serving_lease`. The
lease case uses a never-acquired lease, so if the isolation check is
skipped it fails as stale instead.
- `buzz-deletion`
`postgres_tests::approved_legacy_fence_inventory_accepts_current_catalog`
checks that a legacy digest with 32 fences validates against a live
catalog with none, and that an unknown tenant table is still rejected.
-
`store::deletion::tests::scoped_table_exclusions_match_sql_during_transition`
checks exclusion-list parity.
-
`store::deletion::postgres_tests::serving_lease_acquire_waits_for_fence_lock_then_refuses`
holds the exclusive deletion lock and checks that lease acquisition
stays pending. It then commits `fenced` and requires `AccessDenied` with
no lease row persisted. Removing the lease path's
`guard_community_write` call fails this test, while the other four
lease/admission tests above still pass.
- `buzz-deletion`
`serving_guard_heartbeats_long_operation_through_quiescing` now requires
`AccessDenied` for a lease acquired during quiescing, rather than any
error.

Each test was confirmed to fail when its fix is removed (rc 100, 0/1):

version, the fence-list comparison restored, and one name dropped from

The lease path loses its special SQL assertion and its error-code
translation and reuses the ordinary app guard. The serving and deletion
catalog checks each lose one requirement. No new abstraction. The
`fenced_tables` reader stays only for mixed-version executors; the drop

feat(auth): support explicit mesh JWKS transport (#8382)

## Summary

Allow an issuer to opt into mesh HTTP for its JSON Web Key Set (JWKS).
Public HTTPS remains the default. This supports deployments whose
service mesh authenticates and protects the key endpoint.

The sealed source contract selects transport and contributes to policy
identity. Mesh mode requires a DNS hostname and checks every resolved
address against an explicit allow-list before pinning one address. Both
modes disable proxies, reject redirects, cap responses, and enforce a
whole-fetch deadline. The relay cannot verify mesh security: operators
must enforce mutual TLS, endpoint authorization, and egress
restrictions.

## Summary

This drops the channel-TTL event trigger. The application already
refreshes ephemeral-channel deadlines in the event transaction
(`event_follow_up::refresh_channel_ttls`, from #8135), so the trigger
only repeats that work.

This PR originally retired both follow-up triggers. #8352 has since
retired the push-match trigger in migration 0063, so after the rebase
this PR covers only the TTL half.

Migration `0065_retire_channel_ttl_trigger.sql`:
- `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` (the same bound as 0063)
- drops `events_refresh_channel_ttl` and
`refresh_channel_ttl_after_event_insert()`

Dropping the trigger on the partitioned parent also drops its partition
clones. Published migrations, including 0022 and 0024, stay
checksum-frozen.

The same objects are removed from `schema/` (`schema/functions/…`,
`schema/triggers/events.sql`, `schema/schema.sql`) and from the pgschema
reconcile script. After this, migrated and desired-state databases have
no event follow-up triggers.

Tests:
- `follow_up_retirement_tests.rs` (renamed from
`push_retirement_tests.rs`): the push-retirement upgrade test now stops
at 0063. A new test upgrades 0064 → 0065 and checks that the TTL trigger
is gone from the parent and every partition, that the function is gone,
and that the published checksums haven't changed.

`AppOnly` is the shipped schema, where both triggers are absent. `Dual`
reconstructs the historical overlap of both triggers. The `PushRetired`
arm (the push trigger dropped, the TTL trigger kept) was the shipped
state before this PR. Its tests are removed because `Dual` and `AppOnly`

The trigger and the app no longer both refresh TTL deadlines; the app is

Defines how an enterprise identity adapter issues assertions for agent
keys and how a NIP-FI relay admits them.

recording for the session or request, ban/deny checks on both keys,

deny-set check in WebSocket and HTTP admission, owner-matching
disconnect close scan, and the updated out-of-scope delegation lines.

feat(mobile): find people by name through the relay's name-only profile search (#8333)

🤖
## Summary
In the mobile app, searching for "wes" did not find Wes. People search
matched text anywhere in a profile, including the image data of a shared
default avatar. Many agent profiles use that avatar, so they filled the
results and the real Wes never appeared.

Now every people search in the app uses the relay's new name search: the
Search page, adding channel members, new messages, and @mention
suggestions. It matches only a profile's name and display name and puts
exact names first. The desktop app (block/buzz-app#1084), agent tools
(block/buzz-app#1124) and the CLI (#8331) make the same change.

Compatibility: a relay without the new search answers 404 or 405. That
search uses the old search, and so do later searches on the same relay
for five minutes; then the app tries the new search again, so a relay
that is upgraded while the app runs is used soon after. A query or
result count that the new search cannot take also uses the old search.
Other errors are shown as before.

Order: search results keep the relay's ranking, so "Wes" comes before
"Abe Wes". Before, the Search page and the member and new-message
pickers sorted results by name. The list with no query is still
alphabetical. Each screen still applies its own filters.

Not in scope: the community invite screen accepts only an npub and has
no name search, so this PR does not change it.

### Related issue
Relay endpoint: #8301. This PR does not depend on it; either can merge
first.

### Testing
- Relay session tests: the name query goes to the new search with a
signed request; a 404 falls back and stays on the old search until the
retry time; a 405 falls back; other errors do not fall back; an
unsupported result count uses the old search.
- Updated tests for add members and @mention search, and a test that
search results keep the relay's order while the browse list stays
alphabetical.
- `just mobile-check` and the relay, channel, mention, invite and search
tests (1,962) pass.
- No screenshots: results look the same; only which people are found
changes.

Merge pull request #156 from mvanhorn/fix/110-ios-device-root-launch-retry

fix: retry transient missing physical-device accessibility roots

test(ios-device): cover the root retry boundaries

Add tests for each boundary of the null-root retry: persistent nulls
stop after five reads, a malformed non-null root and a transport error
are not retried, a slow null reply exhausts the scheduling budget after
one read, a root on the fifth read is accepted, and cancellation during
the wait prevents another read. Each asserts the read count and the
error type. An internal rootElement(delay:budget:) seam lets the
count-bound cases run without the production pause.

The rootElement doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry now describe the
behavior as implemented: an immediate first read, at most four retries
each waiting up to 500 ms, a two-second budget that governs retry
scheduling rather than timing out the operation, cancellation during an
in-flight DTX read observed only after that read completes, and retries
that reuse the current session without reconnecting.

fix(test): reset _kernel_mode_frozen in backend selection test (#4399)

test_registration_defers_backend_selection did not reset _kernel_mode_frozen,
so when a prior test in the suite called _resolve_kernel_backend() the flag
was True and _should_use_kernel() returned bool(None)=False before reaching
the cache-rebuild path. Add monkeypatch to reset it alongside _kernel_mode_cache.

feat(python): auto-activate kernel backend when a project environment is detected (#4393)

* feat(python): auto-activate kernel mode when a project environment is detected

Closes #4355 (remaining gap after #4359, #4379, #4381).

Those PRs added the kernel backend but left it opt-in via
GPTME_IPYTHON_BACKEND=kernel. The issue asks for automatic activation
when a project environment is found, so users benefit without knowing
about the env var.

Changes:
- GPTME_IPYTHON_BACKEND now defaults to "auto" instead of "inprocess"
- auto mode: activate the kernel backend when a .venv directory,
  VIRTUAL_ENV, or a uv project marker (uv.lock / [tool.uv]) is found;
  fall back to in-process otherwise
- The detection result is cached so filesystem probes run at most once
- GPTME_IPYTHON_TIMEOUT is now respected in kernel mode too (passed as
  the kernel execute timeout), keeping interrupt behaviour consistent
- Message / list[Message] cell results now pass through the kernel
  backend: a displayhook wrapper (installed into ip.displayhook and
  ip.display_trap.hook to survive ipykernel's per-cell reset) intercepts
  gptme Message objects and delivers them via the bridge, suppressing the
  execute_result repr; gptme skips the summary wrapper when messages were
  delivered this way, matching in-process semantics exactly
- 6 new tests for _should_use_kernel() covering explicit, auto-with-venv,
  auto-without-venv, auto-with-uv.lock, and caching
- Updated test_execute_python_kernel_mode to patch _IPYTHON_BACKEND /
  _kernel_mode_cache instead of the removed _KERNEL_MODE

Git-Session-Id: cd44394f-04e2-499f-8f11-396db928ede8

* fix(python): make automatic kernel selection safe and preserve cell failures

Git-Session-Id: c424decb-abb2-5fbe-84a4-a0fc3066fc68

* test(tui): pin in-process backend for e2e ipython interrupt tests

The python tool now auto-selects the kernel backend when a project
environment is detected. CI runs under `uv run` with all extras, so
VIRTUAL_ENV/.venv are present and the kernel backend activates, which
changed the TUI Ctrl+C log from a KeyboardInterrupt traceback to an
`Interrupted` turn. These tests assert the in-process interrupt
contract, so pin `_IPYTHON_BACKEND=inprocess` in the ipython fixture,
matching tests/test_foreground_output_dedup.py.

* fix(python): invalidate auto-detection cache on workspace change

The auto backend cache was computed once per process, so a session that
started outside a project environment and later moved into one (os.chdir
via a workspace switch) stayed on the in-process backend despite auto
mode's contract. Key the cached result on (cwd, VIRTUAL_ENV) and
re-evaluate when either changes. Adds a regression test.

Git-Session-Id: 35493abd-16e7-53b0-a990-5111f4fddd4f

* fix(python): keep kernel backend stable after first cell

The auto backend re-evaluated on every cwd/VIRTUAL_ENV change, so a
mid-session directory change silently switched between the kernel and
in-process backends and discarded the other interpreter's state (Greptile
P1 on #4393). Freeze the choice once the first cell has executed; a
directory change before that still re-evaluates, preserving the workspace
contract.

Also guard the kernel displayhook's Message delivery RPC: if the bridge is
unavailable, fall back to the normal repr instead of turning a successful
cell into an error.

Git-Session-Id: f318efd3-8f13-5e2d-923a-3b126d1f248f

* fix(python): remove redundant inner pickle.loads in _gptme_deliver_messages

The displayhook was double-pickling messages: kernel-side dumping _msgs to bytes,
then the host-side _gptme_deliver_messages calling pickle.loads on those bytes.
The outer pickle.loads in the bridge handler (which is already guarded by the
128-bit token check at line 162) handles the full call dict including args.
Pass the message list directly through the RPC args instead.

Git-Session-Id: 0a859e28-4a77-431d-88a8-f22fbfa45ebe

fix(webui): guard null tooluse.args to prevent crash on argument-free tool calls (#4398)

* fix(webui): guard null tooluse.args to prevent crash on argument-free tool calls

ToolUse.args can be null when a native tool call carries no arguments
(e.g. @append with no inline args). Both InlineToolExecution and
InlineToolConfirmation called .args.length directly without a null check,
crashing the conversation view with "null is not an object evaluating
'y.tooluse.args.length'" (reproduced in v0.35.1 AppImage lifecycle sweep).

Changes:
- conversation.ts: widen ToolUse.args to string[] | null to match runtime
- InlineToolExecution/InlineToolConfirmation: use (args?.length ?? 0) > 0
  and pass args ?? undefined to detectToolLanguage
- RichToolCall: same detectToolLanguage null coercion
- toolActivity.ts: normalize null args to [] at ToolCall push boundary

is found but does not have ipykernel installed, fall back to
`uv run --with ipykernel` rather than gptme's own Python.  This keeps the
kernel running inside the project's environment (so %pip install goes to the
right place) without requiring the user to add ipykernel as an explicit
project dependency.  If neither uv is available nor a project Python is
found, gptme's Python is used unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Avoid modulo in Polygon pixel test

get_pixel did two modulo operations per edge for every pixel, only to wrap around on the last edge. The RP2040 has no divide instruction, so this was most of the drawing time.

Merge pull request #11617 from MakerClassCZ/audiomixer-dsp

Fix audiomixer phase inversion and use DSP on Cortex-M33

Merge pull request #11613 from dhalbert/zephyr-cp-qspi-4k-page

zephyr-cp: fix flash scratch page bugs; use 4 KB NOR flash layout pages; fix RP2 layout

Merge pull request #11610 from mikeysklar/stm-heap-below-stack

Fix STM32 boards crashing instead of running out of memory

zephyr-cp: use a 4 KB USB MSC buffer

With the default 512 byte SCSI buffer every sector of a write is its own
round trip through the MSC thread and the disk layer, about 4 ms per
sector on RP2040. A 4 KB buffer moves eight sectors at a time. It costs
7 KB of RAM with double buffering.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: test the background flush after a page change

Overwrite a sector, then one three pages later, and never flush or close
the file. Only the background flush can write the last sector before
the simulator is stopped. Fails on main, where the page change stopped
the tick.

Do the same on littlefs, which marks the filesystem dirty before
writing. Fill and free the drive first so new blocks aren't erased,
since writes to erased flash skip the page cache. Fails without the
previous commit to ports/zephyr-cp/supervisor/flash.c.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: don't flush flash on every USB write

Zephyr's USB MSC class issues DISK_IOCTL_CTRL_SYNC at the end of every
WRITE10, and _zephyr_disk_ioctl() turned that into a full flash flush.
The host waited for a page erase and reprogram after each command, and a
page written by consecutive commands, such as the FAT, was erased once
per command.

Leave the cached page for the next page change, the background flush
and autoreload, as the TinyUSB ports do. Unlike them, eject doesn't
flush: Zephyr's MSC class doesn't pass START STOP UNIT to the disk.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: keep the idle flush armed after a page change

When a write moved to a different flash page, _flash_write_block()
flushed the old page with supervisor_flash_flush(). That also clears
filesystem_dirty and stops the supervisor tick. littlefs marks the
filesystem dirty before writing, so its newly cached page was never
written by the background flush. Called from the USB MSC thread, it
could also race the VM thread's background flush, with both seeing the
flag set and both disabling the tick.

Flush only the old page, as ports/raspberrypi does with
port_internal_flash_flush().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

supervisor: don't lose a write that lands during a flush

On zephyr-cp, USB MSC writes run in their own thread while the idle
flush runs in the VM thread. supervisor_flash_flush() cleared
filesystem_dirty and stopped the tick after flushing, and
flash_write_blocks() marked dirty before writing. A block cached in
between stayed in RAM with no tick to write it out. Today the flush on
every MSC write hides this.

Clear the flag before flushing and mark dirty after writing.

This also changes ports whose write path calls supervisor_flash_flush()
on a page change: external_flash.c, nordic, stm, silabs, mimxrt and
cxd56. That flush cleared the flag and stopped the tick, so the newly
cached page waited for the next write, sync or reload. Now the 1 s
flush stays armed for it. raspberrypi and espressif flush the old page
with port_internal_flash_flush() and are unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use the DSP mixer path on every core that has it

The SIMD helpers were limited to ARMv7E-M, so the Cortex-M33 in the
RP2350 fell back to a float divide per sample. Check __ARM_FEATURE_DSP
instead, and mix with integers where there is no DSP, which matches the
DSP result bit for bit.

Fix audiomixer inverting samples at level 1.0

On cores with DSP instructions, a level of 1.0 (1 << 15) shifted left by
16 overflowed into the sign bit, so the mixed sample came out negated:
mono output was inverted and the right channel of a centered stereo voice
was out of phase with the left. Shift by 15 instead.

A centered pan now scales both channels by 1.0 instead of the left one
by 32767/32768.

zephyr-cp: reserve no flash scratch page on RP2040 and RP2350

ports/raspberrypi caches one 4 KB flash sector in a static buffer and
reserves no scratch page, so its filesystem was one page larger than
zephyr-cp's on the same board, and a filesystem it formatted didn't fit.

Add CIRCUITPY_FLASH_SCRATCH_PAGE, off by default on RP2040 and RP2350.
With it off, flash.c allocates the RAM cache once at startup and keeps
it, and the filesystem gets every whole page of the partition.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: check the filesystem partition is NOR page-aligned at build time

flash.c addresses erase pages relative to the start of the filesystem
partition. For the NOR flash drivers, whose layout page size is a Kconfig
setting, fail the build if the partition doesn't start and end on a
layout page boundary. This would have caught the nRF54LM20 DK's partition
with 64 KB SPI NOR layout pages.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

zephyr-cp: use 4 KB SPI NOR and MSPI NOR flash layout pages

Like the nRF QSPI driver, the SPI NOR and MSPI NOR drivers default to
64 KB layout pages. The nRF54LM20 DK's filesystem partition (0x62b000
bytes at 0x1d5000) isn't 64 KB-aligned, so part of it was unusable, and
the RAM cache needed 64 KB. Default both to their 4 KB sectors. Boards
that set the size themselves (the nRF54L15 DK, nRF54H20 DK) keep it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ports/stm: end the heap below the stack in the linker script

Move the fix from port_heap_get_top() into common_default.ld and
common_nvm.ld, as suggested in review. _ld_heap_end now stops at the
same address port_stack_get_limit() returns.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci: Cache Windows LLVM download, and retry curl downloads (#2187)

Our Windows CI often fails suriously in ways that are unrelated to
whatever changes are in a PR, and then succeeds upon retry (sometimes
after multiple retries). Often it's at the step where it's downloading
the pre-built Windows LLVM that we stashed on a Google drive (we could
not find a pre-built one with exactly the options we wanted, and we
can't build LLM from scratch in a reasonable time on the CI machines).

I finally (with some help from Claude) tracked down the source of
these failures: we're hitting Google Drive download limits!

This patch uses GHA cache action to reuse those downloads, generally
only retrieving from the Google drive the first time a branch or PR
goes through CI, which throttles usage enough to keep us under quota.

The specifics:

* Cache the unpacked LLVM (~/llvm/llvm-build) with actions/cache,
  keyed on LLVM_GOOGLE_DRIVE_ID. Both Windows jobs share the
  entry. The save step runs right after Dependencies, so a later build
  failure doesn't lose it. gh-win-installdeps.bash skips the download
  when the cache restored the directory.
* When we do download, check the result with `unzip -t`. If it is not
  a zip, fail with a clear message and print the start of the file.
* Add `--fail --retry 5 --retry-delay 10` to the curl downloads in
  gh-win-installdeps.bash, build_llvm.bash, and build_cmake.bash, to
  ride out transient network failures.
* Fix a missing `;` before `then` in gh-win-installdeps.bash.

build: Switch from FindCUDA to the FindCUDAToolkit (#2185)

This PR replaces use of the deprecated `FindCUDA` module with CMake's newer `FindCUDAToolkit`.

This change is a spiritual successor to Mark's old PR #2073. The overall direction remains the same, but has been reworked on top of the current state of  `main`.

We're including some additional fixes discovered while testing the build on Windows.

#### FindCUDAToolkit Migration

The build now uses `checked_find_package(CUDAToolkit)` and CMake's imported CUDA runtime targets.

The migration:
* Uses the canonical `CUDAToolkit_*` variables internally, while continuing to accept `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR` as a legacy fallback input.
* Links `CUDA::cudart` or `CUDA::cudart_static` rather than manually locating the CUDA runtime and appending Unix-specific system libraries.
* Passes the complete CUDA toolkit include list to NVCC and Clang.
* Adds the relocated CUDA C++ Core Libraries (`include/cccl`) when necessary for CUDA 13 and older supported CMake versions.
* Updates the remaining build and test logic to use `CUDAToolkit_FOUND`, `CUDAToolkit_VERSION`, and purpose-specific OSL variables rather than recreating the old `FindCUDA` result variables.
* Uses platform-aware CTest runtime paths so CUDA and NVRTC shared libraries can be found on both Windows and Unix-like systems.
* Uses `VERBATIM` custom commands so paths containing spaces are handled correctly.

#### Windows Device Alignment Fix

Testing on Windows revealed a separate incompatibility in the CUDA renderer support library. When building with older MSVC versions, Clang CUDA builds can resolve `__builtin_assume_aligned` to an MSVC host-only declaration, producing an error when it is used in device code.

We added a typed `device_assume_aligned` helper. It uses `__builtin_assume` to express the alignment guarantee on Windows and retains `__builtin_assume_aligned` on other platforms. The helper preserves the pointer type and evaluates each argument only once.

#### Standalone CUDA Example

We also migrated the standalone `example-cuda` project to `FindCUDAToolkit`. The build now reaches CUDA source compilation but encounters a pre-existing use of the now-defuct `OSL/device_string.h` API. Updating the example to OSL's current hash-based device string interface will be handled in a separate PR.

The removed `cuda_compile_ptx` helper is replaced with a local NVCC custom command, and the example links directly against the `CUDA::cudart`, `CUDA::nvrtc`, and `CUDA::cuda_driver` imported targets.

The example now propagates its complete dependency include paths into PTX compilation and uses `sm_75` as its default architecture with CUDA 13, which no longer supports the previous architectures. Older CUDA versions retain an `sm_60` default, and `CUDA_TARGET_ARCH` may still be overridden explicitly.

### Tests

We did not add any new tests, and we didn't observe any change in the test results relative to the baseline.

Linux configurations were exercised with CUDA 12.8 through 13.3 and LLVM 15.0.7 through 22.1.8, including the following combinations:

* CUDA 12.8 / LLVM 15.0.7
* CUDA 12.9 / LLVM 18.1.0
* CUDA 13.0 and 13.1 / LLVM 20.1.8
* CUDA 13.3 / LLVM 22.1.8
* CUDA 13.3 / LLVM 20.1.8
* CUDA 13.3 / LLVM 15.0.7

Additional configuration and build checks covered:

* CMake 3.24.4 and 4.0.4.
* Dynamic and static CUDA runtime targets.
* The legacy `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR` input.
* CUDA 13's relocated CCCL headers with an older supported CMake.
* CUDA/OptiX test runtime paths on Linux and Windows.
* CUDA 12.4 and 13.3 installations on Windows.
* CUDA installation paths containing spaces.
* Loading cudart and NVRTC with an otherwise clean Windows `PATH`.

Render slash command prefixes as composer prompt markers (#54742)

## What changed

- Display the leading `/` in the prompt marker instead of the editable text, sharing prefix state with shell mode's `!`.
- Preserve command prefixes and text element offsets across submission, queuing, history, and external editing. Keep prefixes literal in plain-text composers.
- Track composer-owned slash command elements separately, omit them from exported draft elements, and refresh them when command availability changes.
- Let backward deletion at the start of the text remove the prompt prefix while preserving selected-text deletion and Vim Replace recovery.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for slash prompt cursor placement, prefix deletion, history search highlighting, dynamic command availability, and Vim Replace restoration, including Unicode text. Update rendering snapshots for the slash prompt marker.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0da42da8e98bf7885f9b0ba2c8d5ad4f44d6847e

Gate the file-copy extension behind `multi_env_copy_file` (#54741)

## What changed

Add the `multi_env_copy_file` feature flag, disabled by default and marked as under development, to the feature registry and configuration schema. Install the file-copy extension in app-server threads and CLI debug prompt construction when the flag is enabled.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6d8b4c7479974f4b70c39f52333491c13d60d2a2

Close arg0 lock files before removing temporary directories (#54739)

## Why

Removing a directory while its lock file is open can leave `.nfs*` entries on NFS and prevent cleanup.

## What changed

- Drop the `Arg0PathEntryGuard` lock file before its temporary directory.
- On Unix, rename stale helper directories while locked, then close the lock before deleting them. This prevents initializers from publishing at the old path during cleanup.

## Testing

Extend the guard lifetime test to all platforms and assert that its directory is removed after main returns. Strengthen the janitor test to check that cleanup leaves the temporary root empty.

GitOrigin-RevId: 2524afcc63ed7769a7d16b622c1d447918f9478b

Enable BuildBuddy for voice release builds (#54737)

## What changed

Pass `BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY` to Linux, macOS, and Windows voice release builds, and give the dedicated macOS and Windows voice jobs access to the `bazel` environment without creating deployments.

Use the shared Bazel preparation action and BuildBuddy wrapper for Linux and macOS voice builds so they inherit the existing repository cache and remote cache configuration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 52cdf05bc4567f3e8c460d2509e57bb30e667868

Preserve prereleased events when creating GitHub prereleases (#54724)

## Why

Publishing a draft prerelease emits a `published` event instead of a `prereleased` event.

## What changed

Create GitHub prereleases with `--draft=false` so they emit `prereleased` events. Keep stable releases as drafts until all asset uploads succeed.

GitOrigin-RevId: 145fd84f852d7ee9cb3c4edff7007a34c3389e1c

Keep prereleases in draft until release assets finish uploading (#54716)

## Why

Prereleases were published before their assets finished uploading, exposing incomplete releases.

## What changed

Create new prereleases as drafts, matching stable releases, and publish them only after all asset uploads succeed. Publishing a draft emits a `published` event rather than a `prereleased` event.

GitOrigin-RevId: 0d1c52038bb9b7beb4b5b9bf52f0ef4c3734de61

Move V8's ICU Bazel rules into the workspace (#54710)

## What changed

Add `third_party/v8/icu.BUILD.bazel` and wire V8's ICU repository to use it instead of patching upstream `bazel/BUILD.icu`.

Select ICU's custom libc++ flags and runtime dependencies through `//third_party/v8:use_rusty_v8_custom_libcxx`, keeping ICU aligned with V8 and its host generators.

GitOrigin-RevId: 92a1b883f5d42d9a3a464002e922295ab166f2bd

Honor home deletion preferences during Windows uninstall (#54708)

## What changed

Read `desktop.uninstall_codex_home` from the owner's current `config.toml` before recursively deleting a desktop-created Codex home during Windows sandbox uninstall.

- Preserve the home by default for ordinary installations; retain the deletion default for OEM preinstalls when no preference is set.
- Let an explicit boolean preference override either default. Preserve the home when configuration is unreadable, malformed, or contains an invalid preference.
- Capture OEM metadata before Windows removes it during uninstall, and revoke sandbox permissions on retained homes.

## Testing

Add unit tests for missing preferences, explicit overrides, malformed or invalid configuration, and configuration read failures across both installation defaults.

GitOrigin-RevId: 46afc2a7b0f4ecf7f447e46b515e50d0d278e4a8

Preserve MCP tool-list metadata in server status (#54686)

## Why

MCP tool discovery discarded response-level `_meta`, leaving server-status clients unable to inspect metadata associated with the tool catalog.

## What changed

- Preserve opaque `_meta` from the first `tools/list` page through catalog refreshes and caches.
- Expose it as `toolListMeta` in `McpServerStatus`, with `null` when unavailable, and update generated schemas and bindings.
- Scope cached Apps catalog metadata to discovery settings, including client capabilities and extensions, while retaining tools from older caches without metadata.
- Restrict server capabilities in status snapshots to the selected servers.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for listing legacy cached Apps tools during failed startup, and update protocol serialization expectations for nullable `toolListMeta`.

GitOrigin-RevId: 62335e2fd8c482067a7a78a7612b58c3eaa9fb55

Keep TUI session selections bound to their backend (#54681)

## Why

A thread ID alone does not identify the backend that owns a session. Resume and fork selections must retain that ownership across connection replacement so they cannot operate on another backend, even when thread IDs match.

## What changed

- Add a process-local `BackendId` to app-server sessions and session targets, preserving it across reconnects and auxiliary picker connections.
- Reject selections from a different backend before changing session state or sending resume, fork, or unarchive requests.
- Disable local-daemon fallback to an embedded server for auxiliary pickers and after selecting a session, while retaining fallback for fresh startup.

## Testing

Add regression coverage for foreign selections with matching thread IDs, startup resume and fork rejection before requests, shared ownership across picker connections, and fallback eligibility.

GitOrigin-RevId: 05a3ca0a901a8dc24337d130548aa2c048b4d586

Distinguish MCP approval cancellation reasons (#54679)

## Why

MCP tool calls reported every aborted approval as "user cancelled MCP tool call", including interrupted requests and automatic cancellations in `exec` mode.

## What changed

Carry `user`, `interrupted`, or `non_interactive` cancellation reasons through MCP approval metadata and resolution. Mark explicit TUI cancellations as user actions, interrupted requests as interruptions, and automatic `exec` cancellations as non-interactive.

Use the reason to report when a call was cancelled before approval or because interactive approval is unavailable in `exec` mode. Preserve the existing cancellation message for clients that omit the reason.

## Testing

Update tests to verify that a closed approval response carries the interruption reason and that `exec` cancellation responses include the non-interactive reason.

GitOrigin-RevId: be2a5f7fef539b5db2add53b46aea27e2b8a66fc

Add an opt-in tool for copying files between environments (#54674)

## What changed

Add the `codex-multi-env-copy-file` extension, exposing `multi_env_copy_file` when registered by the host. Copy files between distinct selected environments without loading their contents into model context, and return `bytes_copied` on completion.

Require absolute paths in each environment's native path convention and enforce each endpoint's sandbox policy and permission grants. Stream file contents where supported, with a buffered fallback for older executors. Reject same-environment copies and report I/O error kinds without exposing connection details. Warn that failed writes may leave a truncated or partially written target.

## Testing

Add integration tests for binary transfers in both directions, local and remote executors, path validation, opt-in tool visibility, endpoint permissions and grants, and unavailable or disconnected executors. Verify that copied contents stay outside model context.

GitOrigin-RevId: f5d9e423d105019834e0288828cb68c5711b3a49

Use shared Bazel CI preparation for lint and V8 jobs (#54672)

## What changed

- Switch argument-comment lint, rusty-v8 release, and V8 canary jobs to `prepare-bazel-ci` to restore repository caches and configure execution logs. Use `bazel-argument-comment-lint` and `bazel-v8` cache scopes.
- Include changes to `prepare-bazel-ci` in V8 canary path detection.
- Pass `BUILDBUDDY_API_KEY` to the `MODULE.bazel.lock` check.

GitOrigin-RevId: 6ef150f93413d1d30287f0728358eed26e792204

Distinguish retryable thread-store errors from unknown write outcomes (#54664)

## What changed

Add `ThreadStoreError::Retryable` for transient failures known to be safe to retry and `ThreadStoreError::OutcomeUnknown` for writes that may already have committed. Recovery remains the operation owner's responsibility; neither category automatically triggers retries.

Preserve existing app-server error mappings and fatal session startup behavior, and report the new categories in shutdown diagnostics without exposing raw error payloads.

## Testing

Add coverage for conservative SQLx error classification, mutation error mappings, session initialization categories, and shutdown diagnostics that omit raw error payloads.

GitOrigin-RevId: 259a9bfaa6ff3cbfa2ee61a01a1f1e744c90f118

Honor MCP tool-list changes within a turn (#54656)

## Why

MCP servers can expose new tools during discovery. Refreshing the catalog after a tool-list notification lets Codex discover and call those tools in the same turn.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for ordinary MCP servers.
- Track notifications in transport order and refresh catalogs before subsequent discovery or tool binding. Coalesce concurrent refreshes and retry listings invalidated by notifications, including during pagination.
- Retain the previous catalog on refresh failure, apply a retry cooldown, and invalidate affected startup caches. Allow notification refreshes to proceed while admitted calls finish.

## Testing

Add coverage for same-turn discovery and invocation in direct and Code Mode, notifications during startup and pagination, disabled behavior, cache invalidation, and concurrent refreshes with timeout recovery.

GitOrigin-RevId: 9afee8deba00dd9851b5f32625f61f96965aa00c

Allow dynamic tool calls to execute in parallel (#54654)

## Why

Dynamic tool calls should remain independent while waiting for client responses, so one pending call does not block another from reaching the client.

## What changed

Enable parallel execution in `DynamicToolHandler`, allowing code mode programs to issue concurrent dynamic tool calls with `Promise.all`.

## Testing

Add a code mode regression test that waits for two dynamic tool requests before responding, resolves them in reverse order, and verifies that `Promise.all` preserves the expected result order.

GitOrigin-RevId: c93c1fea720f76c772b0e3452ddc8c01fb1a08d8

Prefer resource-specific scopes during MCP OAuth discovery (#54653)

## Why

Authorization server metadata can advertise scopes unrelated to the MCP resource. Using that list for discovery can request broader scopes than the resource requires.

## What changed

Update `rmcp` and use its initial scope selection during OAuth discovery: prefer scopes from the initial `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, fall back to protected resource metadata, and include `offline_access` when supported. Stop using the authorization server's general scope list as the discovered resource scopes.

## Testing

Add coverage for challenge scope precedence, resource metadata fallback, scope normalization, and exclusion of unrelated authorization server scopes. Add a no-browser login regression test for a preregistered client whose authorization server advertises neither scopes nor dynamic registration.

GitOrigin-RevId: 68d83cf61fb0b73dac9e861e476f484990fd93b6

Make remote-control conflict retry tests deterministic (#54647)

## What changed

Wait for the rejected socket to close before advancing Tokio's clock through
capped retry delays. Keep socket I/O on real time so pending handshakes cannot
auto-advance their own timeouts.

Return bodyless HTTP 409 responses in the test server, check that neither
rejection restarts fast retries, and assert that recovery preserves the expected
reconnect attempt count. Both cursor and cursorless cases use the updated helper.

GitOrigin-RevId: da167312f28b7e24b864e6929be749865ea70081

Retry npm release publishing and match macOS verification runners (#54641)

## What changed

- Attempt each `npm publish` up to three times, with 10- and 20-second delays and fresh OIDC credentials on each attempt. Continue skipping already-published versions.
- Enable verbose npm logging and retain debug logs as artifacts for seven days, including on failure.
- Use `macos-15-intel` to verify provisioned `x86_64-apple-darwin` packages, while keeping `aarch64-apple-darwin` verification on `macos-15-xlarge`.
