commits.message:
[Kubernetes] Map H100-MEGA to the nvidia-h100-mega-80gb GKE label (#11104)

The GCP catalog names the A3 Mega GPU H100-MEGA, and GKE labels A3 Mega
nodes nvidia-h100-mega-80gb. GKELabelFormatter turned H100-MEGA into the
legacy nvidia-tesla-h100-mega label, so with the GKE autoscaler the pod's
node selector never matched and the pod stayed pending until
provision_timeout. It also reported the label as H100-MEGA-80GB, which is
not a catalog name.

Map H100-MEGA to H100-MEGA-80GB before building the label, and map the
label back to H100-MEGA, in the same way H100 is handled. H100-MEGA-80GB
requests still produce the same label.

Signed-off-by: Madhav Jivrajani <madhav.jiv@gmail.com>

[Jobs] Propagate scheduler subprocess exit code in consolidation mode (#9646)

* [Jobs] Propagate scheduler subprocess exit code in consolidation mode

In consolidation mode, `_consolidated_launch` discards the return code
of `backend.run_on_head`. When the controller script
(`python -m sky.jobs.scheduler ...`) exits non-zero — e.g. the script's
Python interpreter is missing a dependency, a database write fails, or
the process is OOM-killed mid-flight — the failure is invisible to the
API server. The user's `jobs.launch` request is marked SUCCEEDED while
the managed job row remains in (status=PENDING, schedule_state=INACTIVE)
forever, because both `ha_recovery_for_consolidation_mode` and
`update_managed_jobs_statuses` deliberately skip INACTIVE rows ("may be
mid-submission, don't set to WAITING").

Surface the exit code so the launch request fails when the subprocess
fails. The user sees a clear error pointing them at the script log and
suggesting `sky jobs cancel <id>` to clean up the orphan row.

Non-consolidation paths already propagate subprocess failures (gRPC
`queue_job` aborts INTERNAL; SSH-fallback uses `handle_returncode`), so
this fix is consolidation-mode-specific by design.

Caveat — inverse case worth flagging: if `maybe_start_controllers`
raises *after* `scheduler_set_waiting` has committed, the script exits
non-zero (request FAILED) but `schedule_state=WAITING` is already set
and the controller will be spawned by the next recovery pass. Net:
"FAILED request, job actually runs." This is the inverse of the
"PENDING-forever" bug — we promise SUCCEEDED→runs; we do not promise
FAILED→doesn't-run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Don't fail jobs.launch when eager maybe_start_controllers raises

`scheduler.submit_jobs` does, in order:
1. `scheduler_set_waiting` — DB write that transitions the managed-job
   row to WAITING and persists the dag/env/config content. Once this
   commits, the periodic `managed-job-status-refresh-daemon` will find
   the row and spawn a controller within ~one event cycle.
2. `maybe_start_controllers(from_scheduler=True)` — eager optimization
   that spawns controllers in the same process so the new job picks up
   without waiting for the next recovery pass.

If step 2 raises after step 1 has committed, the script exits non-zero
and (with the previous commit's returncode propagation) the user's
`jobs.launch` request is marked FAILED — but the row is WAITING and
recovery WILL spawn a controller, so the job runs anyway. The user
sees a FAILED status, retries, and double-launches the same intent.

Swallow exceptions from `maybe_start_controllers` after the DB write
has committed. The error is logged at ERROR with full traceback so a
genuine bug in the eager spawn path is still loud, and recovery picks
up the job. The script's exit code now tracks whether the job was
queued (= `scheduler_set_waiting` committed), not whether the eager
spawn succeeded.

Note: this fix only addresses the case where the worker is still alive
and `maybe_start_controllers` raises. If the worker process dies
mid-script (rolling update SIGTERM, OOM, k8s SIGKILL before
the uvicorn graceful wait expires), the inverse can still manifest —
the request is marked FAILED/CANCELLED by HA Pass B or the OSS graceful
shutdown, but a controller is spawned by the next recovery pass for
any WAITING row. That's a separate, harder problem that requires
linking requests to managed jobs and cancel-cascading; tracked as
follow-up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update sky/jobs/server/core.py

Co-authored-by: gemini-code-assist[bot] <176961590+gemini-code-assist[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>

* [Jobs] Drop the swallow around the eager maybe_start_controllers

Master now returns early from maybe_start_controllers(from_scheduler=True)
in consolidation mode, before it starts any controller: the leader-elected
refresh daemon owns the controller pool. In consolidation mode the call can
no longer raise after scheduler_set_waiting commits, so the try/except only
changed behavior on a jobs controller VM, which this PR does not target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Cancel the jobs of a failed consolidated submission

When the scheduler script exits non-zero, the request now fails, but the
job stayed in the queue as PENDING: before scheduler_set_waiting commits it
is INACTIVE, which recovery never picks up. Cancel each job with
set_pending_cancelled, which claims a WAITING job away from the scheduler
atomically. A job a controller already claimed is left to run, and the
error names it.

The cancel hint now lists the ids space-separated: `sky jobs cancel` takes
integers, not the `10-12` range form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [Jobs] Cancel a failed submission's jobs the way sky jobs cancel does

set_pending_cancelled only cancels a job no controller has claimed. A job
a controller claimed before the script exited kept running behind a
FAILED request. Use cancel_jobs_by_id instead: it still cancels an
unclaimed job in the database, and it signals a claimed job's controller
to cancel the job and tear down anything it launched.

Pass each job's own workspace: cancel_jobs_by_id skips jobs outside the
workspace it is given, and launch runs the submission under the default
workspace. The cancel request is recorded with the launch request's ID and
the script's exit code, so set_pending_cancelled no longer needs a reason
argument.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Verda] Keep the existing catalog when no GPU instance type is available (#11102)

* [Verda] Keep the existing catalog when no GPU instance type is available

Verda's availability API lists only instance types with free capacity.
When every GPU type is sold out, the fetcher wrote a catalog with no GPU
rows, which SkyPilot releases before #11101 cannot filter by accelerator

[API] Back off a log stream's status check while the request is parked (#11084)

A client that follows a request with /api/stream keeps the server's log
tail reading the request's status every polling_interval (1 s for LONG
requests). That includes the whole time the request is parked as WAITING,
which can last hours, so each parked request with an attached stream costs
about one requests-DB read per second.

While the request is WAITING, double the status-check interval up to a
10 s cap, the same cap wait_for_request_to_start reaches for LONG
requests. Each interval is cut by a random 0-40% after the cap, so
streams of requests that parked together do not read in step. The quiet
log file is read once a second instead of ten times. Any other status,
and any new log bytes, go back to the base interval.

[Jobs] Emergency recovery keeps a running job on its cluster (#10963)

* [Jobs] Emergency recovery keeps a running job on its cluster

An unexpected controller error used to put the job's task into
RECOVERING, tear its cluster down before the backoff, and relaunch it
on the retry, even when the task was RUNNING and the error had nothing
to do with the cluster (a database outage, a bug in the monitor loop).
That restarts a healthy workload: the job loses its progress since its
last checkpoint and its GPUs, and the relaunch can preempt other jobs.

Now a RUNNING (or WINDING_DOWN) task keeps its status and its cluster
through the backoff. The retry resumes it the way a controller restart
does: the monitor loop re-attaches and its own job and cluster checks
decide whether the job is still alive, relaunching only when the
cluster fails them. The emergency is still recorded on a job event that
carries the task's current status and recovery_source=EMERGENCY, so
alerting and metrics see the episode; the recovery-events metric counts
those events, with its (new_status, recovery_source) index intact.

Tasks that never reached RUNNING, or were already relaunching
(STARTING, RECOVERING), keep the previous path. The last attempt of an
episode also relaunches: an error that recurs on every re-attach can be
tied to the cluster or handle the controller keeps re-reading, and one
relaunch is the only thing that can clear it before the job fails.

Two things come with keeping the cluster. The job is unmonitored while
the controller sleeps, and its cluster is autodowned ten minutes after
the job ends, so a job that finished early in a long backoff would be
relaunched after completing; the backoff therefore keeps its full
ladder (a persistent error still takes hours to exhaust the budget,
leaving time to remediate by hand) but probes the job every six minutes
and ends early once the job has finished or its cluster is gone. And
the bookkeeping that records the emergency needs the database, which is
the most likely thing to be down when an error escapes; it now retries
for up to thirty minutes instead of five rounds, so a database outage
shorter than that costs the job one attempt and no restart.

When the cluster record is gone by the time the loop recovers, the
cluster events are now read by name so the teardown reason still
reaches the controller log.

fix: require a primary key to enable MemWAL (#4561)

## Why

Every MemWAL write and read resolves rows by the table's unenforced
primary key, but `enable_memwal` accepted a table without one. The spec
installed, and every MemWAL `merge_insert` then failed with "table has a
MemWAL index but no unenforced primary key" until MemWAL was disabled.
Lance's MemWAL initialization doesn't catch it: its key checks pass when
there is no key.

## What changes

`enable_memwal` refuses a spec on a table with no unenforced primary
key, for every sharding mode, before anything is committed. The check
runs against the dataset the spec is committed to; a key cannot be
removed once set, and an overwrite or restore of the table conflicts
with that commit. Servers that install specs through this method get the
check too.

The Rust doc on `Table::enable_memwal` now states the requirement; the
Python and TypeScript docs already did.

## Tests

- New `test_enable_memwal_requires_primary_key` (Rust and Python):
unsharded, bucket and identity specs are all refused without a key, a
refused spec leaves nothing installed, and the same table accepts a spec
once a key is set. The Rust test fails with the check disabled.
- Tests that installed a spec on a table without a key now declare one
first (6 Rust, 3 Python).
- `cargo nextest run -p lancedb --features remote --lib`: 1529 passed.
`cargo clippy -p lancedb --features remote --tests --examples -- -D
warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean; no integration test or
example installs a spec.
- Python: `test_memwal_spec.py` and `test_merge_insert_lsm.py`, 43
passed; `ruff format` and `ruff check` are clean.

refactor!: rename LSM APIs to MemWAL and align SSTable/table shard naming (#4075)

## What

Renames the MemWAL surface in two passes, across Rust, Python,
TypeScript, and Java, including the wire format.

### 1. MemWAL APIs drop "LSM"

The write path these APIs drive is Lance's MemWAL; "LSM" described its
shape rather than naming it. Turning it on and off now reads as enabling
a feature rather than installing a spec.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `set_lsm_write_spec` | `enable_memwal` |
| `unset_lsm_write_spec` | `disable_memwal` |
| `get_lsm_write_spec` | `get_memwal_spec` |
| `flush_lsm` / `compact_lsm` / `checkpoint_lsm` | `flush_memwal` /
`compact_memwal` / `checkpoint_memwal` |
| `get_lsm_stats` | `get_memwal_stats` |
| `close_lsm_writers` | `close_memwal_writers` |
| `use_lsm` (query, merge insert) | `use_memwal` |
| `LsmWriteSpec` / `LsmStats` | `MemWalWriteSpec` / `MemWalStats` |
| Java `LanceDbTableLsm` | `LanceDbTableMemWal` |

TypeScript and Java use camelCase (`enableMemWal`, `getMemWalStats`,
...); the napi methods set `js_name` so the generated names keep the
`MemWal` casing. flush/compact/checkpoint keep a `_memwal` suffix so
`compact_memwal` is not confused with `compact_files` / `optimize`,
which compact the base table.

Internal names (`LsmMode`, `LsmScanner`, the `merge::lsm` / `query::lsm`
modules) are unchanged.

### 2. Stats use SSTable and table shard

Aligns the stats surface with the MemWAL naming settled upstream in
lance-format/lance#7943 and #7957, where the persisted unit became an
**SSTable**.

**Generation → SSTable.** A `GenerationStats` describes one flushed
MemTable, which is an SSTable. The generation *number* is kept — an
SSTable is identified by its generation — so only the noun moved.

**Bucket → table shard.** Each entry is one MemWAL shard. "Bucket" names
only the hash sharding *transform*, so it was already wrong for
`identity` and `year` sharding, which produce shards and no buckets at
all.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `GenerationStats` | `SsTableStats` |
| `BucketStats` | `TableShardStats` |
| `stats.buckets` | `stats.table_shards` |
| `BucketStats.generations` | `TableShardStats.sstables` |
| `include_generation_rows` | `include_sstable_rows` |
| `newest_generation` | `newest_sstable_generation` |
| `outstanding_generations` | `outstanding_sstables` |

Docs and comments follow suit: "seal" → "freeze", "L0" / "flushed
generations" → SSTables, "bucket" (meaning a shard) → table shard.

`MemWalWriteSpec::bucket`, `num_buckets`, and the `"Sealed"` shard
status value are **unchanged** — those name the sharding transform or a
server value, not the shard.

## Compatibility

Breaking, for an experimental API. The wire format changes with the
SDKs, so this must roll out together with the matching server change:

- Routes: `/set_lsm_write_spec/` → `/enable_memwal/`,
`/unset_lsm_write_spec/` → `/disable_memwal/`, `/get_lsm_write_spec/` →
`/get_memwal_spec/`, `/flush_lsm/` → `/flush_memwal/`, `/compact_lsm/` →
`/compact_memwal/`, `/get_lsm_stats/` → `/get_memwal_stats/`
- Response keys: `lsm_write_spec` → `memwal_spec`, `lsm_stats` →
`memwal_stats`, `buckets` → `table_shards`, `generations` → `sstables`
- Request fields: `include_generation_rows` → `include_sstable_rows`;
`use_lsm` → `use_memwal` on query and merge-insert bodies

## Validation

- Rust: `cargo test --features remote -p lancedb --lib --tests` — 1467
lib tests and all integration test targets pass; `cargo clippy` clean
- Python: rebuilt the extension; `test_remote_db`, `test_memwal_spec`,
`test_merge_insert_lsm`, `test_query`, `test_permutation`, `test_table`
— 655 passed; `ruff format` / `ruff check` clean
- TypeScript: `pnpm build`; `table`, `merge`, `query` tests — 593
passed; `biome check` clean; `docs/src/js` regenerated with `npm run
docs`
- Java: `mvn test` — 37 passed (Spotless applied with JDK 11; the pinned
google-java-format does not run on JDK 21)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(remote): support set_unenforced_primary_key (#4158)

## Summary

`RemoteTable::set_unenforced_primary_key` returned `NotSupported`, so
the call failed against LanceDB Cloud and enterprise from every SDK —
Python and TypeScript both forward to it. That also blocked sharded LSM
writes, since the server rejects bucket/identity sharding on a table
that declares no unenforced primary key, and the SDK had no way to
declare one.

No server-side support was missing. The unenforced primary key is Lance
schema field metadata, and the existing `update_field_metadata` endpoint
writes exactly that, so the remote table now installs the key through
it. The commit layer behind that endpoint installs the position,
enforces immutability and runs `verify_primary_key()` — the same code a
native table reaches, so both paths agree on semantics and not just on
error messages.

## Changes

- `rust/lancedb/src/table/primary_key.rs`: the request validation
(single column, column exists, supported dtype, key not already set) and
the metadata edit (set the 1-indexed position, clear the legacy boolean
key) move into `validate()` and `install_edit()`, shared by both table
types so they cannot drift. Native behaviour is unchanged.
- `rust/lancedb/src/remote/table.rs`: real implementation —
`check_mutable()`, validate against the described schema, then one
`update_field_metadata` request.
- `python/python/lancedb/remote/table.py`: drop the "Not supported on
LanceDB Cloud." docstring.

No binding changes were needed; Python and TypeScript already forward to
the Rust `BaseTable` method.

## Tests

Three mocked-server tests in `rust/lancedb/src/remote/table.rs`:

- the happy path, asserting the request body carries
`lance-schema:unenforced-primary-key:position: "1"` and a null legacy
key on the right field path;
- the invalid requests a native table also rejects (empty, compound,
unknown column, unsupported dtype), each failing before any write
reaches the server;
- the already-set case, rejected from the schema the server already
reports.

commits.message:
esp32: Espressif ESP-Mosaico (ESP32-S31) board support (experimental) (#223)

The ESP-Mosaico: an ESP32-S31 (two RISC-V cores at 320 MHz, 16 MB PSRAM),
a square 2.16" 480x480 CO5300 AMOLED with CST9217 touch, an ES8311 codec,
a BQ27220 fuel gauge, the AI and BOOT buttons.

- components/muse/boards/board_esp_mosaico.c drives the parts itself, with
  pins and init sequences from Espressif's esp-mosaico-bsp; eFuse USER_DATA
  tells board revisions v1.0 and v1.2 apart (I2C, LCD SCL/RST, codec rail).
  Talk on AI, aux on BOOT; battery from the fuel gauge; power off through
  the board's latch. Hints from Espressif's drawing: the mic at the AI key
  (top edge), the power icon at ON/OFF (bottom, right of USB-C).
- muse_ui: a board's no_ring shows progress as a bar along the bottom edge
  instead of a circle around Muse (the panel is square).
- devices/sdkconfig.muse-esp-mosaico: target, 320 MHz, 16 MB QIO flash,
  PSRAM as Espressif's template sets it, UART console (USB-C is the S31's
  high-speed OTG), unsigned app (a signed one can't hand over to the
  board's Vibe Mode firmware, whose image it checks against our key).
- partitions_mosaico.csv keeps the board's retained first 2 MB (Vibe Mode
  in factory, sysmeta, coredump) and puts the app in ota_0 at 2 MB.
- ESP-Iris and Vibe Mode: devices/sdkconfig.muse-esp-mosaico-iris (the
  product contract the Vibe Mode firmware checks), components_mosaico/
  muse_mosaico_iris (starts ESP-Iris and the app-side recovery support, so
  later installs need no buttons), added by cmake/project.cmake from an
  esp-mosaico-utils checkout (MOSAICO_UTILS).
- tools/muse/board.sh mosaico: ESP-IDF master at 7b9cc1ac (IDF_EXPORT_S31;
  the S31 isn't in v6.0.1), builds an ESP-Iris System Update bundle, and
  flashes it with Espressif's mosaico.py iris system-update, never esptool
  (factory holds Vibe Mode).
- devices/README.md, AGENTS.md: the board, its tools and how to install.

Tested on a v1.2 board: installed through Vibe Mode, boots (display,
touch, audio self-test, battery), normal -> Vibe Mode -> normal with the
same Device ID and new boot IDs, no crash. idf.py build (C5 default),
s3-216 and the host tests (587, OK) and UI simulator pass. Not in CI: it
needs ESP-IDF master and esp-mosaico-utils.

esp32: remember the SDK token pairing used, and stop refreshing to report it (#221)

Muse records a gadget's SDK token only when the gadget pairs: the Muse
app sends it when it mints the device token. A device token refresh
doesn't record one, so the refresh each boot made to "report" the token
replaced the device token for nothing, and a token set after pairing
(in the build, over serial or in Settings) never took effect, without
any sign. Makers who then revoked the old token cut their gadget off.

- Pairing (and the mint path) stores the token's hint, its first 12
  characters as gadgets.muse.ai shows it, under pair_sdk_hint, which
  config_clear_pairing() and config_clear_setup() forget.
- The boot banner warns when the current token isn't the one pairing
  used, and on boards with the full UI the Muse settings page says
  "paired with another SDK token, pair again to use this one".
- The refresh-to-report each boot is gone.
- The README says to pair again after changing the token or revoking
  the one the gadget paired with.

A gadget paired by older firmware has no hint and shows no warning.

Tested: the host suite (new test_link_identity runs identity.c against
an in-memory store and checks the contract in app.c and config_store.c)
has no new failures against main.

linux: remember the SDK token pairing used, and stop refreshing to report it (#220)

Muse records a device's SDK token only when the device pairs: the Muse
app sends it when it mints the device token. A device token refresh
doesn't record one, so the refresh each start made to "report" the
token rotated the device token for nothing, and a token changed after
pairing silently never took effect.

- Pairing saves the token's hint (its first 12 characters, as
  gadgets.muse.ai shows it) in pairing.json.
- `musegadget run` warns once when the current token isn't the one
  pairing used, and `musegadget info` shows both, since a new token
  takes effect only after `musegadget pair --force`.
- The README says to pair again after changing the token or revoking
  the one the device paired with.

Tested: `pytest` (218 passed) on Python 3.9.

Merge pull request #7282 from rockboynton/rockboynton/fix-uart-early-flush-return

stm32/usart: fix early BufferedUart flush

Merge pull request #7113 from VictorVulturescu/feat/nxp-hashcrypt-sha-modes

nxp/hashcrypt: add SHA-1 and SHA-256 modes

stm32/usart: fix early BufferedUart flush

Since #6535, a write that wraps the TX buffer goes in as two write()
calls. If the interrupt drains the first part before the second lands,
it arms TCIE and stops, and TC then sets tx_done with data still
queued, so flush() returns before the last bytes are out. This can be a
problem on half-duplex RS-485, for example, where DE goes low once
flush() returns, which cuts off the end of the frame.

It's a pretty rare error, but at 1 Mbaud on a U575, a stress test lost
the tail of 2-4 replies in every 600.

With this fix, TC only reports done once the TX buffer is empty, every
write pends the interrupt, and writes clear tx_done and commit in one
critical section.

With this fix, I couldn't reproduce the issue with that same stress over
many iterations.

commits.message:
remote-derive: name primitives through ::core::primitive and call WirePayload methods by path (#719)

Fixes #707.

## What

The `buffa-remote-derive` expansions now spell the primitive types they
use as `::core::primitive::str`, `::core::primitive::u8` and
`::core::primitive::usize`. `from_wire` calls
`::buffa::WirePayload::to_str(&__buffa_payload)` and
`::buffa::WirePayload::as_slice(&__buffa_payload)` instead of using
method-call syntax.

## Why

- A type or alias named `str`, `u8` or `usize` in scope at the derive
took the primitive's place. `#[derive(MapStorage)]` beside `type usize =
u32;` failed inside the derive with E0053, and the string and bytes
derives failed the same way.
- A trait in scope, implemented for `WirePayload`, with a by-value
`to_str` or `as_slice` was called instead of the inherent method,
because method lookup tries the by-value receiver before it
auto-references. That compiled, and `from_wire` returned whatever the
trait returned.

The other method calls in the expansions (`.map` on the `Result`,
`.to_vec()` on the slice, `write_str` on the formatter) are safe: the
inherent method matches at the first lookup step, so a trait cannot take
it over.

## Implementation

- `string.rs`, `bytes.rs`, `map.rs`, `forwarders.rs`: the primitive
paths, and the two `WirePayload` calls by path, with a comment on why.
- `lib.rs`: one paragraph under "Reserved identifiers".
- Unit tests: `every_expansion()` now holds the list of expansions that
`every_binding_starts_with_the_reserved_prefix` built, so two new tests
walk the same set with `syn::visit`:
- `every_primitive_is_named_through_core_primitive`: no one-segment path
names a primitive type (all 17 are checked).
- `the_wire_payload_is_never_a_method_receiver`: no method call has
`__buffa_payload` as its receiver, and `from_wire` still reads it.
- New integration test `tests/shadowed_primitives.rs`: type aliases and
unit structs named `str`, `u8` and `usize` beside the string, bytes and
map derives (with `serde` and `arbitrary`), and a trait with by-value
`to_str` / `as_slice` that returns other data. Before the fix the file
fails to compile with 56 errors. With only the two method calls put
back, it compiles and `from_wire` returns `"shadowed"` instead of
`"wire"`.

Net change outside tests: +52/-30.

## Testing

Run locally on Windows (`x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, toolchain 1.95.0,
protoc 33.5):

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass except two `buffa-types` tests that
fail on Windows only, because `SystemTime` there has 100 ns resolution;
unrelated to this crate
- `task doc`, `task test-arbitrary`
- `cargo test --manifest-path examples/custom-types/Cargo.toml`
- markdownlint

Conformance was not run.

AI-usage disclosure: Claude (Anthropic) was used as assistant.

message_field: always inline MessageField::eq (#553)

Closes #550. Follow-up to #455.

With plain `#[inline]`, LLVM inlines `T`'s own `eq` into
`MessageField::eq` first, and for a larger `T` the grown body then stays
a call in the caller, paid even when both fields are unset.
`#[inline(always)]` keeps the presence match in the caller. `T::eq`
keeps its own inlining decision.

Measured on main `e246ee2` with an external schema of about 740 messages
(standalone harness, not in this repo; method in #550), Rust 1.95.0:

| profile | out-of-line `MessageField::eq` before → after | `.text` |
|---|---|---|
| opt-level 3 | 50 → 0 | +0.41% |
| opt-level 3, `lto = true`, `codegen-units = 1` | 48 → 0 | +0.36% |
| s | 47 → 0 | +0.58% |
| z | 61 → 0 | +2.1% |

Per product compared, `eq` goes from 256 to 227 instructions (239 to 227
with LTO), and `eq` on the config message takes 8–12% fewer cycles
(3–20% with LTO). In this repo's benchmark messages, `LogRecord.source`
and `GoogleMessage1.field15` go from out of line to inlined as well.
Details are in the comments.

There is no new test because behaviour is unchanged:
`assert_equality_cases` for `Box` and `Inline` already covers all three
arms. Following the guidance on #504 there is no separate changelog
fragment. Instead, the unreleased #455 fragment, which says `eq` is
`#[inline]`, now says `#[inline(always)]` and why.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D
warnings` and `cargo test --workspace` pass.

json: support a custom repeated_type on repeated enum fields (#714)

Fixes #628.

A `repeated` enum field with a custom `repeated_type` did not compile
under `generate_json(true)`. `repeated_enum::deserialize` and
`repeated_closed_enum::deserialize` returned a concrete `Vec`, so a
field typed `CustomList<EnumValue<E>>` or `CustomList<E>` got E0308 from
both the derived `Deserialize` and the hand-generated one.

Both now return any `C: From<Vec<_>>`, the same shape
`proto_seq::deserialize` has had since #234. `ProtoList` already
requires `From<Vec<T>>`, so every valid custom list works, and a `Vec`
field infers `C = Vec<_>` with no change to generated code.
Serialization already took a slice, so it is untouched.

One visible side effect: callers that spell the type parameters with a
turbofish now name the collection too (`deserialize::<E, Vec<_>, _>`).
The only ones in the repo were tests, updated here; the generated
descriptor code infers it from the seed's return type.

Tests: `repeated_enum_modules_deserialize_into_a_custom_list` in
`json_helpers/tests.rs` decodes into a local non-`Vec` list through both
modules. In `buffa-test`, the new `repeated_enum_json.proto` fixture
(edition 2023, one open and one closed repeated enum) is built with
`repeated_type_custom` pointed at the existing `CustomList` and JSON on,
so the crate does not compile without the fix;
`tests/repeated_enum_json.rs` round-trips it through JSON, checks
`null`, and checks lenient skipping of unknown names.

I could not build the workspace on my machine, so `cargo test` has not
run locally and CI is the real check; `cargo fmt --check` passes on the
pinned toolchain. The changelog fragment does not cite a PR number yet.

Happy to move the fixture into an existing file or adjust if you would
rather shape it differently.

---------

fix(env): make the read/bash differential test deterministic and meaningful

The fake tool API lacked retainedOutput, so every bash case threw on both sides
and the test only compared the error text. Its stdout+stderr case also depended
on the order of two concurrently read pipes and failed intermittently in CI.
The API now provides retainedOutput, each bash case writes to one stream, and
bash cases must return a result.

feat(durable): accept functions for HarnessOptions.models and settings

Like env, models and settings may be a function returning the current value.
Generation, compaction, hooks and tools read it at each use (api.models at each
access), so a host can replace its model configuration without reopening the
Harness. A plain object still works.

fix(ai): treat whitespace-only tool output as empty

Whitespace-only tool results (e.g. a bare \r\n from bash) were sent verbatim
to OpenAI Completions, OpenAI Responses, and Google providers. Some providers
reject that with a 400, which then repeats on every request in the session.
They now use the same placeholder as empty output.

closes #8720

fix(coding-agent): remove fixed output limits from summary requests (#11036)

Compaction summaries were limited to 0.8 * compaction.reserveTokens (13107 by default), turn-prefix summaries to 0.5 * reserveTokens, and branch summaries to a hardcoded 4096. On providers where reasoning shares the output limit (OpenAI Responses, adaptive Anthropic), high thinking levels used most of that limit and compaction failed with "generation hit the token cap", even though the model allows far more output.

Tying the limit to reserveTokens assumed the summary request is as large as the full context, so its output had to fit in the reserved space. It is usually much smaller: recent messages kept by keepRecentTokens are not sent, a split turn goes to a separate request, tool results are truncated, and tool definitions and the normal system prompt are not included. Manual compaction can also run long before the context is full. The provider layer already sizes output from the actual request, using the model's output limit reduced to fit the remaining context, as for normal turns.

Summary requests now set no maxTokens and rely on that. compaction.reserveTokens only controls when compaction starts.

generateSummary() and generateSummaryWithUsage() now ignore the reserveTokens parameter.

espressif: drop CONFIG_FREERTOS_WATCHPOINT_END_OF_STACK from the example defaults (#4236)

On a RISC-V target (P4, S31) with a debugger attached, every context switch
re-arms the stack watchpoint through a semihosting ebreak, so openocd halts
the core at task rate: USB service stops, the attach itself sometimes lands
in the panic handler, and the chip boot-loops after openocd exits. ESP-IDF
leaves the option off by default and the canary stack check stays on.
Dropping it frees one hardware trigger and shrinks configMINIMAL_STACK_SIZE
by 60 bytes, so tasks sized from that constant get smaller allocations,
partly offset by the up-to-60-byte region the watchpoint reserved.

repos.description: idb is a flexible command line interface for automating iOS simulators and devices

commits.message:
Install releases from facebook/fb rather than a local tap

Summary:
`homebrew.py install <tag>` no longer writes a release's attached formulae into the `idb-local/builds` tap. A release now installs from `facebook/fb` itself, so the local tap only ever holds CI builds:

- The tag must be the release facebook/fb carries, which is the `tag` recorded in the tap's `idb-release.json`. Any other tag is refused, with a message naming the release the tap carries.
- brew's clone of facebook/fb must already resolve that version. If it doesn't, the install stops before changing anything and says to run `brew update`, rather than letting `brew install` quietly install a different version.
- Formulae already installed from facebook/fb are left for `brew install` to upgrade in place. Local builds are replaced without asking, and anything from elsewhere still needs confirmation.
- `builds` and the picker mark only that release as installable, and name the release facebook/fb carries on every other row.

CI builds install from `idb-local/builds` exactly as before.

___

Summary:

Inventories are no longer written down: they are read from `BUCK`, `defs.bzl` and the source tree. Workflows live in the `idb-development` skill, and library design in each library's README.

Always-on cost, by the chars/4 estimate the agent rules tooling reports:

| Working in | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `fbobjc/Tools/idb/` | ~23,980 tokens (`idb.md`, 95,926 chars) | ~2,080 tokens (`idb.md` + `idb-swift.md`, 8,315 chars) |
| `fbcode/idb/` | ~510 tokens (`open-source-sync.md`), plus ~23,980 whenever `idb.md` also matched | ~970 tokens (`idb-client.md` + `idb.md`) |
| `xplat/idb/` | ~23,980 tokens whenever `idb.md` matched | ~970 tokens (`idb-proto.md` + `idb.md`) |

That removes ~21,900 tokens from every request that loads the Swift rules. Claude's tokenizer measured ~36k tokens on a slightly smaller revision of the old `idb.md`, so the real saving is larger than the estimate.

The rule is split by audience, so each change loads only what applies to it:

- `idb.md` (all three trees): what idb is, what is published and how to keep internal context out of it, the GitHub CI that alone checks the open-source build, how changes reach users through releases and the Homebrew tap, additive wire changes landed one layer at a time, where each kind of knowledge lives, and keeping the open-source build honest.
- `idb-swift.md` (`fbobjc/Tools/idb/` only): grow laterally — a capability is its own library extending `Simulator` from outside, so `FBControlCore` and `FBSimulatorControl` stay small — plus rules on reporting only observed results, lifetimes and cancellation, the private-API boundary (Objective-C only where a private API or the runtime forces it), keeping API surface small, and updating the libraries' outside consumers in the same diff as a public rename.
- `fbcode/idb` and `xplat/idb` reach `idb.md` through small rules with `deps:`. `open-source-sync.md` is folded into `idb.md`.

Every rule is scoped to the idb trees themselves. The previous `idb.md` matched `.*idb/.*`, which the rules engine searches for anywhere in any in-scope path, and `open-source-sync.md` had no path filter at all.

Several claims in the previous rule had drifted from the code — for example, Smoke suites do not boot their own simulator — and are dropped rather than carried over.

No behavioural change to idb.

- **Traversal:** idb has no traversal option, so an axbridge read uses the automatic traversal, which walks `semantic` when a client is named.

No client sets the field yet; the next diff adds `--client-type`.

Reviewed By: williamtwilson

Summary:
The in-simulator bridge now refuses an accessibility read that doesn't say which traversal to run or which client to claim, and a hit-test that doesn't say which client to claim. Before, it fell back to `view-hierarchy` and `noClient`. No read's output changes: the host has sent both fields on every request since they were introduced.

- **Refusals:** a missing field is a bad request naming the valid values, the same as a malformed one.
- **Command line:** the bridge's manual form needs `--traversal` and `--client-type`.
- **Protocol version:** goes from 2 to 3. Builds made between the version-2 change and the addition of `clientType` send version-2 frames without that field. commits.message:
patch: Fix macOS app menu-bar launch identity (#2095) ## Why Fixes #2092. Launching the macOS app through its shell wrapper replaces the app executable with Python. AppKit then sees Python's bundle instead of Free Claude Code, and the menu-bar item can have a zero-height window even though pystray reports it visible. ## How - Run the installed uv-managed Python runtime inside a native app executable, preserving the app's bundle identity and main thread. Enable UTF-8 and retain the tool environment for imports and child processes. - Build arm64 and x86_64 launchers during release staging and include both in the existing wheel and source distribution. Select the launcher matching the installed Python architecture. - Create and ad-hoc sign the app through a Python installer helper. Validate its runtime, stage replacements, preserve foreign apps and Desktop entries, and recognize existing FCC ownership markers during upgrades and uninstall. - Add native macOS coverage for bundle identity, visible menu-bar geometry, server lifecycle, duplicate launches, child processes, and reinstall. Add Windows and Linux source-distribution rebuild checks and require these jobs in CI.

Confidence Score: 5/5

No outstanding findings prevent merging.

Summary

 The PR replaces the macOS shell launcher with a native executable that keeps Free Claude Code's app identity while running its installed Python environment. - The macOS app keeps its identity while running the desktop app. - Release packages carry native launchers for both Mac architectures. - CI checks the native Mac app on Intel and Apple silicon.

time it fired, so at our 1 ms ACK_DELAY_MS every tunnel connection

Merge pull request #2040 from doronz88/sysmontap-ur

Merge pull request #2039 from doronz88/hid-auth-warmup

core_device: Wait longer for HID surfaces to authenticate in touch_session

core_device: Wait longer for HID surfaces to authenticate in touch_session

touch_session paused 0.3 s after starting the media stream before yielding.
backboardd re-matches the HID surfaces against the authenticated stream
asynchronously. On an iPhone 11 that takes longer than 0.3 s, so the first
CONTACT of a one-shot tap landed on an externalAccessory surface and was
dropped every time. 0.4 s was already enough there, so wait 0.5 s and name
the pause next to KEYBOARD_ATTACH_SETTLE_SECONDS.

Closes #2036

sysmontap: Emit at the sampling interval instead of every 1 ms

The config hardcoded "ur" (the output rate) to MINIMUM_INTERVAL_MS, so the
device pushed ~2300 mostly-empty DTX messages per second whatever the
sampling interval was, keeping DTServiceHub at ~20% CPU. Set "ur" to
interval_ms so the device emits once per sample.

Closes #2037

Merge pull request #2034 from doronz88/binary-declarative

binary: Add composable codecs for variable-length data

binary: Drop the helpers that codecs replace

encode_utf8_cstring(), pad_to(), ByteReader.prefixed() and
ByteReader.read_utf8_cstring() have no callers left: use CSTRING.build(),
Aligned, Prefixed and CSTRING.read().

core_profile_session_tap: Read C strings with CString

The kcdata name parser decoded read_cstring() by hand; it is CString with the
"replace" error handler.

tunnel_service: Declare TLV8 items and tunnel packets as records

PairingDataComponentTLV8 is a record with a u8 type and a u8-prefixed body,
and CDTunnelPacket/RPPairingPacket are records with their magic and a
u16-prefixed body, replacing the header records and hand-written parse and
build. Encodings are unchanged; a TLV8 item with more than 255 bytes of data
now raises BinaryBuildError (a ValueError, as before) naming the field.

afc: Declare the fopen and make-link requests as records

AfcFopenRequest and AfcMakeLinkRequest are BinaryStructs with C string fields
instead of hand-written build() methods; path-only requests use
CSTRING.build(). The encoded requests are unchanged.

remotexpc: Build the payload-to-object dispatch table once

_build_xpc_object() created its 11-entry dispatch dict, lambdas included, for
every value it converted. Converting a 57-value request now takes 7 us
instead of 28 us.

remotexpc: Declare XPC objects with codecs

The per-type parser and builder tables become one Switch: STRING and DATA are
Aligned(4, Prefixed(U32_LE, ...)), ARRAY and DICTIONARY are prefixed arrays of
XpcObject, and XpcFileTransfer is a record with an XpcObject field. Parsing
and building are byte-for-byte unchanged; build errors now name the XPC type
(e.g. "BOOL: cannot encode 'x'") instead of "XpcObject".

binary: Add composable codecs for variable-length data

Variable-length formats were read and built by hand with ByteReader. They
can now be declared, as with construct:

    STRING = Aligned(4, Prefixed(U32_LE, CSTRING))
    OBJECT = Switch(U32_LE, {1: STRING, 2: U64_LE})

A codec is anything with read(reader) and build(value): Prefixed, Aligned,
PrefixedArray, Tuple, Switch, CString, GreedyBytes and Pass, the scalars
(U32_LE etc., now a struct.Struct subclass; U8 and U16_BE are new), Bytes(n),
and BinaryStruct record classes. A record field annotated with a codec makes
the record variable-length; such fields follow the fixed-size ones.

An error raised inside nested codecs records the enclosing cases, elements
and fields in BinaryDataError.path, e.g.
"DICTIONARY -> [2] -> STRING at offset 104: expected 200 bytes, found 16".

binary: Read nested byte ranges without copying

ByteReader.sub() and prefixed() copied the bytes they confine a reader to,
so every nested XPC container, kcdata item and pcapd payload was copied once
per level. A sub-reader is now a window on the same buffer with a narrower
end, and BinaryStruct.read() stops at that end.

ByteReader.data is now always the whole buffer: read a sub-reader's bytes
with read_all(). skip() consumes bytes without returning them.

Reduce CTC keyword-scoring memory and CPU work (#1034)

### Why is this change needed?

CTC keyword scoring built full expanded and projected history tables,
although each recurrence reads only the previous row and both spotting
callers consume only the completed-keyword column.

Keep two expanded-state rows and retain terminal scores/start/end
frames. DP storage becomes O(T + N), preserving predecessor ties, blank
costs, wildcard handling and detection behavior. Add a regression
requiring independent spans for disjoint keyword occurrences.

Validation:
- 18 focused algorithm checks pass against exact production source in an
isolated XCTest harness.
- Bit-exact terminal scores/spans and spotting outputs for 110 cases
from real CTC evidence, including 440 constrained searches.
- ASR-only Release consumer build and contribution formatting lint pass;
existing naming/style warnings remain. Full SDK suite was not run.
- Four alternating optimized process pairs reduced a 75-call scoring
batch from 10.78 ms to 1.42 ms (86.8%). This excludes model inference
and is not a whole-transcription speedup.

fix(tts/kokoro-ane-v3): allocate inputs with tail slack to stop NaN audio on macOS 27 (#1038)

Fixes #1037.

On macOS 27.0, Kokoro ANE v3 failed with `invalidInput("Invalid audio
output")` on ~5–6 s English sentences that fall past the 200-frame fast
bucket and take the original Vocoder + Tail path. The Vocoder returned
an all-NaN `x_pre` from finite, in-range inputs. The v3 array helpers
were adapted from the legacy ones but dropped the slack-backed
allocation the legacy runtime uses to cover the OS 27 BNNS input
overread; re-wrapping just `x_source_1` in a slack-backed buffer made
the output finite.

- `KokoroAneV3Arrays` fp16/fp32/int32 builders and `resizeTime` now
allocate through `KokoroAneArrays.makeArray` (zeroed 16 KB tail slack).
- New `KokoroAneV3ArraysTests` asserts the slack is present and zeroed,
and that `resizeTime` keeps values and zero-pads.

Verified on M5 Pro / macOS 27.0 (26A428): reporter's sentence family
11/72 failing (T = 231–239) → 72/72 pass; the repro sentence renders
139,800 samples. Async prediction and the hosted vs locally compiled
Vocoder bundle were ruled out.

* ci: run build and test jobs only for the paths a PR changes

Add a changes job (dorny/paths-filter) that classifies a pull request's
changed files into package, integration, and examples. The Xcode matrices,
SPM, Linux, and docs jobs run only for package changes; integration tests
also run for Tests/IntegrationTests/**; the Examples jobs also run for
Examples/**. Spell check, format check, and SwiftLint still always run.

Pushes to main and release/* and manual runs still run every job, so the
Release workflow's dependency on a successful CI run is unchanged.
ci-success already treats skipped jobs as passed, and now also depends on
changes so a failed filter cannot pass CI by skipping everything.

* ci: make the paths-filter negation exclusion-aware

With the default predicate-quantifier ("some") a negated pattern matches
every file outside it, so "!Tests/IntegrationTests/supabase*/**" made the
package filter true for any PR. Use some-with-excludes, and move the
positive rules into a shared anchor so the integration filter does not
inherit the exclusion.

fix(postgrest): give each range type its own _PostgresRange bound marker (#1575)

The typegen mapped int4range and int8range to _PostgresRange<Int>, and
tsrange, tstzrange and daterange to _PostgresRange<Date>. So a daterange
operand on a tstzrange column compiled, and Postgres then compared a date
with a timestamp.

Bound is a phantom type, so each range type now gets its own caseless
marker: _Int4Range, _Int8Range, _NumRange, _TSRange, _TSTZRange and
_DateRange. A new compile-failure fixture rejects a daterange operand on a
tstzrange column.

Fixes SDK-2210

perf(postgrest): encode and decode _PostgresBytes hex without a String per byte (#1574)

* perf(postgrest): encode and decode _PostgresBytes hex without a String per byte

Encode with a 16-entry digit table into one preallocated buffer and build
the String once. Decode each hex digit straight from the UTF-8 bytes. The
decoder now also rejects a sign character such as \x+f, which
UInt8(_:radix:) accepted.

Fixes SDK-2209

Appending to Data one byte at a time cost about 25 ns per byte. Filling a
preallocated [UInt8] and building Data once decodes 1 MB in about 4 ms
instead of 24 ms.

commits.message: Clean up failed browser reconnect initialization (#6102) A canceled or failed browser reconnect leaves its replacement connection open and publishes an incomplete session manager. Close the replacement client and clear its manager and focus before propagating the original error. Regression tests cover cancellation and connection errors during target discovery and automatic attachment. The regression fails against the original source. Five session tests, one live Chromium recovery test, pre-commit, and Pyright pass. This change does not replay actions or restore an unresponsive upstream browser. --- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Changes the CDP reconnect failure path and cancellation handling; success-path behavior is unchanged but incorrect cleanup here could affect auto-reconnect reliability. > > **Overview** > **Fixes leaked state when `reconnect()` fails or is cancelled mid-setup.** Previously, a partial reconnection could leave a replacement CDP WebSocket client running and expose a half-built `SessionManager` on the session. > > `reconnect()` now wraps the post-`start()` initialization (session manager, `setAutoAttach`, focus restore, proxy auth, WS drop callback) in `try`/`except BaseException`. On any failure it immediately clears `_cdp_client_root`, `session_manager`, and `agent_focus_target_id`, then runs shielded async cleanup to `stop()` the replacement client and `clear()` the manager before re-raising the original error or `CancelledError`. > > New CI tests simulate failures during `Target.setDiscoverTargets` / `Target.setAutoAttach` (connection error, task cancel, and cancel during client `stop`) and assert the session is left with no client, manager, or focus and that cleanup ran. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e16388ba6e2975f539f597b9e81ab3a69451ee3d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot). --- ## Summary by cubic A failed or cancelled browser reconnect now cleans up its replacement CDP client, session manager, and focus target before propagating the original error or cancellation. - The cleanup runs to completion even when the reconnect task is cancelled mid-teardown, then re-raises the cancellation. - Regression tests cover cancellation and connection errors during target discovery, automatic attachment, and cleanup shutdown. Recover OpenAI browser reads and improve task file access (#6099)

Browser observations could stop the OpenAI runner after transient
failures. Scoped reads also returned invalid labels and replaced valid
element references.

This change adds bounded recovery for state, page reads, and
screenshots. Diagnostics no longer block ordinary actions. Reads retain
references and include the full URL. Output limits shrink to 10,000
characters. Bash uses the configured Python environment and separates
caches from deliverables.

The quickstart enables all browser tools, Bash, Cloud, and native
Responses compaction. The driver never replays uncertain clicks or
typing. Persistent state failures still stop the SDK runner.

Validation: 43 integration tests passed; one skipped. Pre-commit and
type checks passed. Live Cloud smoke:
https://github.com/browser-use/new-eval-platform/actions/runs/38856733788
passed with 21 model turns, 22 compaction events, no tool errors, and
verified Cloud upload/download contents.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core OpenAI browser driver behavior (reconnect, retries,
truncation limits, and ref stability), which could affect agent
workflows; Bash environment isolation reduces accidental secret leakage
but alters default Python/HOME for tool runs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens the OpenAI **BrowserUse** driver against transient CDP
failures and oversized tool payloads. **State** now times out,
reconnects once on transport errors, and tracks **crashed** tabs with
clear errors. **Page reads**, **screenshots**, and accessibility work
get bounded timeouts with a single retry; reads keep stable `ref_*` IDs,
prepend **title/URL**, and no longer wipe refs on every read.
**Diagnostics** attach on a separate timeout-wrapped CDP client and
failures no longer block normal page actions.
> 
> Observation and Bash output caps drop from **50k to 10k** bytes/chars,
with tighter scoped-read JSON and UTF-8-safe labels (including unnamed
controls). Shared **`run_bash`** gains optional **`python_executable`**
and **`home_dir`**; the OpenAI **Bash** tool defaults to
`sys.executable` and isolates `HOME` under `outputs/.tmp/home`.
> 
> The **quickstart** demo wires full browser tools, Bash file output,
Cloud, and Responses compaction. Integration tests cover reconnect,
diagnostic timeouts, screenshot/read retries, crash handling, and custom
Python in Bash.
>

90d2dc6f0cfe96a36bad4458c97345e4ec7e2065. Bugbot is set up for automated
code reviews on this repo. Configure

## Change

Rewrite `CLOUD.md` (2,704 lines -> ~90) as current Browser Use Cloud
facts:

- Cloud browsers over CDP first: $0.02/browser-hour, $5/GB residential
proxy, CAPTCHA solving on by default, profiles, live view, opt-in
recording, 60-minute default / 240-minute max timeout, 10 -> 1,000
shared agent+browser concurrency by lifetime payments, a Playwright
`connect_over_cdp` snippet.
- Then the V4 Agents API (`from browser_use_sdk.v4 import BrowserUse`,
`client.runs.create(...)`) and the MCP server.
- Deleted: v2 quickstart and the full v2 API reference, "Sessions are
currently limited to 15 minutes", the "$15 signup credit" (pricing says
$1 once), and the "Instructions for AI Agents" / "we mainly
encourage..." framing.
- Stealth Bench V2 is labelled as Browser Use's own benchmark and
carries the site-selection caveat, the
every-provider-ran-its-own-proxy/stealth/solver note, and Browserbase's
standard-mode note (Verified needs Enterprise). States that Cloud is
hosted only and not open source; related MIT projects include the
library and Browser Harness.
- Points existing integrators to the API V2 and V3 docs; labels the MCP
server as V3.

## Why

AI coding agents cite this file. In a clean Oct 15 run (40 developer
questions x Claude Code + Codex x 2 seeds), Browser Use was picked 0/12
times on the three cloud-browser questions (Steel/Hyperbrowser
alternatives, Browserbase alternatives, browser API). Codex on the
Steel-alternatives question (seed 1) cited this `CLOUD.md` and filed
Browser Use Cloud as "Hosted AI browser tasks", not as a CDP browser.
The old file led with v2 agent tasks and a 15-minute session limit, and
buried browsers under "we mainly encourage" agent use. Expected effect:
at most 1 flip on these questions; not yet measured.

Every fact links to its source and was checked today:
- Price, proxy, $1 signup credit, concurrency range:
https://browser-use.com/pricing.md
- CAPTCHA default and `solveCaptchas`:
https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/captcha-handling

https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/api-v4/browsers/create-browser-session
- Recording off by default, `liveUrl`:
https://docs.browser-use.com/cloud/browser/live-preview
- Concurrency tiers:

Prevent upper PRLAR_EL1 address corruption (#1512)

This prevents the upper 2-bytes of the
PRLAR_EL1 address from being set during
MPU address checks.

We thank Claude and Ada Logics for their help identifying this issue.

Update port auth buffer size to be arch dependent (#1511)

Use the hardware-natural word size for buffer length. This
enables 64 bit systems.

We thank Claude and Ada Logics for their help identifying this issue.

portable: remove stray installer URL from IAR TrustZone non-secure ports (#1492)

A stray IAR installer download URL was left outside the comment delimiters
in the restore_special_regs section of the IAR TrustZone non-secure ports.
The assembler parses the bare URL as an operand of the preceding ldmia, so
any build of these ports aborts with:

    Error: garbage following instruction -- 'ldmia r2!,{r0,r3,lr} http:'

The line is outside the configENABLE_PAC conditional block, so it breaks
every configuration of the port, not only PAC-enabled builds.

Commit 78e0cc7 ("ARMv8.1-M: Add task dedicated PAC key support", #1195)
introduced the URL in the CM33/CM35P/CM55/CM85 and ARMv8M non-secure
ports. The CM52 (#1334) and STAR-MC3 (#1363) ports inherited it when
their portasm.s was created from an already-affected file.

The stray URL is removed rather than moved inside the comment, matching
the unaffected sibling port ARM_CM23/non_secure/portasm.s, which carries
the same comment text without any URL.

Verified with arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.3.1: all six files fail to assemble
before the change and assemble cleanly after it.

Relates to #1480. The ARM_CM33 non-secure port is handled separately by
#1485, so it is intentionally not touched here.

* portable: fix stray installer URL in IAR ARM_CM33 non-secure port

portable/ARMv8M/copy_files.py derives the non-secure IAR ports from
portable/ARMv8M/non_secure/portable/IAR/ARM_CM33. The previous commit
fixed that source directory but did not regenerate the ARM_CM33 copy, so
portable/IAR/ARM_CM33/non_secure/portasm.s still carried the stray URL.
mpu_wrappers_v2_asm.S and portmacro.h are already identical between
source and destination, so re-running the script changes only this file.

With this commit all seven files that carry the stray URL are fixed,
which makes #1485 (same file, same line) unnecessary.

Correction to the previous commit message: the stray URL is in the #else
branch of #if ( configENABLE_MPU == 1 ), so it is not every configuration
of the port. It breaks every non-MPU build, independently of
configENABLE_PAC; MPU builds never compile the line.

Verified with arm-none-eabi-gcc 13.3.1 (GNU as, not IAR iccarm), using
-march=armv8.1-m.main -mthumb -mfpu=fpv5-d16 and a minimal IAR-to-GNU
directive translation:

  configENABLE_MPU=0, configENABLE_PAC=0   fails before, assembles after
  configENABLE_MPU=1                       line is not compiled

The PAC_KEY_* mrs/msr instructions are rejected by GNU as on this target,
so the PAC-enabled non-MPU configuration could not be exercised here.

Relates to #1480.

commits.message:
Keep animated frames intact in Flip, Rotate 180, Zoom and Resize (#558)

Several transforms treated the stacked frames of a multi-page image as one tall image:

- Flip(DirectionVertical) and Rotate(Angle180) reversed the frame order.
  They now map each loaded page through the operation and restack, via a
  new vipsMapPages helper that vipsExtractAreaMultiPage also uses.
- Zoom left the page height at the pre-zoom value, so an x2 y2 zoom read
  as twice as many half-frames. It now scales the page height by yFactor.
- ResizeWithVScale rounded the strip height and the page height
  separately, so whenever pageHeight*scale wasn't whole the strip came
  out a few rows short and libvips dropped the page height (the #350
  'toilet roll'). When the roundings disagree, the vertical scale is now
  chosen so the strip is exactly pages*newPageHeight, as vips_thumbnail
  does. Output is unchanged when they already agree.
- ResizeWithVScale, Zoom and Flip count loaded pages as
  Height()/PageHeight() rather than Pages(), like Rotate after #555.

Fixes #554

Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the source ICC profile in WebP exports (#556)

webpsave was always given profile="none" when no IccProfile was set,
so WebP output dropped the source ICC even with StripMetadata: false,
unlike JPEG/PNG/TIFF. Pass a profile only when the caller supplied one,
and "none" only for StripMetadata without Keep (webpsave in libvips
8.14.0-8.14.1 ignores strip, fixed in 8.14.2, so "none" is what drops
the ICC there).

Fixes #552

Co-authored-by: diego.choi <diego.choi@kakaocorp.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Count loaded pages in Rotate (#555)

Pages() is the page count of the file, so Rotate(Angle90/270) failed with 'bad grid geometry' when only some pages were loaded.

commits.message:
fix(odf): move hidden ODT sections to the invisible content layer (#4860)

Signed-off-by: Ankit Kumar <ankitkumar19473@gmail.com>

fix(reading-order): bound page-separator candidate work and honor document_timeout (#4633)

Pages whose vector geometry yields tens of thousands of tiny separator
candidates (e.g. venue seat maps drawn as small rectangles) sent the
quadratic candidate merge in build_page_separators into an unbounded run,
and the assembly stage had no document_timeout checkpoint, so the whole
conversion blocked forever (docling-project/docling#4632).

- Skip separator extraction for a page when the raw candidate count
  exceeds _MAX_SEPARATOR_CANDIDATES; reading order falls back to the
  pre-separator behavior for that page.
- Bound separator extraction with an optional time limit: candidate
  collection and the merge fixpoint abort to "no separators" (never a
  partial merge, which could reintroduce ordering-graph cycles) once the
  budget is exhausted.
- Wire the remaining document_timeout budget through the pipeline:
  _build_document records an absolute _conversion_deadline on the
  ConversionResult; _assemble_document passes the remaining budget to
  ReadingOrderModel, which records a TIMEOUT error when the budget is
  exceeded.

Signed-off-by: Junyi Yao <64238008+Kylinny@users.noreply.github.com>

feat(asr): prefetch the native Distil-Whisper presets with docling-tools (#4825)

Add whisper_distil_small_en, whisper_distil_medium_en, whisper_distil_large_v3 and whisper_distil_large_v3_5 to docling-tools models download. They fetch the OpenAI-format checkpoints that the native Distil presets load, into the output directory's Hugging Face cache layout, which is the layout the native transcriber already reads when artifacts_path is set. Plain --all still excludes them, and --all --asr includes them.

Move _DISTIL_WHISPER_OPENAI_CHECKPOINTS from the transcriber to asr_model_specs, next to the presets it describes, so the downloader and the transcriber share one table. docling.utils already depends on vlm_model_specs for the same reason, so tach.toml gets the matching asr_model_specs edges.

The missing-checkpoint error under artifacts_path now gives the docling-tools command instead of hf download.

Signed-off-by: BBC, Esquire <bbc@chintellalaw.com>

feat(asciidoc): parse bold, italic and monospace in paragraphs (#4824)

Inline formatting marks stayed in the paragraph text as literal "*",
"_" and "`", and the Markdown export escaped them ("\_italic\_").

Split paragraph text into runs. Doubled marks ("**", "__", "``") apply
anywhere; single marks apply only at word boundaries, so "snake_case"
and "2*3*4" stay plain, as in Asciidoctor. Bold and italic can be
nested. A paragraph with formatting becomes an inline group of text
items with formatting and code items for monospace, the same structure
the Markdown backend builds. A paragraph without marks is unchanged.

The three places that added a paragraph now all go through
_flush_text_data, so every paragraph gets the same handling.

Signed-off-by: Aeshvarya Awasthi <aeshvarya310305@gmail.com>

fix(pptx): map grouped shape boxes through the group transform (#4859)

Shapes inside a group report their position in the group's child
coordinate space (a:chOff/a:chExt). Once the group is moved, resized or
flipped, that space no longer matches the slide, so the provenance box
pointed at the wrong place. Map each box through the a:off/a:ext and
flips of every enclosing group.

Resolves #4857

Signed-off-by: Yihang Chen <yhc0720@berkeley.edu>

feat(asr): transcribe with a remote OpenAI-compatible server (#4853)

Add ApiAsrOptions for the ASR and video pipelines: the audio is posted to an
/v1/audio/transcriptions endpoint (a Whisper server deployed on its own, or a
hosted service) with response_format=verbose_json, and the timed segments become

Nothing is loaded in the Docling process and FFmpeg is not needed for audio

commits.message: Merge branch 'master' into owm

Radio self-test: find a USB charger on GPIO19/20, name wires by pins

On a hand-wired Yellow AP powered through the S3 devkit's "USB" port, the
test reported "TX and RX of the debug UART are swapped" and "Debug TX
wire not connected" with correct wiring, and the C6 update failed (#586).
That port is wired to GPIO19/20, the S3's USB D-/D+, which the Yellow AP
uses for the radio's debug UART, and a USB charger connects D+ and D-:
the radio's output then shows up on the S3's TX pin as well, and what
the S3 sends collides with it. Measured on an S3 devkit: with a charger
the two pins follow each other both ways; a PC's 15k pull-downs only
make them follow low, and the test and the C6 update work from a PC.

New first step: with the radio held in reset, each S3 TX/RX pair is
checked for a connection in both directions. A connection is reported
and ends the test; for GPIO19/20 on an S3 the message says to plug the
charger into the other ("UART"/"COM") port or use a computer.

The messages now name wires by their pins, as in the pinout table,
instead of "protocol UART", "UART0", ROM or RDY?, and say what to do,
e.g. "The wires on S3 GPIO 17 and GPIO 18 are swapped: swap them" or
"No contact on the wire from S3 GPIO 20 to the radio's RX (C6 GPIO 17)".

Tested on an S3 devkit (charger, PC, nothing on the USB port) and on the
Yellow AP: real wiring twice and the ten simulated faults, each with its
new message, the radio online after every run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

C6 update and radio reader: more stack

The C6 update task downloads the firmware over HTTPS, so the TLS
handshake runs on its stack. Measured on the Yellow AP: of 6400 bytes
only 96 were left after an update from a release URL. A Mini AP v4
(CORE_DEBUG_LEVEL=1, USB CDC) went over the edge: "Crash in task
OTAUpdateTask", cause 65 (64 + debug exception: the end-of-stack
watchpoint), PC in vTaskSwitchContext, reported by Skip. Now 10240
bytes; 3928 left with the same update.

rxSerialTask had 616 of 1750 bytes left in normal use. One of Ei-Qt's
crashes in #586 was an ESP_LOG from the UART driver (vprintf) inside
this task; the cause, the driver deleted under the running reader, is
fixed in 1ba8b875, but a single log line should not overflow the task.
Now 3072 bytes.

The S3 OTA task keeps 6144 bytes: 2980 left, as the web UI downloads it
over plain HTTP. Internal heap stays at about 176 KB free (lowest 125
KB, 131 KB during a C6 update).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.message:
refactor(motors): one rustypot-backed SerialMotorsBus for Feetech and Dynamixel (#4672)

* refactor(motors): drive the Feetech and Dynamixel buses through rustypot

The Feetech and Dynamixel buses reached the wire through the vendors'
pure-Python SDKs, behind a layer shaped like them (port and packet
handlers, group sync readers and writers), and carried their own control
tables: addresses, sizes, sign bits, resolutions, baud rate codes and
model numbers transcribed from the vendor manuals, plus the code applying
them -- byte order, sign encoding, the ID sweep and its timeout.

rustypot implements both protocols in Rust, releases the GIL for the
whole transaction, and states and applies those facts itself. Each family
now names its servo definitions in `_servos()`, the rustypot controller
classes. The base bus resolves a model to one of them (rustypot spells
XL330M288 where LeRobot writes xl330-m288) and a register name by
lowering it, and on connect opens a `rustypot.Bus` with each motor's
definition. Models of one family therefore share a port -- STS and SCS,
XL430 and XL330 -- each read and written in its own byte order and sign
encoding. Retries, sync reads on servos without Sync Read, and the bus
scan are rustypot's as well.

Feetech's `protocol_version` goes: STS and SCS differ in byte order, in
whether they answer Sync Read and in which registers they have, and the
definition knows all three. The handshake accepts any model number a
definition covers, `scan_port()` sweeps the bus itself in place of
`broadcast_ping()`, and `setup_motor()` reaches a new motor at whatever
id it answers through the motor's own definition. `disconnect()` is safe
on a closed bus and releases the port even when disabling torque fails.

Gone: both tables.py, encoding_utils.py, the SDK-shaped protocols, the
`MotorsBus` alias, and deepdiff from the motor extras. pyserial stays in
them for `lerobot-find-port`. rustypot 1.10.0 is the first release that
carries the servo metadata and the multi-definition `Bus`.

The devices that relied on the old surface follow: HopeJR's hand drops
`protocol_version` and sync-reads its SCS servos, OpenArm Mini asks the
bus for the motor resolution, and LeKiwi clamps wheel speeds to the
sign-magnitude range of Goal_Velocity.

Tests replace the byte-level SDK mocks with an in-memory `rustypot.Bus`
keyed by motor id and register name. The IO helpers shared by both
families are tested once, on the base bus.

* docs: document the rustypot-backed motor buses

The install steps stop sending users to the vendor SDKs, the hardware
guide lists the servos rustypot defines and points new models at rustypot
rather than at control tables that no longer exist, and the API page
documents SerialMotorsBus and both family buses.

* build(deps): rustypot 1.11.0, and one serial-motors extra

rustypot 1.11.0 finds a servo model by name with its exact model number,
states what differs between families (homing offset sign, operating mode
values, factory baud rate, whether the EEPROM has a lock), turns the
torque of a whole bus on or off, scans with a broadcast ping, and sets a
new motor's id and baud rate. LeRobot's bus is about to rely on all of it.

One bus class will drive both families, so there is one extra to point
users at: serial-motors installs rustypot and pyserial. feetech and
dynamixel stay, as the names the setup guides use, and now alias it.

* refactor(motors): one SerialMotorsBus for Feetech and Dynamixel

FeetechMotorsBus and DynamixelMotorsBus had become a list of rustypot
classes plus a handful of facts about each family: which way the homing
offset goes, which operating mode value means position control, whether
the drive mode is a register, which acceleration and firmware registers
exist, and the Feetech lock. rustypot 1.11.0 states those facts in its
servo definitions, so SerialMotorsBus is now the one, concrete bus:

- each motor's model is looked up with rustypot.find_model, which gives
  its exact model number and its definition. The handshake and the motor
  search check that exact number again, so an SM8512BL set up as an
  sts3215 is refused, though both share a control table;
- calibration reads and writes the homing offset where the register
  exists (not on the SCS), compares the drive mode where it is a register
  (Dynamixel) and applies it in software elsewhere (Feetech), and centres
  a joint with the homing offset sign of the definition;
- the firmware check runs on the motors that report a firmware major and
  minor version (Feetech); configure_motors writes the acceleration
  registers a motor has; set_operating_mode("position") writes each
  motor's own value for a mode named the same on every family;
- torque goes on or off through rustypot's Bus.set_torque, which tries
  every motor, moves the Feetech lock with the torque, and reports the
  motors that failed: one that does not answer no longer leaves the
  motors after it under torque, and the error names it;
- setup_motor has rustypot change the id and the baud rate (torque off
  and lock open first), with no reopening of the bus, and puts the port
  back at the default rate even when that fails. The motor search tries
  the default baud rate, then the factory one, then the rest in a fixed
  order, with a broadcast ping where the servo answers one, which covers
  a USB adapter's latency once. scan_port takes the model it looks for,
  releases the port when a scan fails, and reports ids only;
- a status packet is waited for 50 ms, not a second, so one lost reply
  costs a 30 Hz loop a tick (the SDKs waited about 35 to 50 ms).

FeetechMotorsBus and DynamixelMotorsBus stay for one release as
deprecated aliases (FeetechMotorsBus still accepts protocol_version), and
so do their OperatingMode and TorqueMode enums. A missing rustypot points
to the serial-motors extra. Resetting the calibration of an SCS no longer
writes a homing offset it does not have. On Dynamixel, is_calibrated no
longer compares the id stored in the calibration file, like Feetech.

* refactor(robots,teleoperators): drive the motors through SerialMotorsBus

The SO, Koch, OMX, LeKiwi, HopeJR and OpenArm Mini devices built a
FeetechMotorsBus or a DynamixelMotorsBus and wrote operating modes as the
value of a family's enum. They now build a SerialMotorsBus and name the
mode: set_operating_mode("position"), "extended_position", "velocity", or
"current_based_position" for the Dynamixel grippers. DriveMode comes from
lerobot.motors.

* docs: one SerialMotorsBus for Feetech and Dynamixel

The hardware guide builds its example robot on SerialMotorsBus, names
operating modes, and says what the definitions settle between families.
The API page documents SerialMotorsBus and DriveMode, and mentions the
two family classes as deprecated aliases.

* refactor(motors): fold the I/O helpers into their callers, drop scan_port

With the torque and the motor setup handled by rustypot, _write,
_sync_read and _sync_write each had a single caller: write, sync_read and
sync_write now talk to the rustypot bus themselves. _read stays, shared by
read and ping, and always raises; its raise_on_error and err_msg
parameters, which only ping used, go, and ping catches the error instead
of asking not to get one. The Feetech firmware check reads the major and
minor versions with one sync read each rather than two reads per motor.

scan_port goes: nothing in LeRobot calls it, and rustypot's Bus.scan and
Bus.broadcast_scan do the same for anyone who needs it.

The tests that went through the private helpers now go through read,
write, sync_read and sync_write against the in-memory bus.

* fix(motors): restore the port after a failed motor search, check a set-up motor

setup_motor started its cleanup only after finding the motor. The search
walks the baud rates, so a motor that was not there left the port on the
last rate tried, and anything done next on the same bus went unanswered.
The search now runs inside the try whose finally puts the port back at the
default rate.

A motor answers the id and baud rate writes before they take effect, and
nothing checked that they did. setup_motor now reads the model number back
at the new id and the default baud rate, and raises if the motor does not
answer there with the model it is configured as.

* refactor(motors): check selections before writing, raise on sync-read errors, document the bus

- set_operating_mode() and set_half_turn_homings() check every selected motor before
  writing any register, so an unsupported motor leaves no partial configuration.
- sync_read() raises on a motor's error status, as read() does.
- Register names normalise whatever their case; set_baudrate() and ping() need a
  connected bus; resolution() raises for a model that counts no steps; the firmware
  check compares the motors of each servo definition on their own.
- Each model is looked up once, and the bus opens rustypot's Bus through _open_bus()
  and reaches it, typed, through _connected_bus.
- Errors name motors by motor ID; docstrings follow the documentation format and its
  cross-references. The hardware tutorial and the motor API page gain the serial-motors
  extra, the SCS limits, a migration note and the DriveMode members.
- Tests cover write and sync-read error statuses, sync writes no motor answers,
  calibrated commands and calibration mismatches of each family, through bus helpers
  shared by the family suites.

* fix(motors): raise when a motor refuses an access, not on an alarm

A status byte also carries conditions a motor reports while it carries the access out:
a Feetech status only reports alarms (input voltage, temperature, current, load), and on
protocol 2 bit 7 is the alert of a latched hardware fault. Raising on them stopped a
control loop on a gripper squeezing an object, and made ping() miss an overloaded motor.

read(), write(), sync_read() and ping() now fail only when the status says the motor
refused the access: an error number on protocol 2. The protocol-1 servos LeRobot drives
are Feetech ones, which never refuse through their status.

* fix(motors): ask the servo definition whether a status refuses the access

rustypot 1.13.1's ServoDefinition.refuses tells a refusal from an alarm for every
servo it defines, so the bus no longer keeps its own copy of the rule, which assumed
every protocol-1 servo is a Feetech one. The serial-motors extra now needs rustypot
1.13.1, and the tutorial links rustypot's servo guide at that version.

fix(websocket): send Pong from the main task and update esp-ml307 to 3.8.0

On 4G modems, WebSocket callbacks run on the AT event task. The automatic
Pong reply was sent from there and waited for an AT response that only
that task can parse, stalling AT handling until the send timed out.

Register OnPing and schedule SendPong() on the main task. The scheduled
call holds a weak_ptr, so a Pong queued before CloseAudioChannel() or
ResetProtocol() is dropped instead of touching a destroyed WebSocket.

esp-ml307 3.8.0 adds OnPing()/SendPong() and fixes ESP/AT transport
teardown, timeouts and WebSocket frame bounds.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

commits.message:
Merge pull request #3978 from alvations/fix-depgraph-contains-cycle-20261016

Fix DependencyGraph cycle detection, dead on every parsed graph
Name the reference check consistently in the test docstrings
Rename the reference cycle check to _topological_sort_finds_cycle
Cite Kahn 1962 and Chu-Liu/Edmonds, McDonald et al. 2005 in the test docstrings
Satisfy isort and ruff on the moved helper and the cycle-path check

Test the cycle guard on real treebank graphs, fuzzed graphs and the parser

Real inputs and outputs, not toy chains: every Penn dependency_treebank
graph (3914) is acyclic by contains_cycle() and by an independent Kahn
oracle on the head fields, and the edges the walk reads from deps equal the
head edges; a cycle planted in each of 200 real sentences is reported with a
path made of real edges; 1000 seeded random CoNLL graphs agree with the
oracle on truthiness and path validity. The in-tree consumer is covered too:
ProbabilisticNonprojectiveParser's MST step collapses cycles only through
contains_cycle, and with the dead guard its own demo parse was the cyclic,
rootless graph {1->2, 2->1, 2->3}, which the module doctest never inspected
(it checks len(parses) only); it is now the rooted tree 0->1->2->3. On
develop five of the eight tests fail, the three true-negative ones pass.
Place the _dep_addresses helper after the imports
Condense the added comment blocks to three lines or fewer
Drop the _redteam_20261016 suffix from the test file names

Add DependencyGraph cycle-detection regression tests

Asserts contains_cycle detects a real cycle parsed from CoNLL (the teeth: it
returned False before the fix), is a true negative on an acyclic parsed chain,
still returns the documented result on the legacy list-deps form, and that
get_cycle_path follows parsed dict-shaped deps. Passes on Python 3.13 and 3.10.

Fix DependencyGraph cycle detection, dead on every parsed graph

contains_cycle was rewritten to an iterative walk to replace an O(V^3)
transitive-closure blowup (a CPU DoS, CWE-407). The rewrite iterated
node["deps"] directly, and a comment claimed that yields the edge targets the
old code used. It does not: _parse and add_arc store deps as a
relation->[addresses] mapping, so bare iteration yields relation-label keys, not
addresses. Every edge was skipped, so contains_cycle returned False on every
graph parsed from CoNLL / Malt-TAB data, silently disabling the guard and the
cycle-collapse branch of NonprojectiveDependencyParser that is its one in-tree
caller. get_cycle_path had the same bug. _tree and triples were already correct
because they flatten deps.values().

Add _dep_addresses(deps), which flattens the mapping (and accepts the legacy
list-of-addresses form the doctests use), and route contains_cycle and
get_cycle_path through it. A real 1<->2 cycle parsed from CoNLL is now detected;
an acyclic parsed chain still returns False; the list-shaped doctest form still
returns [1, 2, 4, 3].
