commits.message:
Merge pull request #2992 from square/leak-trace-object-ids

Read object ids unsigned, and print each leak trace object's id

Say why the WeakHashMap tests don't use System.runFinalization()

On ART it would wait for the daemon that enqueues cleared references,
because its finalization sentinel goes through that daemon. On HotSpot,
which these tests run on, it only runs the finalizers already queued.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Name related leaking objects the way a leak trace names its objects

The labels naming another leaking object read `Also retains leaking object
0x12d36d08 (android.app.ContextImpl)`, a second spelling of what the leak
trace above them writes as `android.app.ContextImpl instance 0x12d36d08`.
They now use that one: `Also retains android.app.ContextImpl instance
0x12d36d08`, and `Also retained by … instance 0x…, which has its own leak
trace`. The labels that group several objects of a class keep their wording.

Both go through one internal function, so the object line and the labels
can't drift apart again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Print each object's id on its line of a leak trace

A leak trace names an object by its class and the fields that lead to it,
which is enough to read the leak but not to find that object again in the
heap dump it came from. Each object's line now ends with its id,
`├─ java.util.ArrayList instance 0x12d4cd48`, so that it can be handed
straight to Shark Dive: in a `shark://<heap dump>/object?id=…` link, or as
the `object` of a `shark-dive --cli` command. It's the same spelling ahat,
MAT, jhat and Android Studio show for that object. That's in
LeakTrace.toString(), the LeakCanary activity and the leakcanary-app leak
screen, so every leak trace Shark builds has it.

It's display only. LeakTraceObject carries the id in a new objectId
property, and only the rendering reads it: the leak fingerprint is still
built from class and reference names, so it doesn't change. The
serialVersionUID is bumped so that an analysis serialized before this fails
to deserialize, rather than reading back an id of 0.

The leakcanary-app leak screen printed the leaking object on every row of
the path instead of that row's own object, which would have printed the same
id down the whole trace. The LeakCanary activity shares its hex helper with
its heap explorer, which had a private copy.

Android Studio's on-device parser of leak traces expects the last word of
that line to be the type, so it needs updating for this as it already does
for `Verdict:`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Write the remaining object ids in hex

Main already writes object ids in hex in leak traces, HeapObject.toString(), the
not found errors, the Shark CLI and the heap explorer. This covers what was left:

- ObjectDominators.renderDominatorTree() named objects by their position in
  Shark's index, which nothing else can look up. Nothing in the repo called it
  except HprofRetainedHeapPerfTest, to explain a failure, so it moves into that
  test and names objects by their hex id instead.
- Two consistency checks of HprofInMemoryIndex spelled ids by hand, which for a
  class above the 2 GB mark came out as 0x-61544530 in a production failure
  before ids were read unsigned. They use the shared helper now.
- Two Shark Dive tree errors wrote node ids in decimal.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read 4 byte object ids unsigned, like every other heap dump tool

An object id is the address the heap dump recorded the object at. Shark
has read a 4 byte id as a signed Int widened to a Long since its first
parser, copied from perflib with the comment "As long as we don't
interpret IDs, reading signed values here is fine". So every object
above the 2 GB mark of an Android heap dump got a negative id,
0xffffffff82000010 for the object at 0x82000010.

Nothing else spells it that way. Android Studio, ahat, MAT, jhat and
VisualVM all show that object as 0x82000010, and ahat and MAT find
nothing given the 16 digits. Several workarounds grew around the
negative ids: HeapObject.positiveObjectId, hex helpers that mask the
low 32 bits back off, and in Shark Dive a second, exact spelling for
its files, two readings of every address typed into a note, and a
range check instead of a sign check to tell a pile from an object.

Every reader of an id now reads it unsigned, which removes all of
those. The in-memory index stores ids as offsets from the smallest one,
so its keys are unchanged and so are the numbers of the perf tests.
HprofWriter now refuses an id that doesn't fit the heap dump's id size
instead of writing its low bytes, which would read back as a different
id now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Migrate to me.saket.bytesize

Use bytesize 2.3.0, type Retained.heapSize as DecimalByteSize

#2711 pinned the 2.0.0-beta04 prerelease because every stable bytesize
2.x release carries Kotlin 2.2 metadata, which the Kotlin 1.9.25 that
LeakCanary built with then could not read. LeakCanary builds with Kotlin
2.4 since #2841, so this moves to 2.3.0. Since beta04, bytesize also
stopped rendering sizes below -1000 bytes in scientific notation
("-1.7949673E9 B" rather than "-1.79 GB"), which a negative
`retainedIncrease` could reach.

`Retained.heapSize` is typed as the concrete `DecimalByteSize` rather
than the `ByteSize` sealed interface. Shark only ever means decimal
bytes, so the signature says so, and a value class whose static type is
an interface is boxed on every read.

That typing is also what lets 2.3.0's same-precision overloads apply
(saket/byte-size#24). `DecimalByteSize - DecimalByteSize` resolves to an
inline subtraction of two longs instead of the `ByteSize` operator,
which boxed both operands. HotSpot scalar replaces those boxes, ART
doesn't: on an Android 14 arm64 device the interface operator allocated
32 bytes per call. With 2.3.0, the compiled shark classes contain no
`DecimalByteSize.box-impl` outside the `sortedByDescending` comparator
over reported growing nodes, which boxed the old `shark.ByteSize` the
same way.

`shark.api` is regenerated: `shark.ByteSize` is gone, and `Retained`'s
mangled names change, so this breaks binary compatibility even for
callers that never named `ByteSize`.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

(cherry picked from commit 1f9b9397cbc13e003a4be2db6fd62626a797c61d)

Wait for cleared WeakHashMap entries to leave the pending list before dumping

`WeakHashMap with cleared key doesn't take over the path to its value` failed
on CI three times today, on three branches, with the leak trace going from a
JNI global root through `Reference.discovered` to the cleared entry, or
starting at the entry itself, and from there to its value.

That root is the VM's reference pending list. A collection puts everything it
cleared on that list, and the Reference Handler thread moves each reference to
its queue some time later. HotSpot dumps the VM's global handles as JNI global
roots, the head of that list among them, so a heap dump taken in between can
reach the entry's value from the root in one or two references, where the
path the test expects takes seven. clearWeakKeys() was a bare System.gc(), so
whether the handler got there before the dump came down to scheduling, which a
loaded CI runner loses.

Holding the Reference Handler back for 300 ms reproduces it every time: 10
rounds out of 10 failed, with both shapes seen on CI. clearWeakKeys() now waits
for the handler: 10 rounds out of 10 passed, each waiting about 320 ms for a
handler held back 300 ms.

It waits for two sentinels, one per collection, because the handler takes a
collection's whole list at once. The first sentinel coming out of its queue
only says the list it was on has been taken. The second can only come out
once the handler is through the first list, so by then the entries have gone
to the map's own queue, which is a longer path from the root than the one the
test expects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Print a thread's native roots as <Native Local> in a leak trace

Shark reads a thread's JNI_LOCAL and NATIVE_STACK roots as references from
that thread, the way it reads its JAVA_FRAME roots, and they all printed as
<Java Local>. Someone reading a trace through native code was told a Java
method held the object, and would go looking for a variable that isn't there.

So ReferenceLocationType and LeakTraceReference.ReferenceType each get a
NATIVE_LOCAL constant, which JavaLocalReferenceReader uses for the native
roots, and which prints as <Native Local>. A Java frame is still LOCAL and
still <Java Local>, so no existing leak signature changes. The native roots
only started reaching a leak trace through their thread since the last
release, so no released signature changes either.

The new constants are appended rather than placed beside LOCAL, which keeps
every existing ordinal. Nothing in the repo reads one, but a consumer might
have persisted one.

An exhaustive `when` over either enum needs a branch for the new constant,
which is the breaking part. Android Studio's on-device LeakCanary task parses
reference lines and only recognizes <Java Local>, so it can't parse a trace
with <Native Local> in it. It already fails on every analysis from this
release because of the Verdict rename, so that costs it nothing more.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

[rollout, vllm] fix: reject engine_kwargs that override verl-managed vLLM args (#8260)

### What does this PR do?

Some vLLM args are derived from verl's own config (TP, DP, expert
parallelism, LoRA, routing replay) but could also be passed through
`rollout.engine_kwargs.vllm`. Which source won depended on where verl
wrote the derived value, and neither direction was reported:
`tensor_parallel_size` from `engine_kwargs` replaced verl's, while
`enable_expert_parallel` was always overwritten with
`expert_parallel_size > 1`. With the default `expert_parallel_size=1`,
an explicit `engine_kwargs.vllm.enable_expert_parallel=True` became
`False`; every GPU then held all experts (and their LoRA buffers) and
vLLM reported no memory for the KV cache.

This PR keeps verl's config as the only knob for these args.
`engine_kwargs` naming one of them now fails at server start with the
config to set instead:

| vLLM arg | set instead |
|---|---|
| `tensor_parallel_size` | `rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size` |
| `data_parallel_size` | `rollout.data_parallel_size` |
| `enable_expert_parallel` | `rollout.expert_parallel_size` (= TP × DP)
|
| `enable_lora`, `max_lora_rank` | `actor_rollout_ref.model.lora` |
| `enable_return_routed_experts` |
`rollout.enable_rollout_routing_replay` |

The check replaces the delta_sharded-only TP/DP override checks. The one
in-repo script that set `enable_expert_parallel` next to
`expert_parallel_size` drops the redundant line, and the perf doc names
the rollout config.

[fsdp] fix: prevent parameter corruption during FSDP2 CPU offload (#8187)

### What does this PR do?

Prevent silent parameter corruption when moving FSDP2 models to CPU with
uneven parameter shards.

I identified this issue while debugging Qwen3-Omni training and
evaluation failures reported in:

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/issues/660
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8039

The observed symptoms included degraded evaluation accuracy in
multi-node training. The investigation traced the problem to parameter
values changing during CPU offloading, without any forward pass,
backward pass, or optimizer update.

This PR uses blocking device-to-CPU transfers in both affected verl
paths:

- Runtime offloading through `offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`.
- Initialization-time offloading inside `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict`,
which reuses the same helper.

This follows the discussion in:

https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741#issuecomment-6139999835

### Root Cause

`model.to("cpu", non_blocking=True)` can leave a device-to-CPU transfer
in progress while FSDP2 processes the converted parameter.

For uneven shards, `FSDPModule._apply` calls
`FSDPParam.reset_sharded_param`, which may allocate new padded CPU
storage and copy the transferred local tensor into it. This CPU copy can
read the transfer destination before the asynchronous D2H transfer has
completed.

Incorrect values can then persist in the new padded storage.
Synchronizing after the entire `model.to()` call returns does not repair
values that have already been copied into that storage.

This is not specific to NPU: I reproduced the same failure on CUDA by
queuing additional computation before the transfer.

### Design & Code Changes

- Use `model.to("cpu", non_blocking=False)` in
`offload_fsdp2_model_to_cpu`, so each transfer completes before FSDP2
can consume its CPU result.
- Route the CPU move in `fsdp2_load_full_state_dict` through that helper
with `empty_cache=False`, preserving the initialization path's cache
behavior.
- Keep the CPU-to-device helper's `non_blocking=True` argument.
- Update transfer-policy tests to require blocking D2H on both CUDA and
NPU.
- Generalize the NPU regression into `test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py`,
shared by CUDA and NPU CI. It covers nested FSDP2 modules, large
even/uneven weights, and the original small bias vectors.
- Queue warmed-up matrix multiplications on the actual conversion stream
and check both default and non-default streams. Change parameter values
between trials and check CPU values after synchronization to distinguish
persistent corruption from an unfinished transfer.
- Update the CUDA regression so it validates parameter correctness
rather than requiring the pinned allocation associated with the previous
non-blocking D2H path.

The fix uses existing PyTorch module conversion behavior and does not
patch private FSDP2 internals or introduce backend-specific
synchronization code.

### Related Work

- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7347 enabled non-blocking
runtime FSDP2 model transfers for performance. This PR changes the D2H
policy to restore correctness. The initialization-time asynchronous CPU
move predates #7347 and is covered here as well.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/8057 addresses pinned-memory
allocation configuration. It does not establish transfer completion
before FSDP2 reads CPU data.
- https://github.com/verl-project/verl-omni/pull/741 provides a
downstream workaround. This PR addresses the shared verl helpers used by
downstream callers.

### Validation

#### Investigation and downstream validation

The standalone reproducer uses two accelerator processes and a nested
FSDP2 model with either evenly or unevenly sharded weights. It writes
known parameter values, saves an independent blocking CPU reference, and
checks exact equality after offloading.

No forward pass, backward pass, or optimizer update is involved.

| Environment | Configuration | Uneven shards: asynchronous D2H followed
by synchronization | Other cases |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NPU: PyTorch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post6 | 10 iterations, no
additional queued computation | 10/20 rank-trials failed | All passed |
| CUDA: PyTorch 2.11.0, CUDA 13.0 | 50 iterations, 64 queued matrix
multiplications before each transfer | 50/100 rank-trials failed | All
passed |

The other cases include evenly sharded controls, blocking D2H transfers,
and waiting immediately after each individual D2H conversion.
Comparisons use `rtol=0` and `atol=0`.

These are aggregate rank-trial counts; they do not establish that every
failure occurred on the same rank.

I also verified that the downstream fix resolves the reported issues and
allows two-node Qwen3-Omni training to run successfully. The downstream
tests and pre-commit checks passed.

These results establish the failure mechanism and validate the
downstream workaround. They are separate from validation of the final
changes in this verl PR.

#### Regression coverage

The relevant tests cover:

- Transfer policy for runtime and initialization-time CPU offloading.
- Cache-release behavior and buffer placement during initialization.
- Nested FSDP2 modules with even and uneven shards.
- Exact CPU parameter values and device round-trip correctness.
- Queued computation before runtime offloading on default and
non-default streams.
- Per-rank failure reporting after the critical transfer window.

The updated CPU transfer-policy tests were run against the previous
NPU-only implementation and the revised implementation:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider \
  tests/utils/test_fsdp2_model_transfer_on_cpu.py -k 'not sharded_save'
```

- Before: 4 failed, 9 passed, 1 deselected. All four failures were CUDA
D2H policy checks, covering runtime offloading and initialization on
both ranks.
- After: 13 passed, 1 deselected.
- The deselected test is the existing two-process CPU snapshot test,
which checks a separate save-to-CPU helper.

These tests verify transfer policy and control flow using mocked device
transfers. They ran with PyTorch 2.10.0+cpu and imported
`verl.utils.fsdp_utils` from the modified checkout. Accelerator
numerical correctness is covered by the distributed regressions listed
below.

Ruff lint and formatting, Python syntax, workflow YAML parsing, license
checks, device-API checks, and `git diff --check` passed.

I ran the revised numerical regression on a single node with two NPUs.
It passed for both default and non-default streams:
```bash
env -u DIST_INIT_METHOD \
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD:$PYTHONPATH" \
  PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
  torchrun \
    --nnodes=1 \
    --node_rank=0 \
    --nproc-per-node=2 \
    --rdzv_backend=static \
    --master_addr=127.0.0.1 \
    --master_port=29517 \
    tests/special_distributed/test_fsdp2_model_cpu_offload.py
```
Result:
```text
FSDP2 npu CPU offload passed: 2 ranks, default and non-default streams
```
This run verified initialization-time offloading, nested FSDP2 modules
with even and uneven shards, repeated runtime offloading with queued
computation, and exact parameter values on CPU and after restoring to
NPU (`rtol=0`, `atol=0`).

Pre-commit checks also passed for this revision.

### Performance Considerations

This change prioritizes parameter correctness over asynchronous D2H
overlap.

Blocking D2H can increase host-side waiting and may change whether the
resulting CPU storage is pinned. Consequently, keeping
`non_blocking=True` in the CPU-to-device helper does not guarantee the
same H2D overlap or throughput as before.

The performance impact of this broader verl change has not been
quantified. The successful downstream training runs are correctness
evidence, not a controlled performance comparison.

### API and Usage

No public API or configuration changes are required.

Existing callers of the two affected helpers automatically receive the
corrected D2H behavior.

feat(perception): omni 视觉输入新增图片序列模式

原有 omni 视觉输入只有一条通路：单条 mp4（H.264+AAC）经 video_url 送入。本次在它
之外加上「按拍摄时间排序的 JPEG 序列 + 独立 m4a 音频」，由配置
perception.engine.input.omni_visual_input_mode 选择 video / image，默认 video。目标是
能在同一套感知管线下对照两种模态的识别效果。video 模式的请求字节与 prompt 逐字符不变
（golden 钉住）；唯一例外是内存行为：为让 video/image 共用同一份 canonical 帧，视频路
改为物化整窗缩放帧，不再沿用 #574 的 lazy resize（量级见 _prepare_omni_visual_frames

- **折叠的窄类型收下授权状态**：降级徽标在折叠两档展开时才都画得出来，并补渲染用例。
- **解冲突手痕回正**：不含逻辑改动。
- **被拒的场景台账补回链路两列**：降级态下也挂得回触发它的事件。
- **两处取值钉住**：台账里授权状态那一列取值的正反两面，以及状态接口下发的授权字段——漏铺一个键、或键名改了，后端不报错、不打日志、也不 500，只有界面上的失效徽标与体检结论悄悄消失。

merge: 并入 origin/main，台账两套新列并存、授权状态那列抬到 v6

**并入原因**：主干同期给动作台账加了新列，与本分支新加的授权状态列落在同一张表上，需要在新库建表与老库迁移两条路径上并存。

**本合并提交的树，前端类型检查是红的**：降级徽标的读取代码保留在动作行组件里，但折叠那一层的窄类型尚未收下授权状态列，折叠两档展开时取不到它。由下一个提交补齐契约并配渲染用例，此后才都渲染得到徽标。后端侧不受影响。

fix(miot): 查询与读取面按凭据收口，不再拿无效凭据空打云端

**问题**：设备、场景、相机、账号身份这几个读取入口在本地缓存为空时会顺手拉一次云端，而它们自己不碰客户端，正落在那处枚举判据的盲点里。

**解决方案**：
- **凭据不可用时不再发这一趟**：返回的东西与刷新失败时相同，不新增第三种状态；已有缓存照常返回，正常态下也照旧自刷新。
- **未绑定时那条「令牌还有效吗」不再真发请求**：手上没有访问令牌就直接返回假。降级态下仍要问云端这一档另有反向用例夹住。
- **碰云端改按引用判**：判据随方法体里引用到的成员走，不随它是否在这里被调用走。
- **路由形参的清洗补回**：拼装函数落到真正导入清洗函数的模块。

fix(miot): 剥换行的覆盖面扩到规则与服务层并收口，同账号重绑不再赔上接入配置

**解决方案**：
- **覆盖面扩到全部路由与服务层**：护栏的范围与判据都由证据推导，唯一实现收成一份，最后一份私有副本并入公共实现。
- **口径对齐**：回车与换行的处理与注释一致，兜底出口与留痕口径一并补齐。
- **同账号重绑保留接入配置**：先比对账号再决定是否清理，同一账号保留全部接入范围配置，换了账号才清。
- **拒绝文案分出「没绑定」一档**：与「授权失效」分开说；同账号重绑的收尾失败不再清配置。

feat(miot): 授权被云端永久拒绝后停止工作，被拒的原因透传到住户

**问题**：失效之后设备控制照常下发、感知照常运行，而下发只会撞 401，感知也会因拿不到相机列表而停止——只是晚一些，且毫无预告。

**解决方案**：
- **永久失效与瞬时故障分流**：云端明确拒绝归入永久失效、立刻停手；超时与连接失败按递增间隔在本轮内重试。
- **走云端的下发一律拒绝**：闸门放在代理层，不靠命名约定——哪些方法算下发面由测试遍历语法树枚举判定，新增而未归类即报错。
- **中断的刷新留痕**：发请求前记下意向，只存令牌指纹不存原文；重启后先验一次再定论，结论未定时不预先判死。
- **失效原因原样传到界面**：控制、推送、场景各条入口此前都把异常包成笼统的失败，会把住户引向反复改文案或去翻设备列表。
- **出错日志不带凭据原文**：进日志的外部可控值一律剥换行，护栏按语法树判而非按行匹配。

fix(miot): 新令牌先落库再走副作用、续期串行化，重新授权与解绑这条路径一并收口

**问题**：刷新令牌与授权码都是一次性的。云端换票成功之后，本地落库排在一串副作用之后——更新 HTTP 头、把新令牌推给原生相机库、重连云端长连接，其中一步跨 FFI 进原生库，段错误会直接带走进程。落库前中断即永久丢失。而两条续期并发时，后到的那条拿着已被消费的令牌去请求，一次正常续期被自伤成永久失效。

**解决方案**：
- **落库紧跟换取**：换到新凭据后立即落库，副作用全部排在其后。续期与首次授权两条路径同款处置。
- **续期与授权共用一把锁**：两条入口串行；临界区到「换票与落库」为止，全量拉取与等待留在锁外。
- **重新授权与解绑收口**：失效档不再被绑定状态门控——访问令牌也过期后绑定状态会翻假，门控在它上面会让问题最严重的那一刻反而不显示。
- **状态条在后端整体不可达时保留上一份**：重拉失败不合成一份「未绑定」的假状态，并边沿触发地给一次提示。

fix(miot): 凭据「存在」与「可用」分开表达，失效在界面、体检与台账上都看得见

**问题**：授权被云端作废之后，绑定状态仍然是真——手上的访问令牌还没到期。而判据只有一个「绑没绑」，于是面板显示一切正常，设备控制与感知正在撞 401。

**解决方案**：
- **新增「凭据可用」判据**：与「凭据存在」分开表达。续期已被永久拒绝、而访问令牌尚未到期时，后者仍为真，前者为假。
- **界面持续可见**：状态条与侧栏账号菜单各呈现一处，红点加原因文字，点击直接唤起既有的重新绑定弹窗。失效档独立于绑定状态且优先级最高。
- **命令行体检**：新增账号失效检查，判不通过、退出码为 1，附失效起始时间。该判定排在「未绑定」之前。
- **被拒的动作留痕**：动作台账记下写入当时的授权状态，事后分得清「设备真的没响应」与「当时授权已失效、根本没发」。
- **重复失败的告警限频**：失效是长期状态，而心跳类的失败日志会持续刷屏，把同期真正需要看的行淹掉。

Include the exception type in query name-lookup warnings without logging private details. Cover the real perception and query paths, fallbacks and logging boundaries, and align the documentation.

fix(cli): service stop 未就绪时直接拆解，压回调用方的 5s 预算

上一条把插件的 start 后台化之后，reload 的失败点从 start 挪到了 stop：openclaw 给
plugin service 的 stop 也是 5 秒，且 stop 超时是硬失败（会连带同一批的其它插件一起
超时 → config reload failed）。而 miloco-cli service stop 在「要拆的是一台刚被
abort 的 restart 拉起、还在初始化中」的后端时很慢：macOS 5.3s、Linux 容器 40.4s
（不收尸的 init 下 supervisord 成僵尸，_is_running 用 os.kill(pid, 0) 把它判成活着，
于是白等满 grace）。

改法：
- 等待预算按「后端是否已就绪（探一次 /health）」分档。未就绪整段共享一个有界总预算
  _STOP_BUDGET_S、到点 SIGKILL；不是各阶段各拿一份 grace —— 那样叠加最坏能到 ~7s，
  越过调用方的硬失败线。
- 未就绪 + 端口还没监听 = 已经证明它还没进 serve 阶段（uvicorn 先跑完 lifespan 再
  bind），没有可收的尾 ⇒ 直接 SIGKILL，不等它。
- _is_running 补僵尸判定（Linux 读 /proc/<pid>/stat 的 state；其它平台按老口径）。
- 升级收尾按进程名全扫（命令行含 -m miloco.main），不能只杀 launchd job 主进程：它的
  python 子进程不会跟着死，会成孤儿继续初始化、最后去 bind 端口。
- 升级收尾里「端口反查 / fallback 来的 PID」也要过 _is_miloco_backend_proc：它们可能
  是用户其它服务占用了 miloco 的端口，而这条路径直通 SIGKILL —— 不能破本文件既有的
  「只杀可证明属于 miloco 的进程」。
- 控制通道失联（sock/conf 缺失但守护进程还活着）时，shutdown 那步会被整个跳过：此时
  必须先 reap 守护进程再杀后端，否则 autorestart 会把刚杀的子进程立刻重生，成为没人
  认领的孤儿。
- 未就绪时 supervisorctl shutdown 的 RPC 超时也吃共享预算（它自带 8s 上限，不并进来
  上界就从 4s 变成 9s）；就绪路径仍是 8s。
- 谓词收敛到一处：按名全扫改用与单 PID 验证同一个词边界正则（substring 会命中
  `-m miloco.main_v2`，而这个谓词的输出直通 SIGKILL），ps 扫描抽成共用的 _scan_ps。
- 未就绪预算的锚点取在函数入口：探活(≤1s)/查 PID/扫残留/bootout 这些 prologue 也折进去 ——
  锚在它们之后等于让这段开销骑在预算之上，该档端到端最坏 ≈5s，正好贴住调用方的硬失败线。
- shutdown RPC 的 timeout 留 0.5s 下限：预算被前面的解释器冷启动吃光时 timeout≈0 会让
  supervisorctl 刚 spawn 就被杀、请求没写进 socket，"断 autorestart"随之落空。这 0.5s 是
  本路径唯一允许超出共享预算的部分。
- Linux 端口兜底补归属验证：未就绪档它的 grace 已被压成≈0（事实 SIGKILL），端口被用户
  其它服务占用时绝不能被收掉；就绪档保持原样（main 上就绪档的同类未验证点留 follow-up）。
- _launchd_reload 里同样的等卸载循环收编到共用的 _wait_launchd_unload，去掉两份手抄。
- _backend_ready 不传 verify：本地 backend 是 http（main.py 起 uvicorn 不带任何 ssl
  参数），verify=False 对 http 毫无作用，还会挂一条 CodeQL
  request-without-cert-validation —— 排查时别去改别处那两处同名写法，动了它们反而会把
  老告警变成"本次改动引入"。
- 就绪路径的预算与 30s grace 保持不变 —— 那里的 30s 是刻意的（后端关停序列里单是
  perception stop_engine 一步就有 10s 预算），压短会丢半截清理和最后一段 trace。

实测（2026-10-14，cat@mac + 同一台机器上的 Linux 容器）：掐断在飞 restart 后立刻
stop，macOS 5.28s→0.17s、容器 40.4s→0.46s；就绪态不变（macOS ~0.5s，后端日志里
是完整优雅关停链）；真 openclaw 热重载（含「enable 后 5 秒内再 disable」撞在飞
start 的序列）全部 applied、零 stop 超时。上界：探活 ≤1s + 总预算 3s。

test: 修复 zsh 转发后的组件安装测试

将服务和控制地址替身写入测试安装目录，确保 zsh 转发后的 Bash 子进程也能重新加载。固定测试服务管理方式为 nohup，避免宿主机已有的 systemd 服务掩盖替身失效。

fix: 非 Bash 解释器统一转发命令到 Bash

Zsh cannot evaluate the Bash-only constructs used by the service layers
(read -r -a, ${!arr[@]}, ${s:i:1}, $BASHPID, $BASH_SOURCE). Under zsh,
service_is_active reported false while the kernel was still running, so
_detect_ext_addr treated its own external-controller port as a foreign
conflict and reassigned a random port on every clashctl ui run, leaving the
printed address out of sync with the live kernel and forcing users to change
the URL repeatedly.

Add scripts/lib/shell.sh with one bash -c forwarder, route every
non-shell-mutating subcommand through it from the dispatcher, and keep
on/off/update/help/version in the current shell. Fold the duplicated
per-command ZSH_VERSION guards into the shared helper and extend
tests/zsh-commands.sh to assert the forwarding contract.
